Continental Magic Association The is an organization established by Serie that acts as the ruling body for mages across the continent. Overview. The Continental Magic Association was established by the Great Mage Serie over fifty years prior to the present day, and it oversees the regulation and hierarchy of mages as well as their deployment on various missions. The association is also responsible for administering the mage class exams and doling out class certifications for mages based on the results of these exams. Mages can be certified from ninth to first-class, with any mages below fifth-class being considered apprentice mages. Some first-class mages receive the opportunity to become Serie's apprentices, and besides being sent out on missions, they may also be asked to proctor mage exams. The Continental Magic Association may be affiliated with the education of mages through establishments such as the Academy of Magic. There are two branches to the Continental Magic Association. The headquarters of the association are in the Holy City of Strahl, and another branch is located in the Magical Town of Äußerst, the largest city of magic in the Northern Lands. Continental Magic Association Northern Branch. The of the Continental Magic Association is located in Äußerst. Serie regularly spends time here, and many first-class mages that take missions in the Northern Plateau are based out of the Northern Branch of the Continental Magic Association. Serie's room in the Northern Branch of the Continental Magic Association is a large room with high ceilings and contains a throne surrounded by books.
Continued Northern Travels Arc The Continued Northern Travels Arc is the fifth story arc in "."

Decke Region A snowy region with rough terrain. It has occasional snowstorms which can be quite deadly without any shelter. Decke Region. A snowy region in the Northern Lands with rough terrain. It has occasional snow storms that are dangerous without shelter. Cabin. A small one room cabin in the Decke Region at the foot of the mountains. It is used by adventurers as a shelter in the event of a snowstorm. It is visited by Frieren in her travels during the fifty years between the two Era Meteors she watches with the Hero Party, and by Frieren's Party and Kraft when they are stranded for half a year by the winter weather. The Forest. A forest in the Decke Region. There are foxes and creatures that look similar to seed rats that live within the forest. History. Frieren travels through the Decke Region in the fifty years between the Era Meteors that she watches with the Hero Party. She stays in the small cabin at the foot of the Schwer Mountains. Synopsis. Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel's death, Frieren's Party have travelled to the Decke Region. Stark has collapsed and there is a heavy snowstorm so they seek shelter in a cabin Frieren remembers was there eighty years ago. Luckily, it is still intact and even looks like it is regularly maintained. As they open the door, they see an elf doing squats inside, and quickly close the door. Fern protests staying in the cabin and asks Frieren to find another place, but before they can, the elf opens the door and asks Frieren if she is an elf. Inside the cabin, the elf, who is named Kraft, has a conversation with Frieren about the rarity of encountering another elf. Stark's temperature is very low so Kraft helps warm him up by sleeping with him. Stark wakes up very confused. After the confusion is settled, he compliments Kraft for his nice body. Because of the weather, the four of them must stay in the cabin for awhile since going through the mountains in the current conditions would be suicidal. The four of them gather supplies from Kraft's wagon, hunt, and forage for food and supplies during the stay. They share their meals together and Kraft shows Fern and Stark various things. One day, while in the forest, Kraft and Frieren have a discussion on the Goddess, spurred by Kraft asking Frieren to give a necklace to Fern for her strong devotion. Months later, once the winter has passed and the mountain is traversable again, Frieren's Party and Kraft part ways as they continue their separate adventures.

Demon Demons are a species of monsters known for their human-like appearance and their natural affinity to magic. They are the main antagonists of "". Introduction. Articulate monsters, who have been at war with every other race in the world. Demons are naturally proficient in magic. They devote the majority of their lives to one magic that they specialize in and master it. Like other monsters, they are individualistic creatures and do not have any concept of familial relationships. However, demons do maintain a basic level of interaction with one another in order to fight against mankind. Their societal hierarchies are based on strength, which can be assessed at a glance through reading a demon's mana. Because mana to demons is what status and assets are to humans, demons cannot imagine constantly limiting their mana, as it is akin to their very dignity. They in turn expect their enemies to not hide theirs, either. They are a long-lived race and view the passage of time similarly to elves. Origin and History. Demons are the descendants of an unnamed species of monsters who had the ability to shout for help as a way to attract unsuspecting victims. Over time that species would evolve, developing a more humanoid appearance as well as the ability to mimic human behavior more accurately as a way to better trick their prey, until they eventually became the monsters known as demons. Eventually an incredibly powerful demon, simply known as the Demon King, would emerge and unite the entire species under his rule. Under his leadership, the demons alongside the Seven Sages of Destruction would wage war against the other sapient races for thousands of years, reducing mankind's sphere of influence to only a third of what once was. The elves were also targeted by the Demon King's army, with many of their villages being destroyed (including Frieren's village, with her being the only survivor). Although it is unclear how successful the demons' genocidal campaign against the elves was, it can be assumed that it is one of the reasons as to why there are so few elves in the modern era. The Demon King would eventually meet his end at the hands of Himmel and his party. With his death, the demons would scatter, serving under the remaining high-ranking members of the Demon King's army, such as the Sage of Destruction Aura. While there are still many powerful demons around the world, none of them seem to have what is necessary to organize an army large enough to threaten the world on the same scale as the Demon King. Biology. Like all other monsters, demons turn into particles of mana and disappear when they die. They are a long-lived race and view the passage of time similarly to elves. Appearance. Demons are monsters that have evolved to look like humans to lure them, and as a consequence, most of them look as close to humans as possible with the exception of their horns. All demons have two horns on their head, but these horns can come in a variety of shape and sizes. Some demons possess a more monstrous appearance, such as the Elder Sage of Corruption Qual, who was tens of meters tall and had jagged teeth, and the demon general Revolte who had four arms and a lower half similar to that of a serpent. Diet. Despite being omnivores, many demons eat humans for sustenance, just like their unnamed ancestors. While not all demons engage in such behavior, it is common enough to be regarded as common knowledge by humans. Behavior and Culture. Personality. Demons are defined as articulate monsters by the Great Mage Flamme. They are incompatible with other races. Demons are by their very nature liars and will talk to humans to manipulate them into dropping their guard and sparing them, though they only know how to use words without knowing its meaning. Aura, for example, feigned a peace mission to destroy Graf Granat's Domain, and a young demon girl would cry for "mother" whenever cornered in an attempt to gather pity from humans that would kill her otherwise. While demons have been shown to feel emotions, they do not feel the same emotions as humans do, and as a result, are incompatible with human ideas of morality. Demons look down on humans and only view them as prey. Demons mock human empathy and think they are weak, which is why they constantly underestimate mankind. They are deeply proud of their mana levels, and due to the power-based hierarchies they form, they will not and cannot conceal their mana for long periods of time. Even temporarily concealing it to avoid detection—something which any demon can do according to Lügner—is considered to be inappropriate in a battle between mages. Social Hierarchy. For demons, strength determines one's position in their social hierarchy, which can be assessed at a glance through reading a demon's mana. Because mana to demons is what status and assets are to humans, demons cannot imagine constantly limiting their mana, as it is akin to their very dignity. They in turn expect their enemies to not hide theirs, either. Personal Relations. Like all monsters, demons are anti-social creatures by nature, preferring to be alone and avoiding contact with other members of their species beyond the necessary. They only form groups so that they can fight against mankind, refusing to form any deep bonds with each other. It seems unusual for demons to show a deep sense of loyalty to another or to show a desire to avenge a fallen comrade, some demons go so far as to show indifference towards the idea of ​​their entire species being in danger. Due to their individualistic nature, the concept of family is foreign to them, and they will often abandon their children once they are born. They also seem to lack the notion of romantic relationships, as no demon couples have ever been seen.

Demon King The Demon King was the leader of the Demon King Army and the primary objective of the Hero Party's ten year quest. He waged war against the human kingdoms of the continent from his castle in Ende for thousands of years before being slain by Frieren and her comrades. Despite his importance in the world, relatively little is known about him so far. Though Demon are solitary creatures without human emotion, he commanded the loyalty of all demons. Personality. Not much is known about the Demon King's personality, however, while most demons value individuality, the Demon King notably fostered order among demons and was able to maintain loyalty among demonkind. Like Macht, the Demon King desired coexistence amongst humans and demons. He resorted to mass killing humans in an attempt to better understand their way of thinking, ultimately reducing mankind's sphere of influence by a third. Appearance. Not much is known about the Demon King's appearance. He seemed to wear full plate armor. Like all demons, he had two horns on his head. Synopsis. History. One thousand years before the era of the Hero Himmel the Demon King ordered his subordinates, including a general of his army and at least several extremely powerful demon mages, to massacre the elven population. Frieren's village was destroyed and its population killed, leaving her as the sole survivor of her village. Ironically, this led to Frieren meeting Flamme, who would go on to train Frieren and give her mission of killing the Demon King, which she succeeded at many centuries later. Approximately twenty years before the Hero Party defeated him, the Demon King Army's offensive intensified, leading to a large increase in the number of mages in the overall human population. It was common to pass by mages walking through the streets of any regular town. However, by about twenty-nine years after Himmel's passing, mages had become a rare sight, only spotted in specific magical towns such as Äußerst. Following his defeat, nearly all his direct higher ranking subordinates disappeared without a trace. However, the remnants of the Demon King Army were still a significant threat to the human kingdoms, and almost a century after his defeat, they still constitute of large enough forces to wage wars against human armies and hold the northern part of the continent. Notable demons of high status from the Demon King army to appear after the Demon King's defeat include Elder Sage of Corruption Qual and two members of the Seven Sages of Destruction, Aura, and Macht. Abilities. Not much is known about the Demon King's abilities. However, given demon societal hierarchies are based on strength, and all demons appeared to answer to the Demon King, it can be assumed that the Demon King was exceptionally powerful. In addition, when discussing the Hero Party's journey, Eisen mentioned that a lot happened in the Demon King's castle, indicating a difficult fight. The Demon King was, according to Solitär, an "eccentric" demon similar to herself and Macht, as the Demon King was both intelligent and possessed a breadth of scientific knowledge. As implied by Frieren, and much like Macht and Solitär, due to the Demon King’s desire to understand humans and “coexist”, he had extensively studied and researched humanity and the differences between humans and demons. Part of his studies involved researching other biological life and he came up with the theory of "convergent evolution" to explain the difference between mammals and aquatic life forms, a theory he then shared with Solitär. The Demon King is noted by Serie to possess immense mana sensitivity and detection, where unlike a majority of his fellow demons, including his most powerful subordinates, the Demon King was able to instantly tell that Frieren had been actively concealing her mana output the second he laid eyes on her. Additionally, he was able to sense disruptions to the space-time of the world and correctly identifies Frieren as the individual that has traveled from the future through the Monument of the Goddess.

Demon King's Castle The is the establishment of the deceased Demon King, located at the northernmost tip of the continent, Ende. Overview. The castle is said to be an insanely cold place. According to Eisen, much has happened there. Frieren found a Shadow Dragon's horn in the castle, which she left in Himmel's possession.

Denken is an Imperial Mage and a first-class mage. Born in the Weise Region, he lost both of his parents by demon attacks and was raised by Glück, the feudal lord of Weise. When he was young, he was the apprentice of Macht, who was serving as the personal mage of Glück's family. Because of his wife's frail condition, Denken became a mage in the Imperial army and tried to gain power and influence in hopes of saving her life, but unfortunately she passed away before he could. After the death of his wife and the formation of the Golden Land, Denken had delayed returning to his hometown until it was swallowed up by the Golden Land. Since only first-class mages are allowed to enter the Golden Land, Denken took the First-Class Mage Exam at the same time as Frieren and Fern. He is the oldest examinee that passed that year's exam. Personality. As an Imperial Mage, Denken is renowned to be a cunning and ruthless politician who reigned supreme in a struggle of power at the Imperial Capital. However, in truth he is quite personable and makes connections with others even to their reluctance, such as going out of his way to approach Richter outside of the First-Class Mage Exam. He is also a rare mage who values coordination and cooperation rather than acting on his own, and was willing to go out of his way to secure allies. Unlike most mages, he does not put too much emphasis in reaching greater heights of power by all means. He believes that the value of magic lies in the pursuit of the magic itself, an opinion which Frieren is in agreement with. Denken is also a competent leader. He is a careful and contemplative person who keeps his calm and analyzes the situation. In the first stage of the exam, he is the first to figure out Frieren's strategy and coordinated his team's conduct to moderate success. He also manages to form a team for the second stage of the exam, where he expresses dismay at the lack of cooperative spirit among other examinees. During their preparation to fight Macht, Denken is ready to wait for at least three years for Frieren to finish analyzing Macht's Diagoldze, exemplifying both his patience and his persistence. Lernen, who is his long time friend, describes Denken as a talented and passionate man who stood up for him until the end when he was expelled from his position in the Imperial Army. Although his current conduct may not indicate it, Serie remarks that Denken still retains his passion and vigor in their interview and is impressed enough to let him pass the third stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. He shows he is willing to go to great lengths to get what he wants, namely when he is ready to engage in a fistfight in order to steal a Stille and pass the first stage of the exam. He is also willing to aim for feats which exceed his abilities, such as challenging Frieren in the first stage of the exam, contemplating how to fight Serie, and attempting to defeat Macht, the most powerful Sage of Destruction and whom was also his master. For most of his life, Denken is weighed down by the death of his wife and is fearful of remembering the happy times he has spent with her. It is why he has delayed returning to visit his hometown for so long that it has become a restricted area due to the Golden Land's expansion. However, the happy memories he has in his hometown with her becomes the impetus for his quest to defeat Macht and save his hometown. Denken has a soft spot for young adults like Laufen, Fern, and Stark since he never had children nor grandchildren of his own. He treats and spoils them before parting ways after the exam. Appearance. Denken is an elderly man who has brown hair and a long, thick beard. He wears a monocle on his left eye. He is commonly seen wearing a long, black robe with white collars. Abilities. Denken is a powerful mage who achieved the rank of first-class mage, a title only under fifty people have ever been able to achieve.

Denken/Relationships Relationships. Lektüre. Denken and Lektüre were childhood friends and distant relatives. They would play together a lot, and eventually got married as they grew up. Due to Lektüre's frail body, Denken didn't try to have children with her to avoid any further strain on her health. He loved his wife and stayed by her side every day until she finally passed away. He still misses her and recalls her fondly, and his desire to honor her memory drives many of his actions, such as taking the First-Class Mage Exam so he can visit her grave, and restoring the Golden Land once he realizes the place in his memories with Lektüre hadn't changed at all. Glück. Glück was Denken's guardian after he lost his parents. He housed the young Denken and had him learn magic under Macht. Later when Denken married Glück's daughter Lektüre their relationship stayed healthy and they mourned Lektüre together when she passed. Macht. Denken hated Macht for being a Demon, but ironically Macht was also his mentor who taught him magic. Macht told Denken that he would make him strong enough to defeat any demon and and that he may be capable of killing him one day. The time they spent together became beneficial for Denken as he knows his master very well, which enabled him hold his own despite being old when he fought Macht in the Golden Land. After a long struggle, Denken finally succeeds in defeating Macht by piercing through his heart, as Macht was distracted after seeing the Fortified City of Weise return back to normal. He eventually finishes him off in front of Glück. Laufen. Denken and Laufen were paired up in the first stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. He cared about her safety and scolded her for being reckless during the exam. Denken seems to cherish Laufen greatly as he never had any children or grandchildren. He treats her as a surrogate grandchild and spoils her. After the exam, he will often buy her treats such as donuts and treat her to meals. Richter. Denken and Richter were paired up in the first stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. Denken dislikes Richter's willingness to kill for his goal and disagrees with Richter's reasoning for taking the exam. While Richter is taking the exam for the utilitarian purpose of attaining Serie's privilege, Denken does not care as much about the privilege, as he believes that the greatest joy is found in the pursuit of magic itself. When Richter threatens to kill Kanne and Lawine, Denken admonishes him and tells him to just babysit them, as killing is unnecessary to pass the exam. Despite Richter's impertinence and Denken's higher ranking, he does not respond to Richter's instigations, as he recognizes in Richter traits that he himself possessed when he was young. After the second stage of the First-Class Mage Exam, Denken visits Richter in his shop and leaves Richter with the parting advice that in three years time, Richter will be far stronger. Lernen. Denken and Lernen are old friends who have known each other for over fifty years. They came from different backgrounds but they got along and are still friends to this day. When Lernen lost his position as an Imperial Mage, Denken argued strongly against this decision, but Lernen told him to let it go. Frieren. Like many mages, Denken admires Frieren and quickly took the opportunity of challenging her in the First-Class Mage Exam. However, he would rather have her as an ally than to seek a fight with her. After being promoted to first-class mage, he thanks Frieren for her help during the exam and tells her that he will be able to visit his wife's grave. Frieren helps him return the Fortified City of Weise back to normal following the defeat of Macht, and Denken remains very grateful to her.

Denken/Synopsis Synopsis. First-Class Mage Exam. First Stage. Denken is one of the participants in the First-Class Mage Exam in Äußerst. There are a total of fifty-seven participants. Denken is assigned to the Thirteenth Party with Richter and Laufen for the first stage of the exam. Denken's team is one of the teams gathered around the lake in hopes of capturing a Stille. However, when Frieren's team freezes the lake with Lawine's magic, Denken recognizes that the mana-sensitive Stilles will now avoid the lake. He realizes that for the Second Party to take such a big action, they must have devised a means to secure a Stille. He decides to confront Frieren's team and and take their Stille instead of searching fruitlessly for their own. While traversing the forest and looking for the Second Party, their team notices casualties who were attacked by Geisel, the alluring corpse bird. Laufen comments that it seems the Continental Magic Association doesn't care if an examinee dies. Richter tells her that it's because the Continental Magic Association cares for the quality of their mages, and anyone were to die from threats in the exam, they aren't qualified to be a first-class mage in the first place. However, Denken says that the Continental Magic Association is behind-the-times. According to him, quality is not necessary as he recalls his past experiences and what he has witnessed as an Imperial Mage. Great power is fearsome and a fearsome authority does not last. For him, magic is nothing to be proud about. This outlook surprises Richter, as he had believed that Denken would share the same outlook as the Continental Magic Association. They continue searching for Frieren's party, but Denken begins to notice that every pond or pool that they've come across has faint traces of mana circulating in it. They are able to deduce the Second Party's plan, which is to wait by a source of water that hasn't been contaminated with mana and thus is more likely to attract Stilles. Denken makes the call that they will wait until the Second Party uses mana, as no mage can cast spells without releasing some mana. They patience pays off, and they eventually locate the Second Party when Frieren uses her spell to capture a bird. Laufen quickly takes their Stille with Jilwer and hides with it. Knowing Frieren will be able to track her, Denken and Richter confront Frieren's team. Denken recognizes Frieren as the mage of the Hero Party and expresses his desire to fight her. Three hours before sunset, the two teams face off with Denken taking on Frieren, and Richter fighting against Lawine and Kanne. Denken tells Richter to refrain from killing one of the two girls as they only need to obstruct them and they only need to keep them from retaking the Stille. Richter remarks that he thought Denken was a ruthless and cold person since he is an Imperial Mage and has gotten rid of political opponents many times. However, Denken does not see the value of being a first-class mage or needless death, and Frieren agrees on his sentiment that first-class mage is nothing but a title. Richter proceeds to give a brief history of the Continental Magic Association and the privilege of attaining first-class, which is being granted any magic that one desires by the Great Mage Serie herself. Richter continues to explain how magic is valuable to him, with Denken finding it absolutely ridiculous and Frieren barely reacting. Richter calls Denken and those who do not care for the privilege as exceptions to the rule. Denken emphasizes to Richter to not kill the two girls, telling him to just put them to sleep for three hours. Crushing Frieren is all that's necessary for Denken. Richter proceeds to split the ground with his Earth Control: Bargland, which separates him, Kanne, and Lawine and leaves Denken and Frieren below. Denken comments that the privilege would only be wasted on the young that can't help but be filled with excessive ardor. Frieren asks why he would think that, which he replies that she already knows the answer. They share the same view that the greatest enjoyment comes from the pursuit of magic itself. As they fight, Denken tries different spells consecutively, but Frieren easily blocks every attack, giving him a hard time. He is trying to end the battle early, knowing that he won't last much longer with his mana. He tries to attack Frieren with Lights of Judgement: Catastravia only for her to counter it and defeat him with mere basic offensive magic at pointblank. Frieren attempts to make Denken reveal Laufen's location but he refuses to speak. Knowing she is just hiding nearby, Frieren takes Denken as a hostage to lure Laufen out, but Denken tells Laufen not to come out no matter what. However, Laufen eventually gives in and attempts to save Denken but is caught by Frieren. Frieren uses magic restraints to bind the two of them to a tree, and Denken scolds Laufen afterwards. Laufen asks why he wants to become a first-class mage so badly despite having everything. He reveals that he only wanted to visit his hometown, particularly the cemetery. It is located in the Northern Plateau that can only be accessed by first-class mages due to the recent surge in demonic attacks there. Denken then tells Frieren that she should go save her teammates, but concludes that it may be too late because it is likely that Richter will kill the two girls before confronting Frieren. However, Frieren is not worried and remains certain that Lawine and Kanne will win. She reveals that she has just finished deciphering the barrier around the exam grounds, and as she breaks it, Denken realizes her true intention. With the barrier broken, the rain outside finally starts pouring in, giving Lawine and Kanne a complete advantage and allowing them to defeat Richter. Richter is washed off his own plateau and he apologizes to Denken for his loss, but Denken states that once Frieren broke the barrier, his loss was inevitable. With the three of them out of mana, it seems to be over for their party but Denken refuses to give up and has them search for traces of other parties. Eventually, they find a pair who has just lost their third member and has no way of passing anymore, though they are still holding on to their Stille. With all parties involved out of mana, Denken and Richter challenge the two to a brawl, while Laufen hides to find an opening to take their Stille. They manage to win, and having secured a Stille, pass the first stage of the exam. The first stage exam ends with six parties remaining and eighteen participants passing in total. The second stage will be held three days later and Genau dismisses all of them. During the intermission between the first and second stage, Denken, along with Laufen, decide to pay Richter a visit on his shop to invite him to eat with them at the restaurant Denken is looking for. Denken has taken Laufen under his wing and treats her like a granddaughter. Richter refuses to eat with the rest of his party at first but eventually agrees after Denken chastises him that as a mage, it would be good for Richter to get Denken on his good side. The restaurant he is looking for is one he went with his late wife with, and he states that the taste there was unforgettable. Richter brusquely tells Denken that he'll be paying, and Denken readily agrees. When they find the restaurant, Denken notes that mysteriously, the atmosphere is still the same even after half a century. Richter comments that Denken has good taste, as this restaurant offers the most delicious food in town, and he often comes there himself. When they go in, Frieren's Party also happen to be there, but Denken chooses to just leave them be because they seem to be having fun and food is meant to be enjoyed. Denken then enjoys a meal with Richter and Laufen. Denken spends the rest of the intermission between the first and second stage of the exam in Äußerst. Before the second stage of the exam starts, he receives the details for the second stage through a messenger bird and is seen reading the details in his inn room. Second Stage. The second stage is set on the Tomb of the Ruined King and the proctor is Sense. Due to the multiple entrances the tomb has, which all lead to the innermost depths, Denken suggests that everyone work together. However, Ton expresses that they have no reason to work together, and in fact risk becoming sacrificial pawns for other mages if they do work together. He is especially wary of Denken, who appears to be knowledgeable about dungeons, and enters alone. Other examinees also proceed to enter the dungeon, either in the same teams as the first exam or as pairs. The three from the 13th Party are left together with Methode and Länge. While Denken thinks that cooperation was the best option to conquer the dungeon and laments that the other mages did not recognize this, Richter repeats Denken's words from the first stage back to him: that not everyone can be sensible, and cooperating "was just not to their liking." Richter is confident the ones left aren't fools and will not hold the others back, and tells Denken to be content with that. The five of them then enter the dungeon together. Once inside, Denken immediately displays his knowledge. He recognizes a trapped hallway where the ceiling crashes down if you step into the center of the room and warns the rest of the team to avoid the center. In the next room, they have their first encounter with Gargoyles. By working together, they are able to defeat both Gargoyles. However, Länge is knocked back by one of the Gargoyle's attacks into a trapped room that seals itself off. Denken tries to break the wall using Catastravia, but the wall seems unbreakable. He tells Länge that there is no other way and to break her bottle to save herself. Deeper within the dungeon, clones of each participant began appearing, with Denken's group encountering and defeating Laufen's clone first. Denken concludes that working together was the right call. However, the worst is yet to come, as they go through a more elaborate doorway into a large, ornately decorated and high-ceilinged room. Frieren's clone, guarding a large double door, floats down to meet them. Richter asks Denken if they will be able to handle that as well; Denken replies that if it were not an exam, he would've broken his bottle already. The four of them are forced to retreat from Frieren's clone, and camp out outside the double doors to wait for more examinees to arrive. About half a day later, Frieren arrives with Fern and sees Denken's group gathered in front of the door. They are still strategizing on how to get past her clone. Frieren deduces that the clones' weaknesses would probably be the same as their original. Richter suggests the use of restraint or hypnosis magic if they are to take on a superior mage, though Frieren thinks her clone would be resistant to both. Believing that a small opening should be enough, Denken has Methode check the efficacy of both restraint and hypnosis magic on Frieren. However, their hopes are dashed as Frieren is correct that she is resistant to both. Methode postulates that Edel, a fellow examinee and a second-class mage who specializes in hypnosis magic, may be able to break through Frieren's resistances. However, Dünste soon shows up alone, with his fellow examinees Edel and Blei having broken their golem bottles and forfeited the exam. He informs the group that Edel's hypnosis magic was unable to reach Sense's clone, meaning the clones do not have minds of their own. Despite what they've learned, Denken thinks that there are still too many unknown variables, with the biggest issue being the identity of the summoner. Kanne and Lawine then arrive, and Lawine informs the group that the one summoning the clones is the Spiegel. She shares her intel from her brother, who had been part of a previous raid attempt of the dungeon, and points out the door behind Frieren's clone, which is the location of the Spiegel. If they defeat its frail body, then all the clones will disappear. Denken adds that the intel seems to coincide with the results of his mana detection. However, another problem aside from Frieren's clone blocking their way is the Sacrificial Treasury Door Lock Magic, a powerful seal on the door which means the door will not open unless the caster perishes. Tearing down the walls are not an option either, leaving them with no other way but to fight Frieren's clone in order to attack Spiegel. Lawine warns them that they should take it down quickly due to the fact that the clones have the habit of gathering at the deepest point of the dungeon with time, which led to the demise of the previous advance party except her older brother's unit. With everyone agreeing that the weakness of the clones are the same as their originals, Fern has Frieren stand next to a wall then suddenly attacks her with combat magic, which Frieren blocks. Denken and Methode are able to pick up on the fact that Frieren's mana detection is interrupted for a mere fraction when she casts a spell, a common error for apprentice mages that she is ashamed of. However, Frieren's other abilites are still too extraordinary, and so the group formulates a plan to get past Frieren's clone together. Denken asks if Frieren thinks they can win, and she replies that dungeons that cannot be conquered don't exist, a claim she backs up with her title as the mage that was part of the party that conquered the most dungeons in all of history. The group decide that Frieren and Fern will fight Frieren's clone while the remaining participants will hold off the other clones. After a brief strategy session where the mages share their own weakest matchups, they assign targets and split up. After defeating his own target, Denken senses the clone of Sense, but he arrives too late to come to the aid of Richter and Lawine. However, Denken thinks to himself that the result would've been the same even if he made it, as he can't see any ways to beat Sense's clone. While he is hiding, Übel and Land stumble upon him. Übel asks him how things are going and comments that he cannot win against Sense's clone. When Denken tells her that it is necessary to take down Sense's clone, Übel acknowledges that she is still an inexperienced third-class mage and is far weaker that Denken or Wirbel, but she believes that she can take on Sense at the very least with her magic. Just as she defeated the Sense clone, her clone along with Land's clone reappears, and all other clones that were defeated earlier reappear also. Denken proceeds to enter into a battle of attrition with Land and Übel until Frieren and Fern finally defeat the clone of Frieren and destroy Spiegel. With Spiegel defeated, all the clones disappear. Denken gathers along with the other remaining examinees in the depths of the dungeon, where Sense congratulates them for conquering the dungeon and passing the exam. Denken looks for Frieren only to see her trapped in a mimic, with Fern trying to get her out. Afterwards, Denken along with Laufen pay Richter another visit in his shop. Richter is in a bad mood due to his failure in the second stage of the exam and wants nothing to do with Denken. Denken tells him that he is here to shop this time, and that he was just unlucky during the exam. Anyone forced to fight Sense's clone would have been forced to forfeit like Richter did. However, Richter believes that he was just not strong enough. He then goads Denken, stating that at least he could retake the exam in three years, time that Denken very well might not have, but Denken does not rise to Richter's bait, and Richter asks why Denken has simply borne Richter's insults. While Denken thinks that Richter is not someone admirable, he bears no resentment towards him, admitting that he was once like him in his youth before becoming an Imperial Mage. Denken leaves Richter with parting words of encouragement that in three years time he will be much stronger, then leaves the shop with Laufen. Final Stage. Falsch announces to the examinees that Serie herself will be hosting the third stage through personal interview. Denken is the eighth to be interviewed after Fern. He expresses that he is honored when Serie recognizes him for his reputation as an Imperial Mage. Serie remarks that she wishes she had met him when he was younger and filled with energy and ambition, and not when he's nearing the end of his life as he is currently. However, Serie judges that her initial assessment was wrong, as when Denken walked in the room, he contemplated how to fight her. Denken replies that he only considered the idea for a moment and quickly gave up on it, but this is enough for Serie to pass him. She comments that despite his old age, his flame is still burning, as people usually wouldn't even think of fighting her. After the exam, Denken thanks Frieren and Fern for allowing him to reach this far, which enables him to finally visit his wife at the cemetery in his hometown. Denken hangs out with Laufen, Fern, and Stark while they are eating. He tells them not to mind him and he seems to be fond of the youngsters. Stark quickly apologizes for talking casually to him after finding out his status, though he doesn't mind as he simply came into town as a mage and not a noble. Stark feels embarrassed to be treated by someone with such status, but Denken doesn't really mind since he has no one else to spend his money on, which makes Stark and Fern wonder aloud if he has no children nor grandchildren. Denken tells a brief story of his life to them. His deceased wife had a frail body and he felt helpless, as it was those times that he needed power and wealth. As he grew older and earned his current status as an Imperial Mage, magic was nothing but a tool for conflict for him, but was reminded of how fun magic can be upon fighting Frieren, which is something he wishes Fern to tell Frieren. He also expresses his admiration for the elven mage of the Hero Party, who had originally inspired him to become a mage himself. However, Fern insists that he tell Frieren himself, as she is certain that it would make Frieren happy, and Denken replies that he will do so. As a reward for passing the First-Class Mage Exam, Denken is granted the magic that he desires by Serie herself at the privilege conferment ceremony.

Draht was a demon who served Aura the Guillotine. He infiltrated Graf Granat's Domain along with Lügner and Linie under the guise of serving as an envoy of peace from Aura. Personality. Draht is extremely confident in his magic, going as far as to challenge Frieren on his own. He is reckless and inexperienced, choosing to target Frieren immediately instead of contributing to Lügner's deception. His sensory abilities are not as strong as Linie nor Lügner's, as he was unable to perceive the threat Frieren posed. Appearance. Draht is a young demon with dull green hair, purple eyes, and horns that are short and curve outwards. He wears a white button down shirt and dress pants with black tuxedo suspenders. His shirt has ruffles down the center and a collar tied with a striped bow at his throat. His shirt's sleeves are loose and taper off into a long cuff. Synopsis. In Graf Granat's Domain, Linie and Draht, operating as peace envoys under Lügner, are sent to Graf Granat's heavily fortified city that is protected by a magical barrier cast by the Great Mage Flamme, keeping demons and monsters out of town. The barrier has made the city impenetrable in its ongoing conflict with a Sage of Destruction, Aura the Guillotine. The demons' mission is to negotiate or coerce Graf Granat into lowering the defensive barrier. However, Graf Granat reveals that he has no intentions of holding negotiations with the demons and he and his guards raise their swords against Lügner. In response, Draht readies himself for a fight, but Lügner intervenes, defusing the situation by falsely claiming his nonexistent father's death in response to the Graf grieving his own son. Later, when Graf Granat leaves to think over Lügner's words, Draht goes to kill Frieren, who has been locked up after attempting to attack the demons when she first entered the town. He kills a guard with his magical wire and enters Frieren's cell, telling her that he is there to kill her. Although Frieren warns Draht that she is stronger than Aura, he responds that he does not believe her and summons a wire around Frieren's neck with the intent to decapitate her. However, Frieren coats her neck in mana, which prevents her own decapitation. Despite this, Draht still acts self-assured of his victory and declares that he can cut through both her mana and neck. Frieren calls him out for his naivety before swiftly cutting his arm off with a blast of concentrated mana casted without her staff. Draht tries to attack her with his other arm, but Frieren cuts it off as well. In his last moments, he attempts to beg for his life, but Frieren blasts his neck with mana and kills him mid-sentence. Later, Linie notes to Lügner that she can no longer detect Draht. The Graf confronts them after finding the guard outside Frieren's cell dead and expresses that Frieren knew not to commit such a crime. He points out that Draht is missing and prepares to confront the demons. Lügner belittles Draht for acting on his own and ruining their mission, and he subsequently attacks the Graf and his guards with his magic.

Dwarf Dwarves are a hardy species of humanoids that are known to work with humans. Biology. Appearance. Dwarves are generally humanoid in appearence and are distinguished by their short stature compared to other species.

Dünste is a mage who participates in the First-Class Mage Exam. In the first stage of the exam, he is placed in the seventeenth party alongside Edel and Blei. Personality. Not much is known about Dünste's personality. He is a quiet individual, choosing rarely to speak and often deferring to others, such as when he listened to Edel's orders to use fire on the frozen lake during the first stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. When he and Blei are running from Sense's Speigel clone, a wounded Blei stays back to hold it off and tells Dünste to flee. Despite his normally deferential attitude, Dünste briefly interjects and hesitates for a moment before running off to find others. Appearance. Dünste is a tall, thin mage with a recessed hairline and long hair that extends past his shoulders. He also sports a neatly groomed mustache. Dünste wears long, black robes with two accented jacket panels and a light colored hood. He wears a white turtleneck shirt beneath the robes. Synopsis. First-Class Mage Exam (First Stage). Dünste is one of the participants in the First-Class Mage Exam held in Äußerst. In the first stage of the exam, he is placed in the seventeenth party alongside Edel and Blei. The party had the idea to wait by a lake for a Stille to appear. When Lawine freezes the lake Dünste and the rest of the party await before Edel has Him and Blei try to melt the lake. It is unknown what happens after this but towards the end a now fallen over Dünste has the Stille sitting on him as Edel and Blei sneak up on it to catch it. Later he is shown walking around Äußerst with Edel and Blei reading the notice about the second exam. First-Class Mage Exam (Second Stage). Dünste is among the participants to listen to Sense explain the second stage of the exam, After some time Dünste, Edel and Blei all head inside. They get pretty far before being cornered by Sense's Spiegal clone, He listens to Edel explain magic and why he and Blei would have trouble fighting in a dungeon before stating that modern magic that they learned is not fit for dungeon combat after Blei ask Edel if she could use her magic on it Dünste ask how long they might need to hold it off. Soon after Sense's Spiegal clone attacks causing them to fall to her level. After Edel attacks by throwing rocks at the clone as Dünste and Blei also chuck rocks at it. At Edel's command him and Blei use Defensive Magic to try to hold off the clone's attacks. As Edel explains it tries to overpower it and slip through it the defensive magic breaks as they jump back. After Edel gets wounded Dünste cast offensive magic to protect Edel before she uses her golem to escape after Edel tells them to find fighters to help them. As they run they are chased by the Spiegal clone, Blei gets wounded. Dünste tries to stay back for a moment to help before Blei tells him to run. Dünste hesitates for a moment before running Dünste later comes across the main group wounded falling to the ground Methode quickly comes to his aid, She ask him where Edel might be to which Dünste explains they were attacked and Edel is out now. He also explains that Blei is gone as well. He then ask if they can work together as Denken comment that's what he wanted from the beginning. He is healed by Methode's Healing Magic as he joins the group to converse to which he affirms the rest that the Spiegal clone's don't have minds so hypnosis magic would not work on them. He then listens as Lawine and Kanne come in as they explain more about the clones. As the others work a plan Fern brings up that the clone's probably have the same vulnerability's as the person they copied. To which Dünste agrees with. Fern then shows what Frieren's weakness much to everyone's shock. After this they all work to find a way to beat the clone. As Frieren and Fern enter to fight the clone, Denken ask everyone which person they'd be most concerned about fighting to which he explains they need to stop the clone's from getting here to help protect the Spiegal. As they each go to fight the clones, Dünste attacks the Richter clone with offensive magic which he dodges. As the clone uses Bargland to disrupt the ground to which Dünste blocks. Before Kanne tries to sneak attack it as that fails, both Dünste and Kanne attack at once as the Richter clone blocks it. Once again Richter clone uses Bargland causing the ground to be disrupted. But right when things we're getting bad the clone disappears showing that Frieren and Fern were victorious. He then joins the crowd of people who pass the Second Stage of the exam. He and the others are then congratulated and told they pass. First-Class Mage Exam (Third Stage). Dünste is later seen amongst the rest of the examinees listening to Falsch explain the contents of the third stage. He is the second examinee to speak to Serie. Serie fails him right away, presumably for being scared of how much mana she has or being unable to visualize becoming a first-class mage. It is unknown what Dünste does after the First-Class Mage Exam concludes. Abilities. Not much is known about Dünste's abilities, though in order to participate in the First-Class Mage Exam, his rank is at least fifth-class. According to Edel, his magic cannot be used within the Ruins of the King's Tomb. It is likely that he uses a modern magic that manipulates matter that isn't found subterraneously or within man-made structures.

Edel is a second-class mage participating in the First-Class Mage Exam. She is placed in the Seventeenth Party, alongside Blei and Dünste, during the first stage of the exam. She specializes in Hypnosis Magic. Personality. Edel is a remarkably level-headed mage while under pressure, as shown by her calm behavior while she is up against Sense in the First-Class Mage Exam and Macht on the expedition to the Golden Land. Despite Macht's renown, she succeeded in reading Macht's memories. Lernen calls her a braver mage than he is. Otherwise, Edel appears slightly apathetic, stating her unwillingness to work after Lernen approaches her with a personal request. She is also highly domineering, constantly yelling at Blei and Dünste during the first stage of the exam. Appearance. Edel has the physique of a petite teenage girl and short, hair with curtain bangs. Her hair is strawberry blonde while her eyes are hazel. Throughout the First-Class Mage Exam, Edel wears a white button-up dress with short puff sleeves and long, black boots. During her investigation of Weise with Lernen, she dons a cape-like coat and long pants. Synopsis. First-Class Mage Exam (First Stage). Edel is a second-class mage that is placed in the seventeenth party during the first stage of the First-Class Mage Exam, alongside Blei and Dünste. Not much is known about the activities of the seventeenth party during the first stage, however, after being paired with Blei and Dünste, Edel appears to take on the leadership role in their party. They decide to wait around the lake for Stilles to gather. However, once the second party freezes the lake, she does not have the acumen to realize that Stilles will no longer approach the lake and orders her teammates to use fire magic to melt the ice instead. She and her teammates are able to secure a Stille in the final few hours of the exam once a Stille lands on Dünste's back while he is hunched over. First-Class Mage Exam (Second Stage). At the beginning of the second stage exam held at the Ruins of the King's Tomb, Edel enters almost immediately with her first stage partners Blei and Dünste, rather than partnering up with the other mages. While the examinees are planning how to defeat Frieren's clone created by Spiegel, the water-mirror demon, Edel is brought up as a possible counter to Frieren's clone. Methode suggests that Edel may be able to bypass the clone's mental defenses, if it has a mind. While Edel and her first stage teammates are inside the dungeon, they encounter Sense's clone created by the Spiegel. Knowing they will not be able to hide for long, Blei asks Edel if her hypnosis magic would be able to work on the clone. Edel orders Blei and Dünste to use full sphere defensive magic in order to give her time to make eye contact and speak to the clone to try and create an opening. However, this fails, leaving her vulnerable to a series injury from Sense's clone, and Edel concludes that the clone doesn't have a mind. Heavily wounded, Edel resigns and uses her golem bottle to escape, failing the exam. After the second stage of the exam concludes, Edel is seen outside the dungeon with the other examinees who failed. As one of Lernen's golems heal Richter, she marvels at the golem's ability to use healing magic capably. The Golden Land Arc. Edel is recruited by Lernen to assist him on the expedition to scout out the Golden Land for information. Lernen tasks her with restoring the functionality of the Stone Bracelet of Servitude, which he believes is defective. Upon arriving, Edel reads the memory of a former citizen of the Fortified City of Weise, who witnessed the ceremony where Macht was equipped with the Stone Bracelet of Servitude. She notes that the command given was not precise enough for a demon to be adequately bound by. Edel also recognizes that the belief that the feudal lord Glück commanded Macht in order to gain wealth is logically unsound, since Macht's gold cannot be refined, which is one of the major properties of gold that gives it value. Before reaching the barrier of the Golden Land, they encounter second-class mage Früh, who was part of the advance party sent to scout the Golden Land. She tells them that the advance party was wiped out in a flash. Lernen asks why Früh was the only one allowed to escape; as he speaks, she begins to turn to gold. He tells Edel to read her memories to no avail, as she turns into gold before either of them can move. After crossing the barrier into the Golden Land, Edel and Lernen are discovered by Macht almost immediately, and a battle between Macht and Lernen ensues. Edel works on restoring the Stone Bracelet of Servitude, but realizes that no defect exists. Edel also confirms that no additional command can be placed on the bracelet except by the one who gave the original command. While Macht is attacking Lernen, Edel sneaks up behind Macht and touches him, reading a hundred years' worth of memories at the cost of most of her strength. The two then manage to escape from Macht, with Edel visibly worn out on the carriage ride back to Äußerst. On the carriage ride back, Edel asks Lernen why he is going so far to help Denken. Lernen tells Edel about his and Denken's shared history, and how now that they are old and the end can come at anytime, he wishes to assist Denken in seeing the colors of his hometown again. Seeing Edel's expression, Lernen asks her whether she thinks Denken made up his mind too late. Edel answers truthfully that Denken was way too late in making his decision, and Lernen agrees with her, but also says that he understands. As humans their time is limited, and there is no such thing as "someday" in their lives. Relationships. Lernen. Edel was personally handpicked by Lernen to restore the functionality of the Stone Bracelet of Servitude. The two are familiar with each other, with Edel having been called upon for jobs by the Continental Magic Association before, presumably for her exceptional mental magic. Lernen thinks very highly of Edel's abilities and her bravery, going as far as to praise her courage in front of Macht himself and calling her a much braver mage than himself. Edel is fairly restrained and respectful around Lernen. After hearing Denken's story from him, she initially refrains from sharing her thoughts, but Lernen is able to read that Edel thinks Denken made his decision much too late, which prompts her to speak her thoughts openly. Abilities. Edel specializes in hypnosis magic, which comprises her family's business. She can manipulate the actions of those she has within her sight by giving verbal commands. In addition, she can read the memories of the person with whom she makes physical contact. On the other hand, her combat ability is practically nonexistent. Edel is capable of quick thinking during battle, as shown when she swiftly analyzes the exact mechanics of Sense's magic when confronting her Spiegel clone and begins devising a strategy to defeat it. She is able to quickly coordinate her teammates to counter the clone, resulting in them successfully putting up a defense against it. Unlike most mages, Edel does not use a staff when casting spells, instead relying on her mental magic or other means of casting.

Ehre is a second-class mage that participates in the First-Class Mage Exam. In the first exam, she is placed in the eighth party alongside Wirbel and Scharf. Fern feels that she is the strongest within both the fourth and eighth parties. Personality. Ehre maintains a cool and collected façade. She remains relatively emotionless and speaks in an even cadence. In fights, she is analytical of her opponents and calmly attacks and dodges. However, once she is met with an attack she isn't expecting, her façade quickly cracks. She is easily overwhelmed by surprises that she doesn't readily know how to handle. When low on mana, Ehre shows a much more petulant and childish side, getting angry when Wirbel attempts to float her and demanding a piggy-back ride from him. Despite her outward appearance, she is friendly towards her party, hanging out with them even outside of the exam. She readily extends offers of kindness, such as when she offered to introduce her grandfather to Wirbel when he complains about having to take the sea-route back north if he fails the First-Class Mage Exam. Appearance. Ehre has wavy, shoulder-length brown hair and dark brown eyes. She wears a long white tunic belted at the waist, a long, dark green skirt, and black boots. Her tunic is long sleeved, covers the neck, and has simple green lining on the sleeves. It is pleated down the middle in the front. Atop the tunic and skirt, Ehre wears a purple cape clasped with a green jewel at the front. When she was younger, Ehre's hair fell to middle back. She wore a pink shirt and a white skirt tied at the back with a bow. When fighting, Ehre uses a metallic staff. Her staff is long, with a single large ring suspended at the top, and thin discs around the handle of the staff at the base and top. Synopsis. History. When Ehre was younger, her village in the north was attacked by demons. Wirbel was one of the humans who defeated the demons attacking her village. First-Class Mage Exam (First Stage). Ehre is one of the participants of the First-Class Mage Exam in Äußerst. During the first stage of the exam, she is placed in the eighth party with Wirbel and Scharf. Their party has no luck finding a Stille, so they decide to ambush a party that has already captured a Stille and steal it. After Wirbel's surprise attack against the fourth party is blocked, she rushes in along with the rest of her party and faces off against Fern. After Land calls for the fourth party to scatter, Ehre faces Fern alone. During their battle, she stays above Fern with flight magic and uses Doragate to try to break Fern's defensive spells. While fighting Fern, Ehre begins to feel uneasy, as Fern fights like a seasoned mage and reminds her of fighting against her grandfather. She asks if Fern is trying to not show her hand by only using basic offensive and defensive spells, and she tells Fern that she wouldn't last long in a fight against Wirbel. However, Fern believes Ehre to be the strongest mage of both their parties. Ehre hesitates before replying that Wirbel, who is the captain of the Northern Magic Corps, has much more experience in fighting. His magic is vulgar and cowardly, but it is extremely effective, and Ehre believes that the girl fighting Wirbel is likely to be killed. However, this taunt doesn't affect Fern, who immediately strikes at Ehre with a saturation attack. Ehre is unable to withstand the barrage of Zoltraak spells, which force her to use an omnidirectional defensive barrier. As Fern's attack continues, Ehre becomes visibly rattles as she is forced to draw her defensive barriers closer to herself. She comments that she cannot handle so many spells, before a large explosion of mana is seen from afar. Fern interrupts Wirbel's battle with Übel and tells Wirbel that she has killed Ehre; hearing this, Wirbel decides to spare Übel, as their party has already been disqualified. When Wirbel goes to retrieve Ehre's body, he finds that Fern hasn't killed Ehre at all, and instead has merely knocked her out. Annoyed at the lie, he tells Ehre to wake up, and he calls Ehre lame for running out of mana since she was the top student at the Academy of Magic. Ehre explains that she was overwhelmed by the sheer force of ordinary offensive spells, though she expects Wirbel to not believe her. However, seeing the path of destruction that Fern's attack has left, Wirbel responds that he does. He tells Ehre that he doesn't understand why she fought Fern head on like an idiot, as it was a battle she could've won. Wirbel tells her that they were to regroup with Scharf, but Ehre tells him that she cannot walk. Wirbel smiles, calling her a pain, before he floats her with a spell; Ehre then exclaims at him to not treat her like an object and demands a piggy-back ride. This elicits genuine annoyance from Wirbel, but he acquiesces nonetheless and carries her on his back while they find Scharf. When they discover that Scharf, too, has run out of mana and cannot walk on his own, Wirbel bemoans that their failure in the exam is absolute. Ehre hears a sound and wonders what it is; Wirbel replies that it's probably raining outside the barrier, which is fitting for his mental state. He lays out the facts of their situation: it is two or three hours before sunset, and they have two party members that can no longer fight, making the odds of them being able to steal a Stille low. Ehre points out that despite this, Wirbel has chosen to help her and Scharf, to which Wirbel retorts that he could ditch them. Ehre continues, asking whether kindness was the reason why Wirbel fought demons and reminds him that when she was younger, he had saved her village from a demonic attack. Wirbel calls this notion ridiculous, as he believes people don't risk their lives out of kindness. For him, the motivation to fight demons came from a girl in his hometown he had a crush on, who fled his hometown to the because of the increase in demonic activity in the north. Wanting to look cool, he promised his crush he would kill all the demons in the north so she could return. However, as this happened when he was four or five years old, he no longer even remembers her face or her name. Hearing this, Ehre smiles and calls him a fool. Wirbel then bemoans that he must go home by boat again, as he gets horrible seasickness. Ehre offers to introduce him to her grandfather, a first-class mage, who could take him by land. She cuts herself off as, in that moment, she spots a Stille. Wirbel catches it with Sorganeil, and he wonders what the point of all their effort was. Before the first exam ends, the eighth party are seen still walking around with Ehre on Wirbel's back and Scharf getting levitated. They are one of the six parties to pass the first stage of the exam. It is unknown what Ehre does during the time between the first and second stage of the exam in Äußerst. She is seen meditating alone in a forest when the messenger birds deliver news of Sense's second exam. First-Class Mage Exam (Second Stage). During the second stage of the First-Class Mage Exam, Ehre enters the Ruins of the King's Tomb with Wirbel and Scharf. They walk along a twisting series of pillars when Ehre is restrained by Sorganeil. She warns the rest of the party that they are being ambushed by three mages that have concealed their mana. Wirbel throws up a shield and blocks an attack meant for the party. He explains to them how Sorganeil works— the user must have their foe in full vision—and tells Scharf to block them from sight using his flower petals. From behind the barrier, they watch as the Spiegel clone versions of their party approach them. Wirbel assigns roles to the team, and he tells Ehre to take care of the clone Wirbel. After defeating the clones, they are found by Methode, who conveys to them the plan that the examinees gathered at the depths of the dungeon have decided upon. Methode asks for their assistance in defeating Denken, who she expects to be one of the more troublesome clones. Methode explains that she will fight the clone of Fern on her own. Ehre warns Methode that Fern is strong, and asks if she will be okay alone, but Methode assures her she will be fine. Ehre fights Denken alongside Scharf and Wirbel for the rest of the exam. After the Spiegel's defeat by Frieren and Fern, she is shown sitting on the floor complaining that she can't move. Wirbel gives her a piggy-back ride to the treasury room in the depths of the dungeon, where Sense announces that all the gathered participants have passed the second stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. First-Class Mage Exam (Final Stage). Ehre gathers with the rest of the examinees that passed the second stage of the exam in front of the doors of the Northern Continental Magic Association in Äußerst. Falsch informs them that the exam will be an interview with Serie. Ehre is the fifth mage that Serie interviews. She is summarily failed for not possessing what Serie determines to be the qualities of a first-class mage. After the third stage, she is shown standing outside the doors of the Continental Magic Association while Wirbel comforts Scharf. After the privilege conferment ceremony, Ehre and Scharf convince Wirbel to go back to the north with them. They watch from the side while Wirbel talks to Frieren about the Hero Himmel. The day after the privilege conferment ceremony, Ehre introduces Wirbel and Scharf to her grandfather, Lernen. The three then leave Äußerst together. Continued Northern Travels. Shortly after the First-Class Mage Exam, Wirbel, Ehre, and Scharf rest at an inn at the fork in the road in the Great Sanft Forest. The road forks off to the Northern Plateau and the Neutral Harbor. They have drinks and a meal in the inn when Frieren's Party walks in, and Wirbel goes to greet them. He explains that because demonic activity in the north has suddenly increased, they will be traveling by sea again, and he will be with Ehre and Scharf until they reach the port town in the Imperial Capital. Ehre joins their conversation and adds that Wirbel has been whining about not wanting to get seasickness. Wirbel then asks Frieren to let him convince Stark to join him in the Northern Frontier. Ehre spends the rest of the time with Wirbel, Scharf, and Stark. According to Frieren, they look to be having a good time. The next day, they bid Frieren's Party goodbye, and Ehre departs towards the Neutral Harbor with Wirbel and Scharf. Relationships. Wirbel. Wirbel and Ehre have a friendly relationship. They both possess knowledge about each other's feats and appear to respect each other as mages. Ehre describes Wirbel's magic as having no character and is under no qualms about his attitude about killing. Wirbel, meanwhile, has higher expectations of Ehre due to her position as a top graduate from the Academy of Magic. Though she loses against Fern, Wirbel still thinks highly of her abilities, and he tells her that it was a match that she could have won had she not fought Fern head on. Ehre shows a much more childish side around Wirbel, and although Wirbel expresses his annoyance at her requests, he acquiesces to them anyways. Wirbel fought against the demons attacking her village and saved the village when she was a child. On Ehre's part, she expresses curiosity at his motivation for fighting demons like the ones that invaded her village, and though she calls his reason foolish, her remark is good-natured and Wirbel doesn't take offense. Upon hearing about his seasickness, Ehre offers to introduce Wirbel to her grandfather, a first-class mage, should they fail the exam. During the second stage of the exam, Ehre enters the Ruins of the King's Tomb with Wirbel and Scharf. After the First-Class Mage Exam, Scharf and Ehre convince Wirbel to travel to the harbor with them, showing that they have become fairly familiar with one another. Lernen. Lernen is Ehre's first-class mage grandfather that she mentioned during the first stage of the exam. She introduces him to Wirbel and Scharf after the First-Class Mage Exam. Presumably, they have a good relationship, as Lernen is willing to take time out of his duties in Äußerst to meet Ehre, and Ehre is confident that she can introduce Wirbel to Lernen should he need a way to travel by land through the Northern Plateau. Abilities. Ehre is a second-class mage and, according to Fern, is the most powerful amongst the fourth and eighth parties. She graduated top of her class from the Academy of Magic.

Eiseberg , the, is a city located in Imperial Territory. It is the seat of governance and administrative center of the Empire. Many nobles and prestigious families of the Empire live in the Imperial Capital. The National Foundation Festival is held in Eiseberg, and was originally meant to be a social season for aristocracy. Eiseberg is the base of operations of the Magic Special Forces, the Shadow Warriors, and the Court of the Sacred Staff.

Eisen is a Dwarf and the former Warrior of the Hero Party that defeated the Demon King, consisting of himself alongside Frieren, Himmel and Heiter. As a Dwarf, he has a much longer lifespan than most humans, but a shorter one than Elves. Personality. Eisen is a witty and troublesome person, and failing to show respect to the king prior to their adventure almost had him and Himmel executed. Eisen is also known to be rather careless and tough, jumping down from extreme heights without a scratch. He initially did not believe in religion, and thought of the deaths of his family in a matter-of-fact manner, shown by having them in a mass grave with a simple stone. However, after listening to Heiter say that he wants to believe they are in Heaven because it would be more comforting to the deceased, Eisen adopted the practice of praying at their graves. He has maintained this practice even in his old age. Appearance. As a male Dwarf, Eisen is of short stature and has a strong build. His brown hair and beard are of similar length and reach past his chest, and most of his face is obstructed by his beard and a horned helmet with a nose guard. Eisen wears a red cape with armor on his shoulders and a brown tunic underneath. Additionally, he wields a large, double-headed axe in battle. In old age, Eisen has a notably thinner build, losing the majority of the muscle mass in his arms.

Eisen/Relationships Relationships. Stark. Eisen adopted Stark when he found Stark after he fled from his hometown. Eisen loved Stark like his own son and took Stark on as his apprentice. He taught Stark all he knows about combat, including his techniques and lessons about perseverance and bravery. Eisen cooked Stark a massive Hamburg steak on his birthday every year, showing he thought of Stark as a warrior who worked hard. However, because of his awkwardness, he never conveyed the meaning of the Hamburg steaks to Stark. Eisen would also entertain Stark with his stories of his adventures. Their relationship became strained when Eisen reflexively attacked Stark during an argument as he feared Stark's strength. However, Eisen deeply regrets this, and asks Frieren to recruit Stark for her journey to Aureole. Himmel. Eisen fought alongside Himmel to defeat the Demon King. Eisen respected Himmel as he was brave and kind. Heiter. Heiter and Eisen were comrades who fought together. Eisen, like Frieren, thought of him as a Corrupt Priest. The two had a good friendship, and after the Hero Party parted ways, the two still frequently wrote to each other. Frieren. As two members of long-lived races, Frieren and Eisen share a closer understanding of time than their other companions in the Hero Party. When Eisen asks Frieren why she will not take on apprentices, he is unable to completely refute her answer that taking on apprentices is meaningless as she will outlive all of them. He is also nonchalant about the long periods of time that Frieren will go without contact. In the Hero Party, the two of them are the more hot-headed ones and will often attempt to fight their way through a problem if they see the goal in sight. Eisen cares greatly for Frieren. Upon seeing her regret at not getting to know Himmel better, he and Heiter work in tandem to find the location of the notes of the Great Mage Flamme. He convinces Frieren to take his apprentice Stark as her vanguard and also convinced her to head to Aureole and meet Himmel.

Elf Elves are a rare humanoid species who have a vast natural lifespan. However, their inability to present their emotions is slowly driving them to their extinction. Origin and History. Around a millennium prior to the story, the Demon King ordered the massacre of elves during his reign with casualties including Frieren's village. Biology. Appearance. Elves are generally humanoid in appearance and almost indistinguishable from humans with the exception of their pointed ears. Due to their long lifespans, their bodies age much slower compared to other species. Behavior and Culture. Personality. Elves tend to have a warped sense of time due to the length of their lives to the point where months passing can seem like just a day to them in the grand scale of things. Frieren has noted that elves tend to lack romantic feelings and reproductive instincts. She has also noted that some tend to do silly or foolish things to stave off boredom due to their lifespans, such as Milliarde.
Empire The is a country in the that once united the majority of the continent. Its capital is Eiseberg.

Ende is a cold region located at the northernmost tip of the continent. It holds the current Demon King's Castle and is also the alleged location of Aureole, a place regarded as heaven or the afterlife where souls rest. Overview. Demon King's Castle. The Hero Party traveled to Ende in order to confront the Demon King in his castle. The journey to reach the castle is described as a long journey where many things happened. Aureole. According to the Great Mage Flamme, Aureole, also known as The Land Where Souls Rest or Heaven, is said to be located in Ende. When Flamme visits Aureole, she is able to speak with the souls of her departed friends. Reaching Aureole is the goal of Frieren's current party.

Eng Road (Locality) The Eng Road is a passageway in the Northern Lands. It is a passageway that is commonly used for merchants traveling in the Northern Lands. It leads to a fairly developed town, which has a festival in honor of the Hero Party liberating it. Eng Road. A passageway in the Northern Lands commonly used as a route for merchants in the Northern Lands. It leads to a fairly developed town. The Town. A fairly developed town in the Northern Lands. It is connected to the Eng Road, which is used by merchants wanting to trade in the town. It is well protected, with walls surrounding the town. Events. Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel’s passing, Frieren, Fern, and Stark are in the Eng Road. They travel with a merchant after clearing a road that has been blocked due to a landslide. When they reach the town, they find out the Liberation Festival is taking place that same night, which commemorates the day the Hero Party subjugated the demon that was oppressing the region. The townspeople celebrate by decorating the statues of the Hero Party. The merchant tells Frieren that it is on this day everyone remembers Himmel and his party, making her recall a memory of when Himmel told her he makes statues of himself and the party so that Frieren would not be alone in the future. They reach the town and see the statues decorated with flowers. The next day, the trio continues their voyage towards Heaven.

Episode 1 is the first episode of the "" anime series. It is the first part of the initial two-hour premier episode, released on September 29, 2023. Synopsis. The world celebrates the Demon King's defeat at the hands of the Hero and his companions. Now that their great adventure is over, what will Frieren the mage do next? Plot. The Hero Party, consisting of mage Frieren and her companions hero Himmel, priest Heiter, and warrior Eisen, return to the Royal Capital after triumphantly defeating the Demon King. On their way, Himmel suggests that despite their achievements, they still need to seek employment upon their arrival and continue forward with their lives. He tells Frieren that the life ahead of her will be much longer than theirs, which she nonchalantly agrees with. The heroes reach the city amidst a large celebration in their honor and receive recognition from the King. That night, they enjoy a festival held by the townsfolk, during which Himmel informs the others that the King intends to erect statues of them in the plaza. The Hero Party reminisce on their journey and the humorous moments that had occurred throughout it, finding it hard to believe that it has come to an end after ten years. Himmel expresses his gratitude towards his companions for the time he spent and the memories he made on the journey with them. Frieren points out that they spent a mere ten years together, surprising Himmel. They all look up into the sky to witness the Era Meteors, an event that occurs only once every fifty years, and Himmel decides to label it as the start of an era of peace. Frieren proposes that she brings the party to a better location for viewing the meteors the next time they occur, and Himmel laughs and accepts the offer. The next day, Himmel and the others accompany Frieren to a bridge to bid her farewell. She informs them that she plans on traveling through the for the next century and collect spells, though she may visit them every now and then. As she departs, Himmel wonders about the life she will lead, and Heiter refers to how time passes differently for her. Frieren immerses in various experiences and activities during her solo journey for the next fifty years. She visits a shop in an attempt to obtain a shadow dragon's horn, but the shopkeeper informs her that the shop does not have one. Frieren remembers that the Hero Party found a horn during their exploration of the Demon King's castle and she had left it with Himmel for safekeeping. With the next occurrence of the Era Meteors approaching, Frieren decides to head back to the Royal Capital and retrieve it from him upon their reunion. Upon returning to the city, Frieren is shocked by how much it has changed. When Himmel reunites with her, she is equally surprised by how much he has aged. Himmel reminds Frieren that fifty years have passed, though he remarks that she still looks the same. He presents the shadow dragon's horn to Frieren, stating that he had always intended to return it to her someday. She and Himmel then prepare for the upcoming Era Meteors at Himmel's home. The two reunite with Heiter, who is now a bishop in the Holy City, and Eisen, and Frieren notices that while Heiter has also aged considerably, Eisen's appearance remains relatively unchanged due to his longer dwarven lifespan. Frieren informs them that it will take a week to reach the location with a better view of the Era Meteors, which disappoints Himmel. As they adventure to the location, Himmel reflects on their memories and how much he had missed traveling with his comrades. The reunited party arrives at a giant lake underneath a clear sky, and as they once again watch the Era Meteors, Himmel expresses gratitude to Frieren for providing him with a wonderful final adventure. Shortly after, Himmel passes away, and the remaining members of the Hero Party attend his funeral. During the procession, Heiter mentions to Frieren and Eisen that Himmel was happy.
