Heiter/Relationships Relationships. Frieren. Frieren light-heartedly calls him "Corrupt Priest" due to his affinity for liquor. They were good friends and companions in the Hero Party. Twenty years after Himmel's death, he asks Frieren to help him translate a book that might have the secret to let him live forever or be resurrected, as he just wants to have a little more time on earth. However, this is later revealed to be a ploy to keep her around and have her train Fern until Fern could protect herself when he was gone, and subsequently, have Frieren take her under her wing when he is gone. Frieren notes that it seemed like he was not afraid to die, but he admits that was a mask he wore beneath his smiling appearance to show off. As seen in his final years where she lived with him, the two really do deeply care about each other. Fern. In his last remaining years, he adopted the orphan Fern and raised her. When Frieren came to visit him twenty years after Himmel's death, he asked Frieren to adopt Fern and train her as her apprentice. Heiter was a good father figure to Fern. She became strong so he would not have to worry about her anymore and could pass away in peace, and to this day she still misses him. In his final days, he wished for Fern to be strong enough so that he could pass in peace without regret.

Heiter/Synopsis Synopsis. History. Early Life. Heiter grew up in a village in the . His parents passed away when he was young and he was placed in an orphanage along with Himmel and other children in the village. From a young age, Heiter was very pious and skilled at the Goddess's Magic. Though he was a kid with an annoying attitude, he also liked taking care of others and often acted as the peacemaker for the kids in the orphanage. He and Himmel were best friends from early on, but Heiter didn't believe that Himmel would be capable of defeating the Demon King and said that he could only be a fake hero because he had a fake sword. Nonetheless, Himmel convinced him to travel with him to defeat the Demon King when they were older. Journey in the Central Lands. The two set off when Himmel was sixteen on their journey to defeat the Demon King. They first recruited Eisen as their vanguard and then Frieren as their mage. While recruiting Frieren, Heiter judged her to be a so-so mage, as she had roughly one-fifth of his mana. The four of them then set off to the Royal Capital, where Heiter and Frieren had to talk the King out of executing Himmel and Eisen for their rudeness. The King sent them on their way with ten coppers. Outside of the Royal Capital, when Frieren pointed out that Himmel had the Hero's Sword, he revealed to her that Heiter's words and lack of belief in him in their childhood led him to want to be a real hero. The newly formed Hero Party would go on to face various demons, monsters, and dungeons together. Early in their adventure, they faced the Elder Sage of Corruption, Qual, in the Größe Forest. The party was unable to defeat Qual and held him off long enough for Frieren to seal away instead. They ushered in a new year in Warm, where Heiter, Eisen, and Himmel saw the first sunrise of the New Year together as part of the New Year's Festival. Heiter was bedridden the rest of the day because he drank too much, though Himmel initially claimed the cause was Heiter's sadness that Frieren missed the sunrise. Throughout their journey, Frieren would also demonstrate her collection of spells to the party. When she showed them the spell to create a field of flowers, Heiter and Eisen looked on in awe. They then chased each other amongst the flower field before making flower crowns for each other. Heiter also reacted with excitement whenever Frieren found a spell to create shaved ice in a dungeon. He remarked excitedly that the ice the spell creates is fluffy, but was disappointed when Frieren didn't have the spell to create syrup. The Hero Party also attempted to conquer dungeons, but early on would fall for the simplest traps. After an experience where Frieren and Eisen fell behind while the party ran from a large boulder, they quickly established a pattern where Himmel would pick up Frieren and Heiter would pick up Eisen any time the party needed to flee from an encounter. During their adventure, the Hero Party became the group that cleared the most dungeons in history. They would frequently strategize together in order to figure out the best way to conquer a dungeon, and these strategy sessions often had to account for Heiter being too hungover to fight, such as when they fought an amphibious, crystalline monster in a dungeon together. Before heading to the, the party stopped at Eisen's house. Heiter prayed for Eisen's family, leading Eisen to correct Heiter and state that people returned to nothingness when they died. However, Heiter insisted that the deceased go to heaven, leading to a discussion amongst the party. Heiter stated that he didn't care whether or not heaven actually existed, only that he thought it "should" exist. He explained that he believed that it was more convenient to think that those who had struggled so hard to live would then be indulging in luxuries in heaven after their death instead of returning to oblivion. The entire party then prayed for Eisen's deceased family. In their time traveling together, the Hero Party grew to know each other's idiosyncrasies well. Out of everyone in the party, Heiter would grow the most visibly frustrated with Frieren whenever she overslept or exhibited lazy traits, going as far as clicking his tongue at her before being talked down by Himmel and Eisen. He shared with Frieren that his favorite food was alcohol, though she already knew this fact from their travels together, and listened as Eisen explained why he cooked Hamburg steaks for the party on their birthdays. Heiter was frequently shocked by Eisen's inhuman feats of durability, such as when he was able to fall headfirst from any height without taking damage. He was also often shown to be exasperated with Himmel's narcissism, often bemoaning the amount of retakes Himmel requested. However, he too would become the subject of several statues during the party's travels across the continent. For Heiter in particular, the party grew used to accounting for his inebriation or consequential hangovers. Journey in the Northern Lands. Some time after, the party stopped in Waal at the Northern Checkpoint, where they proceeded to travel into the Northern Lands with much fanfare from the citizens of Waal. They saved the region around the Eng Road from a monster and had a statue of the party made. The party then stopped in a village that was attacked by a young demon girl. After Himmel agreed with the chief's decision to spare the demon, Heiter would periodically watch over the demon girl during their stay in the village. When the demon ended up killing the chief, he watched as Frieren and Himmel confronted and ultimately killed the demon. They then proceeded further north and faced off against Aura the Guillotine and her undead army and forced Aura to retreat. The head of the Granat family at the time, Graf Granat's grandfather, was grateful for their assistance and expressed his indebtedness to the party. When Himmel was unable to pull out the Hero's Sword, Heiter seemed concerned for his friend. The party continued their travels north. They arrived in the Raad Region, where Heiter commented excitedly about the bars in the town. After, the traveled and met Old Man Voll, and spent time with him before proceeding onward to the Offen Mountain Range. When Frieren fell ill in the mountains, Heiter and Eisen collected the necessary ingredients for her medicine. The party then proceeded to Äußerst. Frieren tried to show her Holy Emblem to the party, but both Himmel and Heiter were unable to recognize it. While in Äußerst, they fulfilled a subjugation request by the renowned chef Lecker of the restaurant Bell. After retrieving Lecker's heirloom knife from the demon that stole it, they were treated to a meal by Lecker. The party would continue to help various humans in their travels, such as saving a young girl from monsters, helping farmers carry boxes, and even traveling—and drinking together in Heiter's case—with others for weeks. From Äußerst, the party's journey continued. They continued to encounter strong monsters, often fleeing if necessary. At some point, they also conquered the Thousand Mirror Tower. In Graf Dach's Domain, they were tasked to retrieve the Dach family's heirloom sword from the demon that had stolen it. They were given no leads for where the demon had gone and eventually tracked it down to the top of the Schwer Mountains and were rewarded with gold for their trouble. They then trekked to the secret hot spring of the Etwas Mountains only to find that it was no more than a footbath. Journey in the Northern Plateau and Beyond. In the Bier Region, they encountered the dwarven alcohol connoisseur Fass, who is seeking out Boshaft. Heiter and Fass immediately bonded over their shared love of alcohol. However, to Heiter's chagrin, they did not have time to assist Fass in his quest to seek out Boshaft. He is dragged away by the rest of the party and they continued their journey. The Hero Party would then stop at Norm Company Territory. Lord Norm supported the party financially and wrote them a promissory note with an unspecified date of repayment. They escaped from a thunder of dragons in the Drachen Region with Heiter carrying Eisen away, stopped at the monastery in Lake Korridor while traversing across the lake, and met Gehen in the Great Tor Canyon. After, the party traveled to the Schmal Snowfield in order to earn money for their travelling expenses and witnessed a large vein of holy snow crystals. Some time after, the party confronted another Sage of Destruction, Böse the Immortal. Böse trapped the party in his indestructible barrier. Heiter noted that he would be able to keep the party alive without food, water, and even oxygen for up to two months using the Goddess's Magic, prompting Frieren to wonder if the party was comprised entirely of monsters. After breaking out of the barrier, he and the rest of the party defeated Böse together. At some point in their years traveling together, Heiter figured out that Frieren was suppressing her mana. In a village where he donates money to restore the village orphanage, Heiter and Frieren spoke briefly about faith and Frieren's lack of belief in the Goddess. Heiter asked her if there was anyone to praise her. Frieren responded that she hadn't done anything praiseworthy, and Heiter questioned if that were really the case even though she had been suppressing her mana her whole life. When Frieren asked why he was interested in the story, he mentioned that his child may one day become a mage. While traveling through the Wissen Mountains, the party saw a Sky-Mountain Dragon from afar. Seven years after setting out on their journey, they reached Kino Pass, where Frieren attempted to decipher one of the monuments of the Goddess. This created a space-time interference that substituted Frieren from eighty years in the future with the Frieren of the past. After they managed to send future-Frieren back to her present time, Heiter along with the rest of the Hero Party swore to keep Frieren's time travel a secret from her. They decided that they would spend the next twenty to thirty years deciphering the spell to return from the Time-Traveling Bird chapter of the scriptures. They then continued their journey into Imperial Territory. Eventually, after ten years journeying together, the Hero Party reached the Demon King's Castle in Ende and defeated the Demon King. They then returned to the Royal Capital while stopping along the way to complete various quests. On the way back to the capital, they note that exaggerated stories are already being spread of their feats. Post Defeat of the Demon King. After defeating the Demon King and leaving the Royal Capital, Heiter settled down at some point in the Holy City of Strahl. He would eventually rise to the rank of bishop. As part of his official duties, Heiter would travel around to various villages in the Central and Northern Lands in order to conduct inspections. During one such inspection, he conferred the holy symbol to Sein's Brother in the Alt Woods and asked his brother to come work in the Holy City. However, Sein's Brother rejected him as he didn't wish to take his younger brother Sein's hometown away from him. Heiter then shared stories of the Hero Party's adventures with a young Sein and Gorilla in order to kindle their adventurous spirits. He told them anecdotes about the other members of the Hero Party, such as the fact that he was unable to read Frieren but he chose to trust in her words instead. He also took them around the area and showed them different sights, such as the statues of the forgotten heroes Monk Kraft and his companion. Heiter is revealed to be the one that gave Sein his alias of "Priest Goatee" after pointing out Sein's visual similarity to one of the statues. In the fifty years between Era Meteors, Heiter presumably also worked to decipher the spell to return in the Time-Travelling Bird chapter of the scriptures, which was determined to be the spell Vialathor. After Himmel's funeral, Heiter continued working as a bishop in the Holy City. During this time, he and Eisen continued to exchange letters and figured out the location of Flamme's real notes, which were in the Voll Basin. After retiring from his duties as a bishop, Heiter initially intended on spending the rest of his days quietly. However, upon reflecting on Himmel's earlier death, he didn't want for the lessons he had learned from Himmel about altruism and kindness to be lost. This would later in part be what inspired him to save an orphaned Fern's life. Heiter traveled at some point to the war-torn Southern Lands. He encountered a young Fern who had recently lost her parents and was contemplating suicide and convinced her to live on. Heiter then took in Fern. The two of them lived in a small cabin in the woods in the outskirts of Strahl. Heiter, seeing Fern's aptitude for magic, gave her her first staff and encouraged her to pursue magic. He also gave up drinking in the hopes of maintaining his health longer and being able to take care of Fern. Beyond Journey's End. After the defeat of the Demon King, the Hero Party arrives back to the Royal Capital to great fanfare. They join the festivities held in their honor and talk about their ten year adventure together. Heiter in particular revels in the free drink that has been provided for the party. The party then watches the Era Meteors together from the Royal Capital, with Frieren remarking that the view isn't very good and stating that she will bring them to a better spot to view the meteors fifty years later. They promise to gather in the Royal Capital again in fifty years. Eisen asks Frieren if she intends to take on an apprentice, but Frieren coldly tells him that there's no point as her apprentice would soon die anyways. Heiter then cuts the tension by telling them to drop the depressing talk and drink up, as today is a day for celebration. When Frieren leaves the next day to travel the Central Lands, Heiter, Himmel, and Eisen see her off. Heiter comments at the disparity in lifespan, and thus the difference in perception of time, between elves and other species. Eventually, he too splits up from the rest of the party. Fifty years later, the Hero Party, now aged, gathers again as promised in the Royal Capital a week before the Era Meteors. Heiter has become a bishop in the Holy City of Strahl. He then treks with the rest of the party to the spot Frieren wanted to show them, where the party witnesses the Era Meteors together one last time. Afterwards, he is in the Royal Capital for the funeral of Himmel. At the funeral, when people begin to whisper about the lack of emotion that Frieren is showing, he deflects the attention and calls out that he and Eisen are also not crying either. This successfully draws the ire of the funeral attendees, who yell at Heiter to act more like the bishop and call him heartless. When Frieren claims that she knew nothing about Himmel and expresses her regret in never getting to know him, he is understanding and comforts her by patting her head. After the funeral, Heiter parts ways from Frieren and Eisen again. He takes a coach back to the Holy City to attend to his bishop duties, and asks Frieren to pour a drink on his grave once he passes. Frieren asks him whether or not he's scared of dying, but he answers that as the party of heroes who saved the world, they will surely be living the good life up in heaven. Twenty years after the death of the Hero Himmel, Frieren finds Heiter's house in the outskirts of the Holy City. She asks him if he would like a drink, only to find that he has quit drinking. Heiter explains to her that the young girl that found her in the woods, Fern, is a war-orphan from the Southern Lands that he's taken in. Heiter asks Frieren to take on Fern, who shows promise as a mage, as her apprentice. However, citing the death rates of apprentice mages, Frieren tells Heiter that she cannot do that. Apparently resigned, Heiter asks Frieren to decipher grimoires of Ewig the Sage instead. The grimoires supposedly contain spells for resurrection and immortality; Heiter explains to Frieren that despite his younger bravado, now that he is older he is scared of death and wants just a little bit more time, presumably so he can take care of Fern. Frieren agrees to decipher the grimoires; on the side, Heiter asks whether she would be wiling to teach Fern some magic. Frieren, Heiter, and Fern spend the next four years living together. Heiter appears to be in good shape despite his age and is picky with his greens. However, his condition gradually deteriorates over time. After four years, Heiter is asking Frieren about Fern's progress when he collapses in the basement of his house. Now bedridden, he is cared for by Frieren and Fern. Frieren tells Heiter she will hurry with the deciphering, and she finds Fern to tell her to hold off on her training to stay by Heiter's side. Fern is adamant about continuing her training. She reveals to Frieren that Heiter saved her life when she was younger, and now she is determined to prove to him that his kindness was not wasted by becoming a fully-fledged mage before he passes. Hearing her conviction, Frieren leaves Fern be to train. More time passes, with Heiter's condition remaining the same. Frieren finally finishes deciphering the grimoire, but as suspected, it contains neither spells of immortality or resurrection. However, this comes as no surprise to Heiter. He tells Frieren that if Ewig the Sage had such spells at his disposal, he surely would have used them on himself. He then asks Frieren how Fern's training has come along. Frieren says that her skills are still unpolished, but she can be considered a full-fledged mage now, which causes Heiter to remark that Fern made it in time, and that Fern shouldn't hinder her in her travels anymore. This leads Frieren to realize that Heiter tricked her into staying long enough for Fern to become a fully-fledged mage. Heiter then asks Frieren to leave with Fern by tonight. He knows he doesn't have much more time left and he doesn't want Fern to experience losing someone again. However, this upsets Frieren, who reprimands Heiter and tells him that instead of acting cool, he should be saying a proper goodbye to Fern and making as many memories as possible with her. Before she leaves, Frieren asks Heiter why he saved Fern. He tells her that it's what Himmel the Hero would've done. Frieren, hearing the sentiment, supposes that she will do the same. Frieren and Fern take care of Heiter until he passes away. After his death, he is buried in a graveyard in the outskirts of Strahl. As promised, Frieren pours alcohol over his grave. She and Fern then set off from Heiter's house and begin travelling the Central Lands together. While traveling through the Wille Region, Frieren and Fern encounter an Einsam. The Einsam takes the form of Heiter for Fern. The phantom version of Heiter uses one of Fern's memories of Heiter, where he had said that he may visit her again if she was a good girl, against her. The fake version of Heiter says that Fern has been a good girl and praises her growth. Fern is initially unable to shoot the phantom, but when Frieren's concentrated Zoltraak blasts away the mist and reveals the Einsam's true form, Fern is able to gather her resolve and shoot it. After, Fern still appears shaken that the Einsam had used her memories of Heiter against her; Frieren reassures her that they are heading to Aureole where Fern will be able to speak to the real Heiter. Later, when Frieren encounters Eisen again, he reveals that after seeing Frieren's regret at Himmel's funeral, he and Heiter worked together to locate the authentic notes of the Great Mage Flamme, which purportedly contain information on speaking to the dead. Eisen reveals that after Himmel's funeral he and Eisen would exchange letters to stay in touch and share their findings with each other. Travels to Äußerst. While wintering in the Decke Region with Kraft, he tells Frieren to tell him about herself, as he will praise her instead of the Goddess if she doesn't believe in the Goddess. This causes Frieren to remember a similar conversation with Heiter. Heiter, having just donated money for the restoration of an orphanage, asks Frieren to tell him about herself, so that he may praise her instead of the Goddess. When Frieren states that she hasn't done anything praiseworthy, he questions why her constant suppression of her mana wouldn't count. He asks her to tell him the story of her mana limitation even if it isn't interesting, as it may be good future reference in case his child becomes a mage. Remembering this conversation, Frieren tells Kraft that she'll pass, as she's already had someone praise her. Kraft comments that she has a good friend and to cherish them. Frieren initially is about to say that Heiter has already passed, but she reconsiders and tells Kraft that he's in heaven now instead. After meeting Sein, Sein recalls how Heiter visited his village in the Alt Woods. When he visited, Heiter told him and Gorilla many stories about the Hero Party's adventures and took them around the area to see things such as the statues of the forgotten heroes. When Sein is fighting the Chaos Flower, one of the stories he recalls that Heiter told him and Gorilla was about establishing trust in a party. He told Sein and Gorilla that he chose to trust in Frieren's words even if he couldn't read her emotions. However, after hearing his brother's rationale for rejecting Heiter's offer to work in the Holy City, Sein has harbored guilt all these years due to the perceived role he played in keeping his brother tied to the village. While spying on Fern and Stark's reconciliation in the village in the Raad Region, Frieren speaks with Sein on a rooftop and praises him for being a proper adult. Frieren recalls a conversation with Heiter during her stay with him and Fern. She had noted that Heiter seemed more mature, but Heiter disagreed. He explained to her that children, especially hardworking children like Fern, needed adults to provide emotional support and serve as role models, and so he was simply pretending to be a proper adult for her. Frieren then asks Heiter who will praise him for pretending to be an adult until he dies, to which Heiter replies the Goddess. Frieren then gives him head pats and tells him that while he is alive, she will praise him instead; remembering this, in the present day, Frieren pats Sein's head and tells him he's doing a good job of being a proper adult. First-Class Mage Exam. During the First-Class Mage Exam, Sense asks Fern how she is so skilled at magic and yet so passionless. Fern explains that when she was younger, she must have poured every ounce of passion into trying to become a fully-fledged mage fast enough to repay someone very important to her and reassure them that she would be okay. During the second stage of the exam, Fern's staff is broken in the fight against Frieren's Spiegel clone. Though she collects all the fragments of the staff, she is told by Frieren to throw it away and buy a new one. This greatly upsets Fern as her staff had been given to her by Heiter when she was young. The staff holds sentimental value for her and she has cherished it and taken care of it carefully all these years. Frieren then takes the staff to Richter to fix it; when Fern sees the restored staff, she recalls Heiter's advice to her. Heiter had warned her that Frieren lacks both emotion and empathy, and thus disagreements between them were sure to arise, but he reassures her that Frieren will worry and care about you to make up for her own emotional shortcomings. Continued Northern Travels. When Stark accidentally asks Fern on a date, he comes to Frieren for advice on places to take Fern. Frieren shows Stark several places around town that she knows Fern would like. Stark tells Frieren that he's impressed at how well she knows Fern, but Frieren says that she isn't very impressive, but Heiter was. Frieren reveals that every chance Heiter had, he would tell her what Fern liked, as he seemingly wanted her to take the place of Fern's parents. After their date, despite the date itself being a little disappointing, Fern and Stark look out over the city together and reflect on their present happiness. They both attribute their happiness—and the peaceful times that have made said happiness possible—to their masters. Goddess's Monument. Fifty-three years before the death of Himmel the Hero, seven years after the heroes' departure, the Hero Party is in the Northern Plateau, specifically Kino Pass. When Frieren touches the Goddess's Monument and is substituted with a version of herself from eighty years in the future, Heiter is among the rest of the party as they check on Frieren's progress with the monument. When Frieren expresses that she doesn't understand a thing, Heiter bemoans their wasted time and asks whether Frieren is half asleep. On the way back to the main path from the monument, Heiter remarks that Himmel and Eisen spoil Frieren too much. He then lectures Frieren to not waste the party's time on magical detours. To Heiter's shock, Frieren apologizes. He tells her it's okay as long as she understands and offers her candy, leading Himmel to remark that Heiter spoils her too. The party then reaches the main road, where they see the remnants of a band of imperial soldiers. They are then confronted by Zart the Remnant, who accuses Frieren of being the source of the space-time meddling he has detected. The party fights Zart together, with Heiter providing support with his Goddess's Magic. Along with the rest of the party, Heiter picks up on the fact that Frieren is hiding something. When Zart uses his trump card and teleports a large chunk of the mountain into the sky, Heiter, Himmel, and Eisen remain calm. They call out the fact that they know Frieren is hiding a spell that can get them out of the conundrum they are in, and tell her that they trust her. Frieren then makes them swear that they will take the knowledge of the spell she is using to their graves. Later, Heiter looks on in awe as Frieren defeats Zart. He remarks that she really is flying. Once Frieren reveals that she is from eighty years in the future, Heiter comments that it's not so hard to believe after seeing her feats. He asks her whether or not they were able to defeat the Demon King. He guesses that the war between the Demon King's army and humans will still be ongoing eighty years in the future, and asks whether they were able to leave any mark on history at all. Himmel states that it doesn't matter; they are the party of heroes, and they will persist no matter how the end result turns out. The party then discusses how they will return Frieren to her present timeline. They head to the nearest town and consult the mages' guild and church. Whilst in town, Heiter begins to partake in drinking. At the end of the night he drinks with the local villagers. He is fairly drunk by the end of the night and is seen nursing a drink on the ground in the tavern whilst Himmel accepts an escort quest. Himmel then supports him out of the tavern. The next day, while escorting the merchant, Heiter asks Frieren whether she's continuing to journey in the future. Heiter is confused but pleased when Frieren tells him that she thinks he's done a great job. Heiter then senses something ominous. He and the rest of the party defend the merchant from an attack by humanoid wolf-like monsters. Heiter moves to guide the wagon back and further from the frontal attack but is ambushed by a pincer attack from the back. He and Eisen face the monsters attacking from the rear and successfully defend the merchant. They then continue searching for clues. When yet another lead turns out to be a bust, Heiter claims it is no surprise, as the monument of the goddess was itself was created in the age of myth, and if there was more information available, deciphering it wouldn't be so difficult. He suggests the party head to a monastery to see if there are written records of the monument. The next day, the party ascertains the location of a monastery on a sheer dropoff. Heiter prays to the Goddess before they set out on the journey. They take a break while Himmel and Eisen discuss the challenge ahead of them, and Heiter muses that Himmel has been able to enjoy anything and everything since they were kids. This surprises Frieren, who despite being told several times by Heiter that he and Himmel were from the same town had failed to remember the fact. Heiter reiterates that he and Himmel grew up together and that Himmel was always optimistic unlike him. He confides that even now he doesn't fully believe they will be able to defeat the Demon King, but that instead, he has chosen to believe in Himmel. The monastery also proves to have no information, so the party decides to seek out oral traditions and folk tales instead. Himmel uses the promise of trying new local brews in order to inspire Heiter. At the next village, he gets very drunk in the bar and claims that he is questioning the barkeep. The barkeep tells them about a city from the age of the Unified Empire nearby that may have information in the cathedral ruins; the next day, a very hungover Heiter assists in taking down the Abyssal Dragon. They then visit another town where they are directed to the dwarven blacksmith Kiesel. Kiesel tells them to look in the ruins of his old village. The party attempts to go into the village but are quickly forced to flee by monsters. This prompts Heiter to cast a spell to prevent trigger of mana detection on the party. They then sneak into the village, but are forced to split up because of a dragon. Himmel and Heiter take refuge together in the town's abandoned orphanage, where Heiter tells Himmel that the guilt of calling him a fake hero all those years ago has been weighing on him. Himmel forgives him easily as he was motivated by Heiter's words, and he knows that Heiter believes in him now. The two of them affirm their friendship and Heiter's faith in Himmel before confronting the dragon with Frieren and Eisen. After, they find records in the abandoned church that speak of the spell to return that is found in the Time-Travelling Bird chapter of the scriptures. Heiter explains that Goddess's Magic isn't that simple; rather than simply being recorded as a spell in the scriptures, the tales in the scriptures are written as cipher texts. Deciphering the text reveals instructions on how to use the spells of the Goddess, but the process of decoding can take from twenty to thirty years to many generations. In addition, the chapter the spell to return is located in is known as the "Empty Chapter," as not a single spell of the Goddess has been found in that chapter since the earth was first blessed with the scriptures. After Himmel declares that the Hero Party will decipher the spell to return after they defeat the Demon King and carve it onto the monument for Frieren, they then head back towards the Goddess's Monument. They are intercepted on the way by Solitär the Nameless Great Demon, Grausam the Miraculous, and Rivale the Bloody God of War. Eisen stays behind to hold off Rivale, but Grausam then casts the spell to guide to paradise: Ansehelschella. Himmel and Frieren are caught up in the illusion, but Heiter is unaffected due to the Blessings of the Goddess. He holds off Grausam long enough for Himmel to begin to fight whilst still in the illusion. After Himmel and Frieren break out of the illusion, he and Himmel stay behind and hold off Grausam and Solitär long enough for Frieren to make it back to the monument and cast the spell to return.

Hero Party Introduction. The Hero Party was the legendary group of adventurers, consisting of the human Hero Himmel, dwarven Warrior Eisen, human Priest Heiter, and elven Mage Frieren, who defeated the Demon King after a ten-year-long journey. The party was dissolved after they returned to the Royal Capital and they reunited fifty years later for one final adventure to see the Era Meteors together. Member Overview. <br> The party that saved the world and defeated the Demon King consisted of an anti-social elven mage, an alcoholic priest, a somewhat narcissistic hero and a cowardly dwarf. The latter two were nearly executed by the King because of their casual way of address. Himmel and Heiter were sociable and, according to Frieren, could easily open up people's hearts. On the other hand, Frieren and Eisen were more awkward, but in fights they were both more hotheaded and would often fight their way to the goal if it was in sight. All four survived the adventure and made it safely back to the Capital, where they were hailed as heroes. Abilities. The Hero Party's abilities were balanced accordingly to their roles. Frieren and Heiter dealt ranged damage using spells and Goddess's magic respectively. Frieren was immensely knowledgeable about magic and was capable of analyzing and dispelling complicated spells such as the barrier magic of the Immortal Böse. However, her reliance on mana detection meant certain mental magics were more effective on her. Heiter was the party healer. He also provided the party with a variety of support spells, ranging from binding spells to a spell that allowed for subsistence without food, water, and oxygen for up to two months. As a priest, Heiter possessed the Blessings of the Goddess, which gave him immunity to even the curses of a Sage of Destruction. Eisen and Himmel were both frontliners. Eisen wielded an axe and acted as the party vanguard. Eisen was capable of withstanding most physical attacks, such as the bite of a dragon, without any physical injury. He was also resistant to poison and could fall from great heights without taking any damage. Eisen was also capable of running across water. Himmel was the leader of the Hero Party and often decided on tactics for the party. He dealt damage at close range with his immense speed and swordsmanship. Himmel's senses were extremely sharp, to the point where he could fight a Sage of Destruction while under the influence of hypnosis magic. Synopsis. The Hero Party is formed when Himmel and Heiter, deciding to act upon their childhood promise to defeat the Demon King, leave on an adventure together. They first recruit Eisen as their vanguard, and then wander the forests of the Central Lands in search of Frieren, the legendary mage they heard was living in the forest. After recruiting her as their mage, the Hero Party returned to the Royal Capital. The newly formed party immediately ran into mishaps, as Himmel and Eisen were nearly executed by the King for speaking rudely to him. The King then sent them off on their adventure with ten copper coins. The party spent ten years adventuring and facing great challenges together while helping other people along the way. During their travels, they fought numerous Demons. Their feats included sealing the Elder Sage of Corruption, Qual, in the Größe Forest, defeating most of Aura's undead army and thus forcing her to retreat and go into hiding, and taking down two other Sages of Destruction, the Immortal Böse and the Miraculous Grausam. They also conquered the Thousand Mirror Tower. By the end of their journey, they would become the party that had beat the most dungeons in history. Eventually, at the end of their ten year journey, they defeated the Demon King. In the ten years they journeyed together, the Hero Party grew close to one another and genuinely cared for each other as friends. Himmel noted that while they have lousy memories, it was fun. At their journey's end, they reminisced on the silly requests they undertook, Frieren always falling victim to Mimics, and Heiter's frequent alcoholism. Years later, all of them are still friends that readily help in others' times of need, like Frieren caring for Heiter in his twilight years and Eisen helping Frieren obtain Flamme's notes and telling her where to find his pupil because he wanted Frieren to speak Himmel one last time in Aureole. After being recruited by Frieren, Stark comments that despite Eisen having lived long himself, he treasured the ten years he spent adventuring with his friends more than any other period of his life. Eisen notes that although Frieren considered her adventure with the Hero Party just one one-hundredth of her life, that one one-hundredth changed her.

Hero of the South The Hero of the South is a Hero who fought on the front lines against the demons for mankind before Himmel met Frieren. He was said to be mankind's strongest. His final battle was in the Northern Plateau, where he faced all of the Demon King's Seven Sages of Destruction as well as his confidant, Schlacht the Omniscient. He managed to take down three of the Sages of Destruction as well as the Omniscient Schlacht before going down. Personality. The Hero of the South was a level-headed and calm person. Because of his magic to see the future, he was unfazed by the actions of others. Before he even spoke to Frieren, he already anticipated her rejection, and as a result his response to it was nonchalant. Despite knowing his own fate was to die at the hands of demons, he remained committed to fighting for mankind. Though he was disappointed that he would not be the Hero to defeat the Demon King and thus his deeds may be forgotten by the people, he didn't allow it to deter him and he pressed on. He was confident in his own abilities, assuredly proclaiming that he was the strongest hero of mankind. The Hero of the South was calm in the face of death, as he knew that his death would not be in vain. He resolved until the very end to cut open a path for the Hero who will defeat the Demon King. Long after his death, the people of the north, specifically the people of Fabel Village, still remember his heroic deeds for mankind, indicating that even with his precognition, the Hero of the South underestimated the mark he would make on history. Appearance. The Hero of the South possessed neatly combed hair with a bang extending across the right side of his face. His face stands out, as he was a middle-aged man who sported a very finely-groomed moustache, in contrast to the young and beardless Himmel. The Hero of the South was typically depicted as being costumed elaborately. His outfit consisted of a button-up white shirt with a cravat, over which an ornately patterned vest and long overcoat that reached the knee with dark hems, a large collar, and dark patterns scrolling across the sleeves were worn. Two belts strapped his swords to his sides. Beneath the overcoat the Hero of the South wore light colored pants tucked into knee high dark boots. He donned a long, dark cape atop his other pieces of outerwear, held by a corded cloak clasp. Synopsis. History. A year before the Hero of the South was killed, he visited Frieren in the forest in the Central Lands that she was inhabiting. He asked Frieren to join him to defeat the Demon King, but Frieren refused. Instead of trying to persuade her more, he casually gave up and admitted that he didn't know the words to persuade her. Frieren commented that his words were as if he already knew the outcome of their conversation. The Hero of the South revealed that she was correct and because he judged that she would never reveal the secret of his magic, he shared with Frieren that the reason he was the strongest was because he could see the future. He told Frieren that one year from their meeting, he would lose his life in the Northern Plateau at the hands of Schlacht the Omniscient and the Seven Sages of Destruction and die without achieving his goal. Despite this, he told Frieren to not feel bad, as even if Frieren did come with him, this was an inevitability. He assured Frieren that a young hero would soon come visit her. They would journey together and eventually defeat the Demon King. Frieren expressed her incredulity at his words, and he told her that she would see once she met the young hero, and that he would change her life. Before leaving, he asked Frieren for a favor: to tell the hero that, "I promise to blaze a path to the future. I, humanity's greatest hero. The Hero of the South. Even if my great accomplishments are buried and forgotten in the shadows of history." Continued Northern Travels. Frieren's Party arrive in Fabel Village, where they are asked to clean up a statue of their hero. However, when they arrive at the statue, Stark is shocked to find that it isn't a statue of Himmel that they're polishing. He asks Frieren whose statue it is, and she tells him that it is a statue of the Hero of the South. The Hero of the South was said to be mankind's strongest Hero. Stark initially believes this to be an exaggeration, but Frieren states that he deserved the title. The party watches a puppeteer reenact the Hero of the South's story while Frieren tells them about the Hero of the South's feats. He managed to wipe out the Demon King's frontline troops within a year and pushed them back to the northernmost end of the Northern Plateau. There he faced all Seven Sages of Destruction and the Demon King's right hand, chlacht the Omniscient. Schlacht possessed the ability to see a thousand years into the future, and the Hero of the South knew he was beaten. However, he still managed to kill three of the Seven Sages of Destruction and managed to slay the Omniscient Schlacht with his final strike before he fell. Many people in the region were saved from the control of the Seven Sages of Destruction because of the Hero of the South. Their faith in him is strong, and there are some who believe that the Hero of the South is still locked in battle against the Omniscient Schlacht up to this day since his corpse was never found. However, because the demons he fought were man-eaters, Frieren states that it is likely they simply ate him instead. As they begin to clean up the statue, Frieren remembers her meeting with the Hero of the South a year before he fell at the hands of the Seven Sages of Destruction and the Omniscient Schlacht, where he revealed his magic to see the future to her and predicted that she would have an encounter with Himmel and his party that would change her life. After cleaning up the statue, Frieren watches as the villagers gather around the statue, and thinks that the people of the village haven't forgotten the Hero of the South, and he definitely made his mark on history. Abilities. The Hero of the South was immensely powerful and lived up to his title as the strongest of mankind. He was able to take down three of the Seven Sages of Destruction as well as the Omniscient Schlacht in a battle against all of them at the same time. He possessed the tactical knowledge and battle acumen to push back the Demon King's frontline troops to the northernmost end of the Northern Plateau in just a year.

Himmel was the Hero of the Hero Party. With the help of Priest Heiter, Mage Frieren, and Warrior Eisen, he defeated the Demon King, creating an era of peace. After his death from old age, Frieren resolves to get to know Humans better, making him the catalyst for the main storyline of . Personality. Himmel was a laid-back and amiable man, effortlessly getting along with others and forming strong interpersonal connections. Despite challenging circumstances, his unwavering dedication to protecting people made him a beacon of bravery and inspiration for his companions. His selflessness and willingness to go above and beyond to help others left a lasting impression on everyone he encountered. He had a profound impact on those around him, encouraging his friends to follow in his footsteps of kindness and compassion. This influence is evident in Heiter's decision to save Fern from despair, raising her as his own and emulating what he believed Himmel would have done in a similar situation. Though known for his heroism, Himmel did have a slightly narcissistic side, playfully declaring himself handsome and taking great care of his appearance, even in his older years. This added a touch of lightheartedness to his otherwise serious demeanor. Throughout their adventures, it became evident that Himmel harbored romantic feelings for Frieren. Despite the strength of these emotions, Frieren remained unaware of his affection, which added a bittersweet dimension to their bond. In summary, Himmel was a charismatic and caring individual, who fearlessly protected others and inspired his companions with his selflessness. His playful narcissism added charm to his character, making him a memorable and endearing presence in the story. Despite his unrequited feelings for Frieren, his respect and admiration for her endured, leaving an emotional undercurrent in their friendship. Appearance. Himmel was a male Human with blue hair and a mole near his left eye. His eyes were light blue. He was self-declared to be handsome, and took great care of his appearance, even in old age. Himmel wore a long beige cloak that drapes down to his ankles, a fitted blue tunic, white pants, and black boots. Around his waist, he wore a white belt which contrasted with the blue fabric of his tunic. In his old age, Himmel went from a rather tall man to a senior even smaller than the already short Frieren. He was bald in his old age, wore a dark blue mantle, and walked with a cane. Abilities. Himmel was a swordsman with incredible speed and keen senses. Though the Hero Sword he possessed was merely a replica, his caliber more than made up for it, which enabled him to face strong enemies and eventually defeat the Demon King. As the leader of the Hero Party, he was also the tactician. Himmel was also smarter and more intuitive than he let on; although not a mage, he had a hunch Frieren was more powerful than any mage he had met thus far in his journey, despite Heiter's mana supposedly being five times higher than hers on their first meeting.
Himmel's Travel Diary is the fourth spin-off chapter of the "" anthology. It is written and illustrated by Kazumi Yamaguchi.

Himmel/Relationships Relationships. Frieren. Himmel first met Frieren when she found him lost in a forest when he was younger and she wordlessly pointed out the direction of the nearest human settlement. Though he initially thought her response to be cold, Frieren then cast a spell to create a field of flowers. This was the first time Himmel thought that magic was beautiful, and is implied to be part of the reason why he sought Frieren out to be the mage for his party. He was the one that encouraged Frieren to join the party when she herself had already given up on her goal of defeating the Demon King. Himmel loved Frieren greatly, going so far as to give her a mirrored-lotus ring symbolizing eternal love. He understood the difference in emotional and time perception between a long-lived species and himself, and knew that Frieren would not be aware of the meaning behind his actions. In their years journeying together, Himmel helped Frieren open up emotionally to him and to the party. He encouraged her to remember Flamme and asked her to carry his and Heiter's memories to the future with her. Himmel commissioned statues of himself and the Hero Party throughout the land both out of vanity but also as a physical sign of their party's existence. By commissioning statues around the lands, he ensures that the Hero Party will live on in other people's memories and Frieren will not have to carry their memory alone. Though his dream was to marry Frieren, at some point in the journey he gives up on this dream without telling Frieren of his feelings. However, it is strongly implied that he held feelings for Frieren until his death. He is not shown to have had a spouse or children. In his old age, he still talked about Frieren as he traveled around the land, and was described to be happy whenever he talked about her even though he wondered if she had forgotten about him. However, he still had faith that she would fulfill their fifty-year promise to see the Era Meteors again as a party. Heiter. Himmel and Heiter were best friends. The two grew up in the same orphanage. When they were children, Himmel saved a merchant and the merchant gifted Himmel a replica of the Hero's Sword. However, Heiter called Himmel a fake hero, as with a fake sword he could never be a real hero. This would be the initial motivation for Himmel to endeavor to go on and become a real hero that could pull out the Hero's Sword. Throughout their years traveling together, Himmel proved to Heiter that he was a true hero; Heiter would later apologize for calling Himmel a fake hero all those years ago, but Himmel easily forgave him as his words were Himmel's original motivation to travel, and furthermore Heiter truly believed in Himmel now. Though he himself had little faith in the idea of defeating the Demon King, Heiter commented that he believed in Himmel, who always made the impossible possible. Whenever Heiter became cynical about their odds, Himmel was the one to reassure him or otherwise raise the mood again. During the Hero Party's adventure, Himmel and Heiter were both the mood makers of the party, with Himmel often glibly calling out Heiter's alcoholism or making fun of how Heiter was a fake priest in order to distract from heavier moods. Eisen. Eisen was the vanguard of the Hero Party. The two of them greatly respected one another and became close in their ten years journeying together. Himmel trusted Eisen wholeheartedly with his life despite Eisen's admission that he had run away in the past which resulted in the death of his family. He reassured Eisen that they were in a party together, meaning if the need to flee arose, then they would flee together. Himmel is also seen trying to reassure Eisen whenever he noticed Eisen's fear. Though he isn't able to reassure Eisen as he had hoped to, since he himself was scared, Eisen claimed that his words still helped to assuage his fears. Himmel was also well aware of Eisen's capabilities and didn't express surprise at any of Eisen's feats, such as appearing completely unsurprised when Eisen was fine after being flung away by a dragon. The two of them were both fans of scaling difficult terrain, and they would discuss the challenges that awaited them together.

Himmel/Synopsis History. Himmel and Heiter grew up in the same town and orphanage and were best friends with each other as children. According to Heiter, Himmel had been candid and optimistic ever since they were young, with Heiter's more pessimistic personality contrasting him. However, Himmel would often prove Heiter wrong whenever the latter would doubt him, and they were close enough for Heiter to be the first individual that Himmel told about his dream to become a hero. At some point when he was a child, Himmel became lost alone in a forest when picking herbs, and he considered this time as the first time he had experienced solitude in his life. It was at this point where he was found by Frieren, who told him the directions to a nearby human settlement without a word of encouragement. Himmel found her to be cold, but after seeing Frieren produce a field of flowers with a magic spell, he thought for the first time that magic was beautiful. It is implied that this incident is what caused Himmel to seek out Frieren as the mage for the Hero Party. When he was around sixteen years old, Himmel decided to officially set out on a journey to defeat the Demon King. He presumably asked Heiter to join him first, and the two would go on to meet and convince Eisen to join the party. Before officially setting out on their journey, Himmel, Heiter, and Eisen chose to seek out a mage. Upon finding Frieren living alone in the forest, Himmel asked Heiter for an assessment of Frieren's mana. Though Heiter called her an average mage, Himmel was able to intuit that she was the strongest mage he had ever met. Frieren initially did not want to accompany them, stating that she had not fought a demon for five hundred years and that her chance to journey had passed, as it was too late now. However, Himmel declared that what she had done in the past was unimportant, as he was talking instead about the story that she would have now. He stuck out his hand and told her to accept it, as he was her chance at traveling, and this what would ultimately give Frieren the courage to set out on their journey. Synopsis. Beyond Journey's End Arc. After defeating the Demon King, the Hero Party, consisting of Himmel, Frieren, Heiter, and Eisen, is greeted with a grand celebration upon their return to the Royal Capital. During the celebration, they reminisce about their time together and watch the Era Meteors. As per Frieren's suggestion, the Hero Party promises to reunite in fifty years to watch the Era Meteors at a location with a better view. Fifty years after the end of their adventure, Frieren keeps her promise and returns to the Royal Capital to watch the Era Meteors together with the rest of the party, and she also takes the Shadow Dragon's horn that she entrusted Himmel to store for her. Himmel reunites with his party for one last adventure, where they travel for a week to Frieren's proposed location for watching the metors. As they enjoy the sight, Himmel thanks Frieren for granting the party this opportunity. Himmel passes away shortly afterwards, and his funeral is held at the Royal Capital. His death becomes the catalyst for Frieren's journey to better understand humans. Twenty-eight years later, Frieren discovers a ruin containing notes from her late master Flamme, inside which Flamme wrote about the existence of Aureole, otherwise known as the land where souls rest and located at the northernmost end of the continent, Ende. Among these notes, she describes her experience speaking with the souls of her former comrades. At Eisen's suggestion, Frieren decides to embark on a new journey to Ende for the opportunity to speak with Himmel once again. Goddess's Monument Arc. After saying the word written on the Goddess's Monument and touching it, Frieren is sent back to the past at the very same time the Hero Party arrived to the Goddess's Monument. Frieren touches Himmel's face to check that what she is seeing is real. She then asks Himmel's age, to which he replies twenty-three. Frieren realizes she returned to a time period fifty-three years before the Hero Himmel's passing and seven years after the Hero Party started their adventure. As they leave and resume their journey, Himmel and the others quickly notice that something is unusual about Frieren. After finding their way back, they encounter Zart the Remnant, a demon and servant of Grausam the Miraculous, who senses that the source of the space-time interference was Frieren. Himmel engages him in battle, but Zart teleports behind Frieren and sends her high into the sky with his teleportation magic. Zart attempts to make Himmel and the others surrender by using the falling Frieren as his hostage. Himmel initially is ready to comply, but Frieren then shoots a spell at Zart, and Himmel takes this as Frieren's message to refuse. Frieren manages to land safely and counterattacks, and Himmel and Eisen wound Zart as they corner him against a cliff. Himmel notes that Frieren is strangely easy to fight with, as she has adopted a supportive fighting style. However, as the party corners Zart, he uses his magic and touches the cliff itself, teleporting it above them. With evasion seemingly futile, Himmel turns to Frieren and tells her that it is fine for her to go all out, as they have already seen through her unusual behavior since earlier and assumes she may have a spell that can save them. He assures her that she can trust them, and at her request, they swear to keep everything that happened a secret all the way to their graves. Frieren proceeds to destroy the cliff and kills Zart with Zoltraak, guaranteeing that Zart does not live to tell anyone of his realization that Frieren came from the future. Afterwards, Frieren explains that she came from a future no less than eighty years from now. As expected, curiosity arises and Heiter asks if they were able to take down the Demon King successfully. Himmel tries to direct the conversation away from this, but Heiter insists on asking since the Demon King has reigned for so long despite being challenged by legendary heroes. Eisen adds that it is something that even the Hero of the South failed to accomplish. Heiter assumes that the battle against the Demon King is still ongoing in the future, but he requests to know if they were able to leave a mark. This causes Himmel to ask Heiter what he hopes to achieve by asking and if he intends to give up knowing that they cannot beat the Demon King. He remains positive and reminds them that they are the Hero Party and they will fight despite an uncertain future that awaits them. This stops Heiter from asking further, and he thanks Himmel for the reminder. Himmel turns to Frieren and asks her if she knows how to return to the future, which she replies that she does not know how. Heiter notes that they're dealing with the Goddess of Creation's magic, which makes it harder due to the fact that countless mysteries about the Goddess's magic remain unsolved. The group decide to help Frieren return to the future by any means necessary. They later struggle with gathering information about the Goddess's Monument. Himmel takes an escort request along the way, and they successfully deal with an ambush attempt by a group of monsters. They continue their informational seeking quest by asking around in nearby towns but to no avail. Frieren apologizes for the hassle, however Himmel tells her it is fine and the process is also fun. Assuming that some literature about the Goddess's Monument remains, Heiter brings up that monasteries may possess some information. Heiter notes that making copies of books are among a Monk's practices, with the purpose of preserving them for future generations. After asking directions from the church of a nearby village, they head to a monastery on the top of a cliff, which requires them to climb to get to. Himmel and Eisen in particular are excited about this prospect. However, all of their efforts to reach it are in vain as they discover nothing. They continue asking in villages until they got a lead from the barkeeper of a tavern Heiter drinks at. According to what he heard from some adventurers, there were city ruins just to the south that are said to be a city from the age of the Unified Empire, and at its center lies a cathedral. However, an Abyssal Dragon takes the whole town as its territory. The Hero Party manage to take down the Abyssal Dragon, but they are unable to find anything useful inside the cathedral. As they continue searching for information in different villages, they are pointed to a dwarven blacksmith named Kiesel. When they arrive at his place, Kiesel already recognizes Himmel due to tales of his acts of heroism that easily spread, such as repelling the forces of Aura the Guillotine and defeating Böse the Immortal. Frieren then asks about his knowledge of the Goddess's Monument, which he replies he does not have any. However, he recalls that he noticed several books in the chief's home of the village he used to live long ago. He offers to tell the location in exchange for Himmel letting him see his Hero's sword. Himmel acquiesces, and he admits to Kiesel that it is merely a replica. However, Kiesel explains that he is already aware, and he reveals that he forged the blade himself long ago as a collector's piece. He offers to take the blade in exchange for something more suitable for Himmel's caliber. However, Himmel refuses, as he swore that he will wield the sword until he defeats the Demon King and peace is restored in the world. Kiesel then offers to sharpen it instead. He then points the direction of the village and warns them that it has become a den of monsters. Himmel replies he could not ask for more. The swarm of monsters proves to be too much for the Hero Party and they are forced to run. Eisen is flung away by a dragon but survives the fall unscathed, leaving a deep crater in the ground. The group decides to go through the back of the village. They manage to evade the monsters by hiding and through Heiter's spell to avoid mana detection, arriving at the chief's residence. However, the dragon from earlier suddenly appears and attacks them, forcing them to hide indoors. Himmel and Heiter are separated from Frieren and Eisen. While hiding, they reminisce on their childhood memories and Heiter apologizes for calling Himmel an imposter who could never become a true hero back then. Himmel thanks him, as he used his words as motivation and they would have never gotten this far if not for it. He then confirms with Heiter that Heiter believes in him now. As they expected of Frieren and Eisen, the two engage the dragon in a fight, and Himmel and Heiter hurry to support them. After eventually taking it down, they search the chief's residence, and Frieren finds a record that involves the Goddess's Monument. The book they read speaks of the "time-traveling bird." As they analyze the scriptures, they are unable to decipher them, as the scriptures are too complex even for a priest like Heiter. Heiter explains that the scriptures do not have the actual spells of the Goddess recorded, but they are instead a compilation of tales from the Mythical Era. He adds that the tales from the Mythical Era written in scriptures are actually from an extensive cryptogram that conceals the means to cast various spells from the Goddess. According to him, there are far more undiscovered spells than those discovered, and the spells that have been deciphered are chronicled within the Holy City's records. Himmel concludes that the name for the spell to return Frieren to her time has been concealed within the time-traveling bird chapter, and Eisen asks Heiter the estimated time for it to be deciphered, which Heiter cannot determine for it depends on the spell involved, mentioning that it may take decades or even centuries. He adds that the time-traveling bird chapter is also referred to as an "empty chapter," meaning that no one has been able to uncover any spells from said chapter ever since the scriptures were brought to the world by the Goddess. Seeing Frieren's desire to return to the future, Himmel decides that they will take action from then on. He asks Frieren if she had noticed carvings on the Goddess's Monument prior to activating it. At that moment, she remembers noticing "Vialathor" carved, which Fern had mentioned was from the chapter about the time-travelling-bird. As Frieren recalls, Himmel tells her not to tell them what it is. He tells her that word is the name of the spell that will return her to the future and also the word the Hero Party will spend decades deciphering and carve on the monument after they defeat the Demon King. Since returning will require her to touch the monument while reciting the spell, the group heads back to the monument's location. Just as they make their way back, the Hero Party is suddenly attacked by the Greater Demon Rivale, who is aided by Greater Demon Solitär from the shadows. Eisen tells them to get to the monument and stays behind to hold back Rivale. While sprinting their way towards the monument, Grausam the Miraculous, one of the Seven Sages of Destruction, appears before them and casts his spell to guide to paradise: Ansehelschella, trapping Frieren and Himmel into an illusion where they are getting married. As a priest with the Goddess's blessing, Heiter is unaffected by the spell. He tries to wake Himmel up but to no avail. Believing that Himmel will overcome the illusion, Heiter buys some time and fights Grausam. Within the illusion, Himmel stops Frieren from kissing him and tells her that there maybe a way out of the illusion. With an illusion that seemed so real, Frieren deduces that their enemy is none other than Grausam. She admits that she may not be able to do anything, but she is certain that Himmel can figure something out, as the Hero Himmel that she knew never fell for such an illusion. With her guidance, Himmel moves his body despite still being trapped in the illusion. He attacks Grausam, who is about to finish off Heiter. He focuses on his five senses in battle to fight Grausam, and he manages to cut off Grausam's right arm, which finally frees them from the illusion. At the same time, he figures out Solitär's location based on her blades. Himmel then tells Frieren to get back to the monument. Frieren thanks Himmel, who tells her not to worry about it because he was able to witness a great dream, before she runs to the monument. Himmel then attempts to stop the demons from retreating, however, after Solitär makes a threat, he becomes cautious enough to allow the demons to retreat. They pick up an unconscious Frieren at the monument and tell Eisen that they are retreating, and Eisen's battle with Rivale ends in a stalemate. Sometime after, Frieren finally wakes up after returning back to her current self. Himmel tells her that it seems she has safely returned. Frieren wonders what he is talking about, to which he replies is a story meant for the future. Afterwards, the Hero Party continued on their journey and would face Grausam once more at some point. They succeed in killing him this time. Three years later, they successfully defeated the Demon King. Some time much later, Himmel, now an old man, returns to the location of the Goddess's Monument with the purpose of fulfilling his promise to Frieren to carve the spell to return on the monument. While traveling within the area, he meets a young soldier who offers to escort him in the forest. He tells the young soldier the stories of his adventure with the Hero Party but refuses to share his business with the Goddess's Monument. While lamenting on the fact that Frieren may have already forgotten him, he remains hopeful that she will come see him in the end. After carving the words to return on the monument, he then returns to the Royal Capital.
Imperial Territory Travels Arc The Imperial Territory Travels Arc is the ninth story arc in "."

Kanehito Yamada is the writer for the "" manga series with Abe Tsukasa, the illustrator. Previous Works. Nanashi wa Ittai Dare Deshou? was a series written by Kanehito Yamada and illustrated by Kosuke Okazaki, published in Shonen Sunday S. The series ran from June 2014 to May 2015 and was compiled into five volumes. Bocchi Hakase to Robot Shoujo no Zetsubouteki Utopia. was a series written and illustrated by Kanehito Yamada, published in Sunday Webry by Shogakukan. The series ran from September 27, 2016 to December 5, 2017 and was compiled into two volumes. A sequel is set to release on September 15, 2023, the same date as Volume 11 of "Frieren: Beyond Journey's End".

Kanne is a third-class mage who participated in the first-class mage examinations, where she was paired with Frieren and her childhood friend Lawine for the first exam. Personality. Kanne is bright, friendly, and easy-going. She is able to chat easily with Frieren and Fern when she meets them. However, she can be timid and a little scared at times, such as when originally trying to practice Flight magic. She is the type to improve with praise, though Lawine claims this is a result of being spoiled by her parents growing up. According to Lawine, Kanne tries really hard even though she is a coward, works hard when others aren't looking, and is considerate of others. Appearance. Kanne is a young, petite girl of similar stature to Frieren. She has orange eyes and short orange hair, which is styled into uneven bangs and two pigtails with strands that reach the bottom of her face. When she lets down her hair, it gets slightly wavy and reaches the edge of her face. Her usual outfit is composed of a cropped white top with puffy sleeves that reach her elbows and bright green shorts with a white belt. The top is decorated with bright green edges and has shoulder cutouts and triangle-shaped cutouts near her chest and on her back. She additionally wears white over-the-knee boots. When casting spells as a mage, Kanne uses a long, straight staff with a jeweled center and three prongs that are reminiscent of crystals. Synopsis. History. According to Lawine, Kanne was spoiled by her parents growing up. She and Lawine have been friends from childhood. At some point, she attended the Academy of Magic with Lawine. During flight magic training, Kanne was paralyzed by fear and was stuck on the cliff while the rest of their class moved on. Lawine remained with her and attempted to praise her to encourage her. However, when Kanne called one of her compliments creepy, Lawine kicked her off the cliff and towards the water below. This ended up being the push Kanne needed to use her flight magic and served as an example of how Lawine had always encouraged her. First-Class Mage Exam. First Stage. Kanne is one of the participants in the First-Class Mage Exam in Äußerst. In the first stage of the exam, she is placed in the Second Party with Frieren and her childhood friend Lawine. Kanne and Lawine spend a lot of time bickering and fighting with each other. However, once they encounter a Stille, she and Lawine and able to perfectly coordinate their spells in order to trap the Stille in ice. However, this is for naught, as the robust Stille is easily able to escape. After, the party spends time observing Stilles for information. Later that night, Kanne awakens due to a noise she cannot place and sees that Frieren has left the campsite. She wanders into the woods in search of Frieren, but her weakness in mana detection means that she is ambushed by a Geisel that knocks away her staff. In fright, she calls out for Lawine, before the timely arrival of Frieren saves her. Frieren and Kanne have a conversation where Frieren asks about her and Lawine's relationship, and Kanne tells Frieren that they are close despite how their relationship may seem. She then tells Frieren about the sound she heard—rain falling against the antimatter barrier erected around the exam grounds. Frieren formulates a plan with the new information. The next day, the three of them review the information they have learned about the Stille. Frieren then explains her plan to capture the Stille, and the three of them decide to enact it. Taking advantage of fact that water cannot cross the barrier around the exam grounds, thus leaving the rivers dry and preventing rainfall from making its way inside, they plan to pour mana into all of the bodies of water they can find with Kanne and Lawine's spells, then have Frieren wait near a body of water with no mana. The mana-sensitive Stilles are more likely to approach a body of water with no mana, thus allowing Frieren to use her spell to capture a bird. Kanne runs across the exam grounds, pouring her mana into whatever pools of water she comes across. The party then rendezvouses and Kanne and Lawine hide until Frieren is able to capture a Stille. However, the Thirteenth Party has been waiting for the moment when Frieren releases her mana; as soon as they sense it, Laufen uses Jilwer to steal the Stille away. They then engage in battle with the Thirteenth Party. Richter uses Bargland in order to raise a plateau and separate Kanne and Lawine from Frieren. They attempt to put up a fight against Richter, but their difference in mana and ability is too great, and he knocks both Kanne and Lawine down. Lawine attempts to threaten Richter, but he tells both of them to stay down, as his job is to babysit them, not kill them. They watch Frieren's fight versus Denken from atop the plateau. However, once Frieren defeats Denken and reclaims the Stille from Laufen, they are forced to fight Richter again. Though they are outmatched against Richter, Frieren has deciphered the barrier that Serie has erected around the exam grounds and breaks it. This allows the rain to pour down within the barrier. Frieren states that she cannot envision defeating a mage that manipulates water in the rain, and asks Denken whether Richter could. Up above, on the plateau, Lawine is finally able to freeze a shaken Richter's hands to the ground, thus giving Kanne and opening to attack him. Kanne gathers up a huge sphere of rainwater using her water manipulation spell, Reamstroha, and drops it onto Richter, easily crushing his defense magic and defeating him. After, they leave the scene with Frieren, who has secured the Stille, and proceed to hide until sunset. They are one of the six parties that pass the first stage of the exam. Between the first and second stage of the exam, Kanne and Lawine are seen together in Äußerst. Kanne watches from atop a wall as Wirbel and Scharf scout for a warrior. Then, when Lawine shows up garbed in fancy clothes, Kanne compliments her, stating that Lawine looks even prettier than usual. She then gets down on one knee and takes Lawine's hand, cheekily stating that since Lawine is all dressed up, Kanne will be her escort today. This prompts Lawine to sit on her back and pull her pigtails. The two then proceed to go to the same bakery that Frieren, Fern, and Stark are at. Kanne states that meeting Frieren here is good timing, as she had planned to visit Frieren at her inn later. She then buys a basket of treats from the bakery. The two of them tag along with Frieren's Party. Once Wirbel accosts Stark and Fern tells him to take Stark away, Kanne asks whether it's okay to do that, as Wirbel had been an opponent in the first stage of the exam. The four of them then return to Frieren and Fern's inn room, where Kanne presents Frieren with the basket of treats as gratitude for helping her and Lawine pass the first stage of the exam. They then sit and eat treats together, with Kanne's treats restoring Fern's mood. A bird then arrives with details about the second stage of the exam. Kanne and Lawine both bemoan that their chosen proctor is Sense, as she has not passed anyone in the last four exams that she proctored. Second Stage. In the second stage of the exam, Kanne and Lawine head into the Ruins of the King's Tomb together. They are able to make it far into the dungeon thanks to information that Lawine has from her eldest brother, who was part of the advance party that the Continental Magic Association sent to raid the ruins. They come across the group that has teamed up near the innermost depths of the dungeon and join them. When Richter questions why they didn't team up initially if they had intel, Kanne comments that Frieren and Fern were gone by the time they realized teaming up was an option. When Fern reveals Frieren's weakness to the rest of the group, Kanne and Lawine are both unable to see what Frieren's weakness is. They join the rest of the group in formulating a strategy to clear the dungeon. Each of the mages reveals who their worst matchup amongst the other mages would be, and that mage is sent to fight the Spiegel clone of themselves. Kanne and Dünste team up to fight the clone of Richter. After Frieren and Fern defeat the Spiegel clone of Frieren, they reconvene at the chamber in the depths of the dungeon, where Sense tells them that they have passed the second stage of the exam. After the second stage, Kanne and Lawine stand atop a wall overlooking the city together. Kanne muses that three years until the next exam is a long time. A visibly glum Lawine tells Kanne that if she plans on making fun of her, to do so already. However, recognizing that Lawine doesn't want to be made fun of, Kanne comforts Lawine with a pat on her head. Frieren then approaches the two mages, asking them where the best repair shop in town is. Third Stage. In the third stage of the exam, Kanne is the first to be interviewed by Serie. Serie immediately fails her when she enters the exam room. Kanne hesitantly asks why, and Serie tells her that even now, she is afraid of Serie's mana. She cannot visualize herself becoming a first-class mage, and in the world of magic, what cannot be envisioned cannot be. Afterwards, Kanne sits on the steps of the Northern Continental Magic Association alone, musing that the next exam will be in three more years. After the privilege conferment ceremony, Kanne and Lawine see Frieren's Party off when they leave Äußerst. Despite failing, the two are in high spirits. They thank Frieren for all her help and tell her that they'll try again in three years. The two of them remain in Äußerst, and are later seen watching the city from the walls again. The Golden Land. In Edel's memories, she runs into Kanne and Lawine on the streets in Äußerst some time after the First-Class Mage Exam. Edel admires the pastries Kanne and Lawine have bought from the bakery close by. Kanne has chosen a pastry in the shape of a kitty. When Lawine takes a huge bite out of her own pastry, a bunny, Kanne hugs her around her middle and begs her to show more love to cute things. Relationships. Lawine. Kanne grew up with Lawine and the two attended and graduated from the same Academy of Magic. They frequently clash and fight each other physically, a long-standing habit, and their fights usually consist of Lawine grabbing and pulling Kanne's pigtails while pinning her on the ground. They also verbally assault each other, including calling each other names and shutting down the others' ideas if they deem them unnecessary or useless. Despite their unruliness with each other, the two mages are very well versed in coordinating their attacks due to the level of trust they have between them. Additionally, they regularly train together and maintain substantial familiarity with each others' strengths and weaknesses. The coordination and cooperation the two exhibit, along with the ability they have to perfectly time attacks with each other without any hesitation, impresses even Frieren. Although Kanne constantly voices her hatred of Lawine, she regards her as a good friend and depends on her in times of need. Likewise, Lawine supports Kanne through various methods such as praise or force when she is unable to move forward on her own due to lack of confidence or fright. Kanne expresses gratefulness for her actions, as they have allowed her to improve herself and her resolve.
