Macht/Synopsis Synopsis. History. Macht of Golden Land is one of the Seven Sages of Destruction - powerful demon subordinates of the human kings who occupied important territories in the demon war against other races. His unbeatable magic and overwhelming battle prowess earned him the reputation of being the most powerful Sage of Destruction. As a servant of the Demon King, he occasionally carried out attacks on human settlements under the latter's orders, though he detested conflict and seemed dismayed when the Omniscient Schlacht forced him to fight against his will. During his tenure as a Sage of Destruction, he had made acquaintances with other figures in the Demon King Army despite claiming little interest in the Army's survival, such as Demon General Shräg and Qual. He is one of the eleven mages who have defeated Frieren in battle, one of the four demons to have done so. According to Frieren, they had fought about six hundred years ago. Coincidentally, during one of his routine destruction of human settlements, Macht realized that he lacked certain human emotions which humans naturally possess and began on his journey to try understanding them. To do this, he massacred countless humans meaninglessly in an attempt to feel malice and guilt, with little success. At one point, he encountered Solitär, a demon who researched people, to ask about the emotions he was trying to find, and learned human magic from her in the process. Before the battle between the Hero and the South and the Seven Sages of Destruction, Macht was approached by Schlacht and solicitated to fight. Macht was reluctant to cooperate but was compelled to lend his aid with the presence of Miraculous Grausam, a fellow Sage of Destruction and his worst match. Under Schlacht's directions, his memories of the battle was later erased, leaving him with no recollection of the event. During one of his massacres, as he forced a couple of childhood friends kill each other with the promise to let the survivor live. Macht witnessed a human boy demonstrating what he deemed to be "guilt" after killing his childhood friend. He concluded that it was a step closer to the answer he was looking for, and thought he might be able to experience "guilt" as well after killing someone "close" to him. To that end, he set out to find human acquaintances whom he could call "close" after spending a long time together. As he approached the Fortress City of Weise, he attacked a nobleman's carriage out of a whim, killing all of the noble's subordinates. This noble was Glück, the feudal lord of the Fortress City of Weise. Glück offered to teach Macht about the emotions he lacked in exchange for the demon's service to help him deal with his political opponents and take control of the Fortress City of Weise. Intrigued by the noble's machinations, Macht agreed to the deal. He began working for Glück, first by assassinating all of his corrupt political opponents. When the Demon King was defeated by Himmel, Glück introduced him publicly to the people of Weise as a mage of the feudal lord's family. In his new position, he befriended the nobles of Weise according to Glück's commands and eventually gained most of the townspeople's trust. He was put in charge as the magic instructor to Denken, the child of Gluck's deceased relative, after appealing his capacity in magic to Glück. Under his tutelage, Denken became a competent mage. Denken joined in the military and achieved great feats, securing his marriage to Glück's daughter, Lektüre. About twenty years after the beginning of his contract with Glück, a demon attack destroyed the northmost Fortress City, rumored to be done by a single demon. This heightened the anxiety towards demons, which the nobility of Weise made good use to cause political instability. They pressured Glück to bind Macht was equipped with the Stone Bracelet of Servitude, the only magical item in the world capable of controlling a demon's mind, in order to control him. Macht accepted the conditions, knowing full well that the commands they chose were useless against him. Glück thus bound him with three commands, which were: Macht continued to serve Glück afterwards, as the lord grew old. He witnessed the death of Glück's daughter and the departure of Denken from his hometown. One day, as he accompanied Glück back from a visit to his daughter's grave, the feudal lord commented on how old he had gotten and how little Macht had changed in such time. Macht found that this was the impetus to test out what he had set out to do at the beginning: to destroy something "close" to him in order to find guilt and malice. After declaring his intention to Glück, he transformed the entirety of the Fortress City of Weise into gold. Yet the Bracelet of Servitude did not activate, and he had once again failed to gain any new emotion. Disappointed by his failure, Macht spent several days in the destroyed city of Weise, languishing his lack of discovery before deciding he needed to move on. However, it was enough time for Great Mage Serie to show up to eliminate him. Serie revealed she had a magic which reflects all curses back to the casters, effectively countering Macht's specialized magic. She taunted Macht about his inability to return Weise to normal, which seemed to affect him greatly. They engaged in battle, where Serie had the upper hand and was able to neutralize all of Macht's attacks. However, in the midst of battle, Serie's disciples intervened, Lernen being one of them. He begged Serie not to kill Macht and let Diagoldze be lost forever, proposing instead that they seal Macht inside the Fortress City of Weise until they could find a cure to the curse. Serie was incredibly skeptical at this prospect, but she acceded to Lernen's request regardless and departed from the battle. With Serie's approval, Macht was subsequently sealed by the first-class mages inside a powerful barrier, but every year his magic continued to spread outside of its range. The Continental Magic Association continued to manage the barrier and adjust it every year to cover the expansion. During his imprisonment, he continued to kill trespassers of the barrier, although interestingly he did leave some survivors. In an attempt to deter humans from venturing further, he would impale the corpses of intruders he killed and put them on display before transmuting them into gold.

Mage are the magic-wielding class in the world of "". Overview. Mages dedicate themselves to learning how to focus, control, and develop their mana in order to wield magic and cast spells. A mage's abilities vary based on their training and inner nature, but all rely on visualization. In order to successfully cast a spell, a mage must have knowledge of the spell via a grimoire or teacher, a strong image in mind of the spell's effect and outcome, and enough mana to cast it. Many mages are often seen using a staff when using magic, however, some spells can be casted without the assistance of one. While a mage's education can shape the magic they cast, their inner nature and mentality shapes each mage's unique strength, skill, abilities, limitations, and weaknesses with magic. Mages are formally defined as the classes of individuals certified by the current Continental Magic Association. Subclasses are assigned to them based on their capabilities, with fifth-class mages generally being considered full-fledged mages. To receive certification, mages must pass a class exam. Abilities. Humans. Human mages are known for their imagination and flexibility with magic. In the mythical era, human mages were known for developing truly fantastical spells that did not rely on logic and understanding but perception, emotion, and faith, highlighting human imagination and ingenuity in the world of magic. For the variety of spells a human mage can learn and develop, most magical institutions practice what is called "basic magic", which has been developed and refined over decades of study. Most modern-day mages learn to sense the mana around them to detect the presence and power of other mages, suppress or conceal their mana to avoid mana detection, basic attack magic in the form of the Zoltraak spell, defensive magic via creating magical barriers to deflect physical and magical attacks, and flight magic which allows mages to float and soar through the sky. The main limitation of human mages is their lifespan and the amount of mana they can achieve, as mana generally increases in proportion to the number of years trained. Certain spells and magic require an amount of time and study that surpass the ordinary human lifespan, and some mages can spend their entire lives pursuing a spell or branch of magic without reaching their goal. However, among human mages, there are unparalleled geniuses whose magic possesses extraordinary longevity and enduring potency, such as Flamme, who could surpass even modern magic despite being from a period a thousand years prior. Elves. Elven mages are known to be far stronger than human mages due to their great lifespans, which can reach several thousands of years, allowing them to develop an extensive arsenal of spells and a truly immense amount of mana, which they are easily capable of controlling. Known elf mages do not appear to use a separate magic system from humans and are capable of being taught spells from humans and interchangeably teach theirs to human students as well. Some of the greatest mages are known to be elves and have contributed greatly to the development of magical knowledge and spells throughout the ages. However, elves do have limitations in their skills and capacity with certain magics. The stunted emotions of most elves and their tendency to rely heavily on logic limits their versatility. While the magic developed by elves is exceptional, it is often rooted in reason and analysis while human magic can be rooted in emotion, faith, and perception. Therefore, human magic may be difficult for most elven mages to learn, but not impossible. Demons. Demon mages are considered far stronger than average human mages and rival the strength of elven mages, typically requiring mages and warriors of immense skill and strength to defeat them. They naturally possess the ability to perceive and detect mana, and unlike human and elven mages, demons will often learn only one magical discipline. They will improve and master their specific magic and spells for the rest of their lives, which can last for centuries, therefore making them incredibly powerful at the cost of a lack of variety in their magic. Demon society has a hierarchy established through mana, which creates a necessary tie between a demon's mana and the demon's status and pride. The magic a demon mage develops is unique and some demons, such as the, utilize magic that is considered beyond human or elven comprehension and do not abide by the laws of nature due to the differences in human and demon physiology. This results in demon magic being considered a vastly different magic system compared to the ones used by humans and elves. However, with time, research and dedication, mages can learn certain aspects of demon magic in order to adopt or even counteract the spells used by demons, such as Frieren did with Aura the Guillotine's Auserlese spell. Flight magic, which humans only recently incorporated into their magic system, was reverse engineered from a magic that comes naturally to demon mages and is still not fully understood. Additionally, Zoltraak was originally a piercing spell, a killing magic developed by the Elder Sage of Corruption Qual. Through extensive human research, it was deciphered and integrated into basic mage training, alongside powerful defensive barrier magic designed to counteract it. There do exist outliers among demon mages who are so skilled, they are capable of successfully incorporating human spells into their magic. Such demons include Macht and Solitär, a and a respectively, who were capable of using human spells like defensive barriers and Zoltraak. Monsters. Monsters, which include demons, are capable of using curse magic, a unique type of magic that can sedate, petrify, or transform the state of living or nonliving matter, and humans have yet to learn their principles or how to lift them with human magic techniques. Thus, dealing with curses requires a Priest that can use the Goddess's Magic, and devout priests have a level of natural resistance to curses. Mages are unable to recognize or sense curses directly, however, they can be sensitive to the presence of one, which may result in side effects such as errors in mana detection. Classes. Within the mage class are various tiers of mages, which are bestowed through exams held by the Continental Magic Association. The tiers are, from lowest to highest, ninth to first-class. First-class. Mages who have undergone and passed the perilous First-Class Mage Exam are granted the title of first-class mage. The exam itself has a high failure and mortality rate and in the fifty years the Continental Magic Association has existed, less than sixty mages have passed the exam and gained the title of first-class mage. Being granted first-class status comes with privileges many mages consider worth the risk. These include travel access to areas safeguarded by the association, resources and knowledge unavailable to the public, and a single spell of the mage's choosing, including lost and forgotten spells from the mythical era that modern mages could never hope to learn under normal circumstances. The last privilege is granted by the founder of the association, the Great Mage Serie, one of the oldest and most powerful mages in the world. Third-class. Not much is known about details surrounding third-class mages. Fern has maintained the title of the youngest mage to pass with the highest score on the third-class exam ever since she took it at the Holy City of Strahl before starting her journey with Frieren. Fifth-class. Mages that become certified as fifth-class are considered full-fledged mages. This is the minimum required tier a mage must have before they can take the First-Class Mage Exam. Approximately six-hundred mages are currently fifth-class at least. Ninth to sixth-class. Ninth- to sixth-class mages are generally considered in the apprentice stage. Approximately two-thousand mages are currently ninth-class at least.

Magic Special Forces The is an organization of mages serving the Empire that focuses on handling uprisings, particularly among mages. Overview. The Magic Special Forces is an organization consisting of the most powerful mages within the Empire. Imperial mages are trained in warfare and utilize magic specialized for military purposes, with members of the forces being mages officially acknowledged by the Empire. As a result, the forces act as national defense agents that focus on handling uprisings or other incidents involving mages within the Empire. The forces may also be assigned on defense missions, such as acting as bodyguards or monitoring gates. Uniform. Members of the forces wear a uniform consisting of a belted and collared tunic, trousers, a black ascot tie with a gem, a collared cape, black gloves, black boots, and a matching officer cap decorated with the emblem of the Magic Special Forces. Additionally, they each wield a sharp weapon that resembles a baton with an arced hand guard. Synopsis. History. Sometime during his childhood, Land and his grandmother were raided by a member of the forces for an unknown reason. Because of this experience, Land views the forces negatively. The Golden Land Arc. After Solitär dispels the barrier sealing Macht inside Weise, Denken confronts Macht in an attempt to buy time for Frieren's escape. During their battle, Macht notes that he cannot allow Frieren to escape into the Empire, as dispelling the Empire's barrier and dealing with the Magic Special Forces that defend it will be difficult, even if he works alongside Solitär. Foundation Festival Arc. Übel and Land infiltrate a gathering for nobles in the Empire in order to retrieve intel from fellow first-class mage Linear. They are discovered by Magic Special Forces members Kanone and Neu but manage to escape outside. As they make their escape, Land explains the purpose and competence of the Magic Special Forces to Übel, however, he is interrupted when Neu ambushes them. Although Übel attempts to fight against him, Land chooses to give themselves up after Übel is blinded by Neu's magic, and the two are arrested.

Methode is a first-class mage that participated in the First-Class Mage Exam at the same time as Frieren and Fern. She is later assisted by Frieren's party in subjugating demons in the Rufen Region of the Northern Plateau. Personality. Methode possesses a friendly, calm and confident personality, making her a valuable strategist and team player, as demonstrated during the second stage of the First-Class Exam when she willingly cooperated and strategized with other mages. Among the first-class mages, Methode is considered to be considerably upright by Lernen. She has an extreme fondness for cuteness and tiny individuals, especially towards elves like Frieren and Serie. She is notably unfazed by Serie's intimidating presence, focusing solely on how cute the elf is. Ever since becoming a first-class mage, she frequently asks to pat Serie's head, to Serie's reluctance and annoyance. This pampering is not limited to Serie, as she has an easier time giving hugs and pats to Frieren through bribery. After working with Fern to subjugate demons, Methode comments that she also finds Fern's anger adorable. Similar to Denken and Frieren, Methode has a love for magic that she believes separates her from others who only rely on magic to battle. Appearance. Methode is a tall, young adult woman of well-proportioned figure. She has mid-back length brown hair that is wavy and parted through the middle. During the First-Class Mage Exam, her attire consists of a white top with frills at the top, secured by two crossed straps around her neck. She wears a black corset that is laced with white cords and decorated with white outlines and three stripes on each side, over the top and black shorts. Her outfit also includes dark red leggings and tall, laced boots, all of which are concealed under a long, white collared cape that extends below her knees. When she reunites with Frieren and her party deeper into the Northern Plateau, Methode wears a tight-fitting black long sleeve jacket top adorned with thick, black fur at the end of the sleeves and over the collar. She pairs this jacket with a long black waist cape, maroon-red pants, and slim black boots. Synopsis. First-Class Mage Exam (First Stage). Methode is a second-class mage who partakes in the First-Class Mage Examination in Äußerst. She was in the First Party with Ton and Länge for the first stage of the exam, in which they successfully in captured a Stille in an unknown manner. First-Class Mage Exam (Second Stage). In the second stage of the exam, Methode is among the five mages who chose to remain behind, alongside Richter, Denken, Laufen, and Länge, before entering the Ruin's of the King's Tomb together. Once the presence of the water-mirror demon Spiegel was revealed, Methode becomes a valuable piece in coordinating against the demon's imitation of the mages inside the dungeon due to her wide skill set. She is tasked with fighting Fern's clone, against whom she is confident she could win. As a result, twelve mages, including Methode, passed the second stage of the exam. First-Class Mage Exam (Final Stage). The third stage of the exam involves Serie personally interviewing each of the twelve examinees. Methode passes and becomes a first-class mage immediately when she tells Serie that all she can think of during the interview is Serie's cuteness. Divine Revolte. As a newly appointed first-class mage, Methode is tasked by Serie to subjugate demons in the Rufen Region of the Northern Plateau alongside Genau. Genau finds this strange as he believes that Methode does not seem to be a person suited to fighting violently in the plateau, and Methode finds the former to be unpleasant. The two are stationed at Genau's hometown which was massacred at the hands of demons, including the presence of an evidently strong demon. At the same time, Frieren's Party is also tasked with the same subjugation mission, leading both parties to work together. With Stark's input, Methode is able to determine that the said strong demon had to have been a quadruple wielding demon general working with three other demons. She later groups up with Frieren and Fern to search for the demons, leaving Stark and Genau to defend the ravaged village. She takes this as an opportunity to caress and hug the elf by bribing her with a grimoire, much to Fern's annoyance. Their momentary respite is abruptly interrupted by the appearance of two demons: one casting the spell Fog Control: Nebeladora, and the other, a sword-wielding demon who immediately engages Methode in combat. Quickly realizing the need to dispel the fog for Fern, she switches to a wild fighting style while successfully analyzing and dispelling the fog, thus quickly leading to the deaths of the two demons at the hands of Fern. With Stark's and Genau's success in killing the Demon General Divine Revolte, the party is successful in subjugating the demons and the two are healed by Methode. The group temporarily resides in the village before Genau and Methode depart to join the escort of the Chivalric Order of Norm. Methode extends her services to Frieren's Party before leaving, but is rebuffed due to the party's willingness to wait for Sein's return. Relationships. Serie. Methode first encounters Serie during the third stage of the First-Class Mage Exam, and she immediately finds the elf to be tiny and adorable, rather than being intimidated by her mana. This impression prompts Serie to pass her, granting Methode the title of first-class mage. Serie later takes her on as an apprentice, and Methode affectionately expresses her desire to be useful as an apprentice. Due to her fondness for smaller individuals, Methode regularly attempts to pat Serie's head, but Serie seldom allows it and shows a distaste towards the gesture. Edel. Methode is familiar with Edel. She knows of her abilities and thinks highly of them, as she recommends Edel's hypnosis magic as a possible solution for Frieren's Spiegel clone. When an injured Dünste arrives, she asks about Edel's safety. Methode appears to find Edel cute, as she enjoys patting her head. However, Edel considers her scary and eccentric. Abilities. Methode does not seem to specialize in any magic spells, instead relying on her wide pool of spells to take advantage of a situation. She is related to a clan in the Northern Plateau dedicated to killing demons, which shows in her use of a wild, reckless fighting style when necessitated.

Milliarde is an elf acquaintance of Frieren and the creator of the inscription that names Boshaft as the finest spirit in the world. Personality. Milliarde has an apathetic demeanor and spends most of her time spacing out with no direction. She appears to enjoy pranking others as a method to pass time. Appearance. Like all elves, Milliarde has pointed ears. She wears round earrings, and her hair is light-colored with sideswept bangs. Her attire consists of a long dress and a shawl with a single fastening. History. At some point in her life, Frieren met and became acquainted with Milliarde as a fellow Elf. To kill time, Milliarde carved an inscription in ancient Elvish that described Boshaft as the "finest spirit" despite it tasting horrid. Frieren later encountered her and remarked on her passive lifestyle. In response, Milliarde shared a past experience in which she had pursued something for a considerable amount of time, only to discover that the end result was worthless, resulting in her behavior. She explained that elves avoid such a situation by spending the entirety of their lives in the pursuit of something. Milliarde's inscription is discovered by Fass, prompting him to begin his 200-year Boshaft quest. Synopsis. Frieren and her party are shown Milliarde's inscription by Fass after he requests for their help in dispelling the magic barrier protecting the supply of Boshaft. Knowing Milliarde, Frieren is reluctant to help Fass with the quest, but she ultimately gives in after pressure from Fern and Stark. As Frieren works to dispel the barrier, she tells Fern that there are Elves like Milliarde that do anything to relieve boredom, and dedicating one's life to something like the pursuit of Boshaft isn't worth the effort.

Norm Company Territory The is a region situated in the Northern Plateau. It is the location of the Norm Mining Company. Overview. Norm Mining Company. The Company runs an armed transport and distribution network for settlements on the Northern Plateau. Its headquarter is located in the center of a fortified town. Chivalric Order of Norm. The order presents the military arm of the company and their members are in general able to fight demons. They maintain garrisons and among other services provides escort for corpse transports.

Offen Mountain Range A forested mountain range situated in the Northern Lands. Notable landmarks in the region include the Icicle blossom tree. Offen Mountain Range. A forested mountain range situated in the Northern Lands. It is a sparsely populated region with not many people. It contains a diverse amount of plants and animals, which include the Icicle blossom tree. Cabin in the mountains. In the mountain range, there is a small cabin where a man lives. There used to be more houses there, but that was a few dozen years ago at present, and this is all that remains. Events. Twenty-nine years after the Hero Himmel’s passing, Frieren's Party are in the Offen Mountain Range. Stark is walking back to their camp, and is surprised to see that Frieren and Fern are still asleep. He prepares their food, and when he tries to wake Fern up, he notices that she has a fever. He wakes up Frieren so she can check on Fern. Frieren deduces that Fern has a fever, so she will use the notes Sein left them about herbs to cure Fern, but she will have to find out what Fern has first. She diagnoses Fern with magic and finds out that it's just a cold. Stark says that they should find shelter before they get the herbs, luckily they find a cabin. They thank the owner of the cabin. Stark comments that Frieren has been holding Fern's hand since they got here, she tells him it calms Fern down, Fern is embarrassed by this and tells Frieren to stop treating her like a child. They then depart to get the herbs. While finding the herbs, Frieren comments on how Fern will soon be an adult. While at an Icicle Cherry Blossom Tree, Stark asks Frieren why she held Fern's hand since she never treated Fern like a child to that extent before. She said that she had no intention of treating her as one, she said that it is the only way she knew to ease her pain. Frieren asks Stark what she should have done, and he told that what our hearts tell us to do. It then jumps to a flashback of the Hero Party, where Himmel is holding Frieren's hand like she did to Fern. They get back to the cabin and prepare the cure. Afterwards, Fern's condition improves and they then depart to continue their journey.

Official Contests The following lists various official contests related to "". This includes popularity contests, art contests, etc. First Character Popularity Contest. The first character popularity contest took place between September 21, 2022 and October 5, 2022. Voting was conducted online using a points based system, where one point was given for voting on the website, 1000 points were given for a retweet vote, and 10,000 points were given for a retweet vote while following the official Twitter. The contest was in commemoration of the serialization of the 100th chapter of Frieren, as well as for the announcement of the . Accordingly, one hundred characters were available for voting. These characters were officially listed on a Web Sunday campaign page. The results were published with Chapter 105 of the manga, released on December 7, 2022. First Chapter Popularity Contest. The first chapter popularity contest was announced on September 26, 2023 and released alongside an anime celebration campaign where readers could view Volumes 1 through 10 for free online. The chapters eligible included all chapters from Chapter 1 through Chapter 112. The results of the vote were shared in Issue #2 (2024) of Weekly Shonen Sunday, which revealed that 208877 votes were submitted in total. First Fanart Contest. The first fanart contest was announced by the official Twitter account on November 4, 2023, with entries being accepted through December 8, 2023. The contest had two categories: manga and illustrations. Winners were announced on March 1, 2024. Format. Illustrators could enter the contest by posting their work on Twitter with the tag codice_1. Prizes. Two winners, one from each category, were grand prize winners and each received a ¥50,000 travel voucher alongside commentary from the judge of their respective category. Additionally, one runner-up from the manga category and two runner-ups from the illustration category each received a ¥10,000 travel voucher. Second Character Popularity Contest. A second character popularity contest was announced on March 1, 2024, which was also the beginning of the voting period. Audiences were allowed to vote an unlimited number of times. The voting period lasted until March 24, 2024, and the top thirty rankings were published by the official Twitter shortly after. The remaining results will be included in a future issue of Weekly Shonen Sunday. There were a total of 116 characters that could receive votes, which included all introduced characters from Chapter 1 through Chapter 116 of the . A total of 12,688,733 votes were cast. Ranking (Unique Votes). A separate ranking was released with placements for characters based on unique votes, without considering the duplicate votes (one vote per character per person). Over 1.44 million unique votes were casted. First Panel Popularity Contest. The first panel popularity contest was announced on January 26, 2024, with the voting period lasting through February 16, 2024. The selected panels aligned with what was covered during the first cour of the, Chapter 1 through Chapter 36. The panel with the most votes were chosen for sticker and acrylic keychain merchandise. The results of the vote were shared on March 27, 2024 and revealed that 196709 votes were submitted in total.

Official Fan Book The is the first fan book of the " series, released on January 12, 2024. Overview. The fan book is the first official guide book for the series, consisting of 160 pages of content dedicated to describing the characters and world of ".

Orden is a nobleman presiding over the Vorig Fortified City and the current head of the Orden family, one of the Three Great Knightly Houses of the Northern Lands. Personality. Orden has a stern and unexpressive demeanor that often makes him come across as tactless and forceful to others, a trait that Frieren recognizes to be inherited from his grandfather. This trait has often caused him to throw sarcastic remarks against others or start petty arguments. Despite this, he still shows a reassuring and loving side to his sons, Wirt and Mut. Appearance. Orden is a middle-aged man of comparable height to Sein. He sports neatly groomed brownish-red hair, with long bangs draping over the right side of his face where an eyepatch conceals his damaged eye. His eye color is red. His attire consists of a black and blue military uniform suited for a nobleman. He wears a black shirt adorned with dull gold and silver linings, featuring a central red jewel connected to the shoulder by three aiguillettes on the right side. This is complemented by green fabric with intricate gold details under a dark blue coat, embellished with thick dull gold linings in the middle and gray accents on the shoulders, cuffs, and waist. This outfit is paired with dark blue pants and tall black boots. Synopsis. Orden is the current head of the Orden family, recognized as one of the Northern Countries' Three Great Knights. He presides over Vorig, a fortified city that serves as a crucial defense line against demons. His family is said to have a lineage tracing back to a warrior village in the Klee Region. History. At some point, Orden sustained an injury to his right eye during a battle against demons, preventing him from continuing to fight on the front lines. Right before the next large-scale demon invasion, Orden engaged in a trivial argument with his oldest son, Wirt. This resulted in Wirt proclaiming that he did not want to see Orden's face again. The subsequent large-scale demon invasion occurred a month before Frieren’s Party arrived in the region, and the city successfully repelled the demonic forces. Unfortunately, Orden was unable to reconcile with his son before his fateful death in a battle against a demon general. This event was witnessed only by Orden, Gabel, and some confidants. In his final moments, Wirt shared his last wish: to conceal the news of his death and maintain morale until the city's forces were replenished. Abiding by this will, Orden began preparing doppelgangers for an upper-class evening party that will be happening in four months. Travels to Äußerst. Twenty-nine years after Hero Himmel’s demise, Orden and his servant, Gabel, chance upon Stark and the rest of Frieren’s party on the outskirts of Vorig from his carriage. The two promptly approach Stark, examining his body, with Orden expressing admiration for Stark’s body and appearance. As a result, Orden extends an invitation to the party to visit his estate. Inside his estate, Orden initiates an interview with Stark, only to be interrupted by Frieren, who identifies Orden and remarks on his assertiveness reminiscent of his grandfather's traits. Frieren attempts to speak on Stark’s behalf, but Orden dismisses her, sarcastically suggesting to Stark whether he requires his mom's permission to continue the conversation. Orden discloses a request for Stark, offering a reward. This prompts Frieren to leave before being reminded by Fern of the party’s meager funds. Frieren decides to at least hear Orden out. Orden presents the party with a portrait of his eldest son, Wirt, whose resemblance to Stark is striking. Orden then discloses his specific request for Stark – to impersonate his late son at an upcoming party scheduled three months later. The purpose behind this plan is to sustain the city's morale until its manpower is rebuilt. As an incentive, Orden offers 10 Strahl gold coins and a grimoire to Frieren. Orden shares that he has informed his people about Wirt's ongoing recovery from a battle and emphasizes that Stark's distinctive head scar will serve as a suitable symbol of honor. Despite Stark's reluctance, he is compelled to accept the request by Fern. Following this, Orden instructs Gabel to commence Stark's training in noble etiquette. In the midst of Stark's training, Stark questions Orden about his cold demeanor, considering Wirt only recently passed less than two months ago. Orden clarifies that he is simply adhering to Wirt's wishes and admits that a previous look-alike he prepared fell short compared to Stark's appearance. While Orden acknowledges that he does not enjoy the situation, he asserts that this is all for the sake of his son. Subsequently, Orden escorts Stark to an open court, taking the opportunity to introduce Stark to his youngest son, Mut. During this introduction, Orden remarks on Mut's slow progress in swordsmanship, triggering memories of Stark's own past struggles. As Orden initiates the teaching of the Orden Family's swordsmanship technique, Stark begins to tremble in unease. Orden, sensing Stark's discomfort, offers reassurance, emphasizing that this is not Stark's village. Curious about Orden's opinion of Mut, Stark inquires, prompting Orden to acknowledge Mut's lack of natural talent compared to his late brother. However, Orden highlights that he is hard working, expressing confidence that he will eventually surpass Orden in becoming a formidable knight. Stark is reassured in this assessment and encourages Orden to convey his thoughts to Mut. Orden reveals that he frequently does so, contributing to Mut's current struggle for improvement. Orden orders Fern to undergo the same etiquette training as Stark, asserting that a young man like Stark should not attend the party alone. Orden, staring at Frieren, asks if Stark’s mom is going to escort him instead, prompting Fern to begin training. On the night of the party, Orden, accompanied by Gabel, reflects with regret on whether Wirt would have survived had Orden not sustained his eye injury and remained in the front lines. After the event, Stark approaches them, and Orden instructs Gabel to give Frieren her reward. Orden then tries to extend an invitation for Stark to join his family, but Stark firmly maintains that he cannot replace Wirt. Orden concedes, acknowledging that he cannot fill the void left by Stark's father either, but points out that Stark currently lacks a place to call home. Orden reveals his remorse for not reconciling with Wirt after a trivial argument before his demise, recognizing Stark's arrival as a kind of miracle. In response, Stark smiles and says that for a similar reason, he needs to return to his foster father with tales of his journey.

Prequel Novel The "" is a prequel novel that was released on the same date as Volume 13 of the series, April 17, 2024. The novel was written by author Mei Hachimoku and supervised by the author of "Frieren: Beyond Journey's End", Kanehito Yamada. Overview. The Prequel Novel is set before the main events of the series. It contains five original short stories revolving around Frieren, Fern, Stark, Kanne and Lawine, and Aura.

Qual , also known as the the, was a Demon who served the Demon King and was feared during the king's reign. Qual committed great atrocities in the region surrounding the Größe Forest and was the creator of Killing Magic, or Zoltraak, the first piercing spell which was able to overcome all of mankind's magical defenses at the time. Personality. As a Demon, Qual is unable to experience human emotions including empathy. However, he is shown to be level-headed and calm, as upon being unsealed by Frieren, he is not angry and instead greets her like an old acquaintance. In addition, he demonstrates loyalty towards the Demon King: once hearing that Frieren had defeated him, he immediately decides that he will avenge his king. Qual has a strong faith in his magic, appearing surprised when Frieren and Fern are able to block a blast of Zoltraak. In addition, he is highly adaptable and analytical, as shown when he immediately discerns the mechanisms and weaknesses of defensive magic and launches an appropriate counterattack. Appearance. Qual, despite being a Demon, exhibits a monstrous appearance. His face features a square jaw, slanted eyes that appear stapled shut, and jagged teeth that are always visible. Light brown, mask-like markings surround his eyes and dark brown markings recede into his hair line. He has an ashy-brown skin tone covered with dark tattoo bandings and staples that run around his arms and across his body. Two ragged, yellow horns protrude from his head. Qual has long, light-blonde hair that begins in a tuft between the base of his horns and extends to the middle of his back, as well as a long beard which reaches past his waist. Qual's figure is larger than most Demons, and in his sealed form, where he is crouched down, Frieren is only able to reach up to his knee. Qual wears a fur shoulder cape, fur wrist cuffs, and a long, dark-gray loincloth held in place by a chain and a string of tusks. His fingertips taper off in long, pointed nails and are colored red. Synopsis. History. Qual was known as the Elder Sage of Corruption. During the reign of the Demon King, he caused great destruction in the Größe Forest, causing the death of about 40% of the adventurers and 70% of the sorcerers in the region. The source of his power was the magic he developed: Killing Magic, or Zoltraak, which pierced through all of mankind's defensive magic and equipment. During the Hero Party's adventure to slay the Demon King, he engaged in combat with them. Qual proved too strong for the party to defeat, causing Frieren to seal him as a last resort. In the years after Qual was sealed, sorcerers across the continent analyzed his Killing Magic and developed countermeasures against it, with Frieren greatly contributing to the research. As a result, Zoltraak and its counterdefense became the basis of the modern human magic system, turning into ordinary offense and defense magic, respectively. Frieren's seal on Qual remained intact for eighty years, though once a year, Himmel would visit to check on the status of the seal. Beyond Journey's End. Twenty-seven years after Himmel's death, Qual is unsealed by Frieren during her visit to a village in the Größe Forest. After being released and realizing that the Demon King had been defeated, he engages in combat with Frieren and her apprentice Fern. However, he is unable to break the basic defensive magic barrier conjured by Fern with his signature Killing Magic due to his spell being studied and incorporated into human magic systems. After trying to overwhelm the magic barrier casted by Fern with a multi-directional assault, he is defeated in one attack by Frieren using the same magic that he had created. Abilities. Qual was an outstanding sorcerer even among the Demon King's army, managing to kill 40% of the adventures and 70% of the sorcerers in the region of Größe Forest. Due to his immense strength, the Hero's party was unable to defeat him, forcing Frieren to seal him away so she could finish him off later once she was powerful enough to do so. It would take eighty years for mankind to reverse engineer Qual's magic and create a counter-measure against it.

Raad Region The is a region in the . It is a forested region with a large village bisected by a river. Overview. The Raad Region is located in the Northern Lands. The region is heavily forested. There is a large village bisected by a river in the region. The Village. A large village is situated in the region. It has many houses, tarp covered shops in the marketplace, and an inn, with most of the structures and paths built with stone and wood materials. The roofs of the buildings are covered in a variety of materials, including red clay tile and green or blue colored materials. The town also has a large clock tower with a blue roof over an archway. In the square in the center of the village, there is a statue of the Hero Himmel. The town has grown in size since the Hero Party's journey eighty years ago, with more buildings being built on the other side of the main river bisecting the village.

Revolte , also known as, is a demon general. Revolte wields four swords made of magic. Appearance. Revolte is a tall demon with two big, claw-type horns and long, light-colored hair cut into a fringe. On both sides of his face he has two big and deep scars through his eyes that he covers with a mask with circular decoration, five long ornaments dangling over his forehead and two ornaments attached to the bottom of his mask that fall over his cheeks. On his shoulders, he wears a pair of gold pauldrons connected by an pearl-type ornament. He has two pairs of arms. On his wrists, he wears three bracelets. Around his waist, he wears a decorated scarf. The humanoid resemblance ends after his upper half - from waist down, where most demons have legs, his legs are replaced by a light colored snake's body.

Richter is a second-class mage who participated in the First-Class Mage Exam at the same time as Frieren and Fern. He owns a magical store in Äußerst where he specializes in repairing things. Personality. Richter is a pessimist with a gloomy demeanor who comes across as unfriendly and untrustworthy, often showing little respect for others regardless of their stature. Despite this, he can develop a soft spot for others, as evidenced by his willingness to spend time with his former team members after some convincing. He is also seen to be kind to an old woman who frequents his shop despite not wanting to be treated like a kid. As a mage, Richter exhibits a ruthless nature in battle, showing no hesitation when it comes to eliminating other mages to secure victory or prevent their success. He is a pragmatic individual who prefers to assess the situation before taking action and is open to cooperation with others. Richter is also arrogant and confident of his own abilities, to a point where others can easily take advantage of him. He notably takes offense to Frieren giving up from requesting his help on repairing Fern's staff when he initially refused to, ultimately deciding to assist the elf. Synopsis. First-Class Mage Exam. Second Stage. During the second stage of the exam, Richter is one of four other mages who stays behind when Denken proposes that they all cooperate to clear the dungeon together. The others are Laufen, Länge, and Methode. The five of them enter the dungeon together, and Denken's expertise helps them evade an early trap in the dungeon. However, in the next room, gargoyles attack them and Länge is trapped in a small room away from everyone else. The room has spikes on both walls that slowly close in on the victim in the middle. Denken fires Catastravia at the wall to no avail; he directs Länge to break her golem bottle. After she does, the rest of the party watch in awe as the golem carries Länge to safety. The party later comes across a clone of Laufen, though they're able to defeat it quickly. The next clone they come across is Frieren's. The party is unable to defeat it and are forced to retreat. While trying to come up with ways to defeat Frieren's clone, they are joined by a few of the other examinees,

Riegel Canyon The Riegel Canyon is a location in the Central Lands. Eisen’s apprentice Stark used to reside in a village along the canyon before joining Frieren’s Party, and the Fortified City of Waal can be found along the canyon as well. Riegel Canyon. A location in the Central Lands with towering cliffs, rugged forest terrain, and a river running through the canyon. It has many dangerous creatures such as dragons. The Town. A modest town located in the Riegel Canyon. Like most towns it has inns, shops, restaurants, etc. The village has been attacked by dragons, but the warrior Stark was able to repel them. Stark lived in the village after repelling the dragon for some time, before joining Frieren’s Party. Fortified City of Waal. A fortified city that serves as the checkpoint to the Northern Lands. It is a fairly developed city with many shops and other businesses. The city is governed by a castellan, who currently has prohibited entry into the north due to the state of high monster activity past the checkpoint. Walls surround the city, giving protection against monsters which is complimented by the city’s guard. Events. Chapter 10. Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel’s passing, Frieren and Fern have traveled to the Riegel Canyon. While traveling through the Riegel Canyon, they encounter a Solar Dragon in its nest. This is the first time Fern has seen one. Frieren notices a grimoire which she plans to take by killing the dragon. They try and kill the dragon with magic, which seems to be ineffective. The dragon is now angered, so they run away successfully. They think getting a vanguard might help in killing it, which so happens to be what they were traveling to the Riegel Canyon for. More specifically they were searching for Stark, an apprentice of Eisen. They arrive in a village along the canyon and a old lady approaches them with a message from Stark, who wishes to speak with them. While being lead to Stark by the old lady, she tells them of what he has done for the village like defending them from a dragon attack. After the dragon attack Stark has chosen to stay in the village. They meet him at a cliff side with a few children. He asks them if they were the ones that agitated the dragon, telling them to not do that since it could bring harm to the village. He also adds that they should not mess with dragons, showing a scar he got while combatting a shadow dragon. He assumes that they were sent by his master. Frieren then introduces herself. Stark thinks that his master is furious with him, due to him ditching his master and coming to this village in secret. Frieren then asks why he has not killed the dragon yet. Stark does not answer and instead asks them to tell something about themselves. Frieren then tells him that the reason they are here is to ask him to be their vanguard so they can get a grimoire from the dragon’s nest. Frieren asks how much experience Stark has, to which Stark replies that he has none. He begs Frieren to help him defeat the dragon. He believes he was spared on a whim by the dragon, and feels guilty about how well the villagers have treated him. Frieren and Fern give him a day to think it over. After dinner in the town, they hear a sound from the direction they met Stark in. They guess that it is him and Frieren asks Fern to check. She finds him training, and discovers that the unnatural ridge of the cliffside is made by the continuous blows of his axe the past few years. Chapter 11. Fern and Stark talk about protecting the village and about Eisen, Stark’s Master. Fern recalls her first time facing a monster, relating to Stark. The night passes and Frieren and Fern are waiting for Stark so they can face the dragon. Stark is late so Frieren, assuming he will not be joining them, wishes to leave and fight the dragon. She is delayed enough by Fern hugging a tree because she does not want to fight for Stark to arrive. Stark reaffirms with Frieren that she will kill the dragon no matter what, even at the cost of Stark's life. He faces off against the dragon, hitting it with a deadly blow with his axe and killing it in one hit. Before he realizes this, he gets angry at Frieren and calls her a stinking hag when he sees she is making no move to battle the dragon. After he realizes he felled the dragon on his own, he feels proud and Frieren congratulates him. Frieren takes her desired treasures from the nest, though Fern limits her to only three items. The day after, Frieren, Fern, and now Stark depart for their adventure. Chapter 12. Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel’s passing, Frieren, Fern, and Stark are in Waal. Entry to the Northern Lands has been prohibited because monster activity is brimming, so Frieren decides they can relax in Waal for the time being. Fern discovers that they might have to stay in the city for two years, so she and Stark try to find another passage to the north, but to no avail. Stark does not want to stay too long as he wants to experience a deplorable yet fun journey and share his tales with Eisen. Fortunately, the Castellan of Waal finds out Frieren is present, and as thanks for her prior service to the city and in consideration of the plight of the Northern Lands, allows her party to pass through the barrier. With great fanfare, the trio continue their voyage into the north.

Rivale , also known as the, is a Greater Demon. He is recruited by Solitär to fight the Hero Party when the Demon King senses that Frieren has interfered with space-time. Rivale fights Eisen, and out of respect for Eisen's strength, chooses to face Eisen with an axe. He survives the encounter and later attacks Stark's village. Personality. Not much is known about Rivale except that he is usually laid-back and addresses fellow Greater Demons casually. When he meets a strong opponent he cannot help but enjoy combat. Appearance. Rivale is an extremely tall, middle-aged demon. He has long, light colored hair and like all demons has two horns curving out of his head. Rivale's horns are medium-length and point straight up. He wears a black cloak. Synopsis. Rivale is one of the Demon Generals and a Greater Demon. He fights with the Hero Party seven years into their journey in the Kino Pass on the orders of Solitär and relishes in fighting Eisen who is the first opponent he has encountered in a century who is able to block one of his attacks. Rivale then summons an axe and tells Eisen that he will fight him with the same weapon that he uses out of respect. However, their fight ends inconclusively, as Eisen knocks Rivale off the cliff with a Lightning Strike once Himmel orders him to retreat. Sometime after the death of the Hero Himmel, Rivale arrived in Stark's hometown in the Klee Region and razed the village. During the encounter, he fought Stoltz and the other warriors of the village and presumably killed them all, leaving Stark as the only survivor. Relationships. Eisen. Rivale respects Eisen's strength. Eisen is the first person that Rivale has encountered in one hundred years that is able to stop one of his blows. Rivale chooses to fight Eisen using Eisen's preferred choice of weapon, an axe. Abilities. True to his title, Rivale is a Greater Demon and the strongest warrior amongst demonkind. His strength rivals that of Eisen's.

Rohr Road The Rohr Road is a route in the Northern Lands, which has connections to many towns. Rohr Road. A route in the Northern Lands, which has connections to many towns including Äußerst. Town next to the road. A small town next to the Rohr road, located near a bridge in the Rohr road which passes through a gorge. It has many houses and establishments. It is where the stubborn granny lives. Events. Chapter 34. Twenty Nine years after Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren's Party is traveling through the Rohr Road. Sein is asked why he is on a journey, and he says it's to reunite with his best friend. The friend's name is Warrior Gorilla, while Sein's is Priest Goatee. They stop by a town, and Sein gathers clues, which leads him to a grandmother who makes them do errands. The final errand is polishing a statue of some forgotten heroes that look like Sein and Kraft. A flashback occurs where Sein and Warrior Gorilla are standing next to a statue of forgotten heroes, with Heiter. Warrior Gorilla vows to be a hero remembered like Himmel and Heiter gives them the odd nicknames. Sein and co are now done polishing the statue in the present. The Granny tells them where Warrior Gorilla went, which is opposite of where they are going. Sein is unsure of what to do now. They then continue their journey. Chapter 35. right after the events of the last chapter, Frieren's Party is on the Rohr Road. They are discussing Warrior Gorilla's whereabouts, which are likely in the opposite direction from Äußerst. Finding Warrior Gorilla was Sein's reason for going on a journey, so this complicates things. They decide to put off the decision of what Sein will do until tomorrow, and they then go to the cabin Stark rented. While getting supplies, Fern notes that her hands are chilly, Frieren says it's because it's gotten colder lately. They attempt to continue their journey the next day, but a cold wave stops them, which will last for about a month. So they will have to stay in the village for a bit longer. Around the end of the cold wave, Frieren calls on Sein to mediate between Fern and Stark again, which leads to Stark apologizing to Fern. Afterward, Frieren and Sein are having a drink in a Tavern, which leads to Sein asking Frieren why he was so concerned about him, telling him to go on a journey with them. Frieren tells him it's because he reminded her of her old self before she subjugated the Demon King. She also said it's what Himmel would have done, saying that them giving her a chance have her the courage to travel and understand how fun it is to travel with comrades. Sein agrees, that it was fun. Afterward, when the cold wave is over, Frieren's Party departs for their journey. Although it is without Sein, who has chosen to pursue Warrior Gorilla. The now separate parties continue their journeys.

Royal Capital The is a large city in the that holds the King's palace. It is where the Hero Party was tasked with defeating the Demon King and the final destination at the end of their journey. After the party disbands, Himmel resides in the city until his death. Overview. The Royal Capital is a city situated in the . It is the seat of government for the kingdom, however, the size of the kingdom's domain is unknown. The Capital is a bustling city with numerous houses, a palace, and a cathedral, and it has been shown to have lively festivals as exemplified by the celebration for the Hero Party's return. The Palace. The Palace is the residency of the King and the location where he congratulated the Hero Party for successfully defeating the Demon King. It is very large with multiple towers and high walls. Outskirts. Outside of the city is a lush forest with a ravine and bridge, which serves as the location for the Hero Party's disbandment. At a one-week's journey from the Royal Capital, lies a place where the Era Meteors can be seen beautifully. This is where the Hero Party viewed the meteor shower together for the last time, shortly before Himmel's passing. Hero Party Statue. The Hero Party statue is a statue of the members of the Hero Party in the Royal Capital. It is erected in the middle of the plaza after the Demon King's defeat. Himmel's House. The Hero Himmel resides in a house in the city after returning from his journey with the Hero Party. It is a small house inside the Royal Capital and has a fireplace and rocking chair. The Cathedral. The Cathedral is a building in the Royal Capital and the location of Himmel's funeral. History. At some point in Frieren's past after the death of Flamme, a small village began developing near the forest she frequented. The village gradually expanded and grew until it became a large city, serving as the Royal Capital. Himmel, Heiter, and Eisen later encounter Frieren in the nearby forest and recruit her to defeat the Demon King. Synopsis. The Hero Party makes a triumphant return to the Royal Capital after defeating the Demon King. They are congratulated by the King in his palace and statues of the party are erected in their honor. As the party members celebrate in the plaza, they reminisce about their long ten-year adventure and express gratitude for the opportunity to adventure together. At the same time, the party watches the Era Meteors occur, and they all vow to meet again to watch the meteor shower again fifty years later. The next day, the party members depart in the outskirts of the city to go their separate ways, with Frieren going on a journey to acquire more magic throughout the . In her pursuit of magic, she is led her back to the Royal Capital five decades later. She meets up with Himmel in the city and visits his house in her search for a Shadow Dragon horn. Afterwards, they reunite with the rest of the party and travel for a week to see the Era Meteors. Shortly after, Himmel passes away, and his funeral is held in the Royal Capital's cathedral, with the Hero Party mourning his passing. After the funeral, the Hero Party once again bids farewell to each other.

Ruins of the King's Tomb The is a dungeon situated in the . It is set into the side of a sheer rock face that is overgrown with vegetation. A long set of stairs leads to the entrance of the dungeon. The Ruins of the King's Tomb It is inhabited natively by gargoyles, mimics, and the water mirror demon, the Spiegel. The dungeon contains many traps and served as the location for the second stage of the First-Class Mage Exam in Äußerst proctored by Sense. Overview. The Ruins of the King's Tomb is located in the Kühl Region in the Northern Lands. It is an unmapped dungeon from the Unified Dynasty Era. The dungeon contains many entrances, with some being safer than others. Most of the dungeon is built with brick and tile, with round arches and a variety of support pillars. There are a variety of pathways to the innermost depths of the dungeon, with some being long hallways and others being cavernous rooms with winding paths. The dungeon is populated by a variety of monsters, including gargoyles, mimics, and the Spiegel. A wooden door leads to the innermost depths of the dungeon, which consists of a very large, open chamber with high ceilings and ornate flower-motif patterns on the floors. There is an ornately embellished door on the far wall that leads to the treasury room. The Spiegel resides inside this room. There are various real treasure chests inside the dungeon. Most of them contain what Fern deems to be magical junk, though Frieren takes interest in some of the medallions found throughout the dungeon in the chests. The treasury room possesses an enormous mound of gold and treasure, though at least one of the chests in the room is a mimic. Synopsis. First-Class Mage Exam (Second Stage). Sense, the first-class mage proctoring the second stage of the First-Class Mage Exam in Äußerst, chooses the Ruins of the King's Tomb as the location for the second stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. The goal of the exam is to successfully make it to the innermost depths of the dungeon before dawn the next day. Sense, who proclaims herself to be a pacifist, chooses the dungeon in order to limit the mage versus mage fighting necessary to pass. Though the dungeon has never been mapped before, Sense claims that a first-class mage must be able to make the impossible possible, and keep going forward even when the path is unexplored or untrodden. She also provides each participant with a golem in a bottle that was created by Lernen both as a means to escape the dungeon and create a time limit for the exam. Though Denken is a strong proponent of all the examinees working together to clear the dungeon, in the end, only five mages remain behind to team up with Denken. These mages are Richter, Laufen, Methode, and Länge. Other mages choose to enter the tomb with prior connections that they have. Wirbel and Edel both enter with their teams from the first stage of the exam. Meanwhile, having known each other prior to the exam, Frieren and Fern as well as Kanne and Lawine enter together. Ton from the First Party chooses to enter alone, as he is wary of becoming a sacrificial pawn for another mage that is more experienced with dungeons if he joins a team. Übel chooses to enter with Land, as she is still trying to empathize with him to obtain his clone magic. Sense decides to enter the dungeon with Frieren and Fern, judging them to have the best chance of making it to the innermost depths of the dungeon. Frieren is easily able to navigate through the dungeon, pointing out traps and gargoyles before they can activate. She gets caught up in mimics multiple times, but also discovers various loot from chests. Sense talks with Fern about her views on magic, as she recognizes Fern's talent but doesn't understand why she doesn't sense any passion for magic from her. Fern tells Sense that she must have exhausted her passion when she was working to so hard to become a fully-fledged mage to repay someone dear to her for their kindness. When Sense asks why she continues to pursue magic, Fern tells her that Frieren's excitement at discovering magical items made her smile, and that she continues to pursue magic with Frieren in order to see her happy. Denken's makeshift team enters the dungeon. Denken is also able to recognize traps, but they are ambushed by gargoyles and a trap separates Länge on the other side of the wall from the rest of them. Denken attempts to use Catastravia to break the wall to no avail; Länge is forced to forfeit the exam and use Lernen's escape golem in order to retreat. The golem easily breaks through the wall and carries her outside of the dungeon. Wirbel's team also make it deep inside the dungeon. Scharf comments that something has changed; Ehre interrupts Scharf and Wirbel to say that she's been retrained, and there are three mages concealing their mana nearby. Wirbel is able to deduce that the spell Ehre has been bound with is Sorganeil; he tells Scharf to hide them from enemy view with his flower petals in order to disrupt Sorganeil. Clone versions of Wirbel, Ehre, and Scharf then walk into the room. They plan for Scharf to take down Wirbel's clone, Ehre to fight Scharf's clone, and for Wirbel to fight Ehre's clone. Denken's party have also encountered the clones. They have defeated a clone version of Laufen, and note that the mana and skill of the clone were exactly the same as the real Laufen's. The party speculates whether or not the clone has Laufen's memories and whether the caster of the clone spell is able to control multiple clones at the same time. Richter adds that at least they can easily tell who is a clone, so friendly fire will not be an issue. Their party then reaches the chamber in the innermost depths of the tomb, where they realize that there is another clone guarding the door to the treasury in the innermost depths: Frieren's clone. Richter asks Denken whether or not they will be able to defeat this clone, and Denken says that if it weren't an exam, he would have used his golem bottle long ago. They make a hasty retreat from the clone of Frieren. Elsewhere in the dungeon, Land and Übel have been ambushed by Übel's Spiegel clone, who immediately slashed Land and stole his escape golem bottle. Land appears to be in bad condition; he is bleeding heavily and no longer has his bottle to escape with. The two of them are able to deduce that the clone of Übel has copied her memories and personality as well, but is just unable to talk. The only reason the clone hasn't rounded the corner and attacked them is because it is wary of Übel's Sorganeil spell. Übel asks Land whether he is the real version; she then gives Land her own escape golem bottle, and tells him she will get his bottle back for him. Land attempts to stop her, as the bottle is to ensure her own safety, but she ignores him and faces off against her clone. Though she is ultimately caught by her clone's Sorganeil, she comments that her clone is even unluckier than her. Her clone turns around, distracted by the appearance of an uninjured Land, which gives Übel the opportunity to defeat her clone. Land asks Übel, if she knew that it was his clone that was dying and not his real body, why she would go to such lengths. She admits that she knew from his reaction to her offering the escape golem bottle that he wouldn't let her die if she created a situation where she was dying, and says that she feels she was able to learn a little more about him. Various other groups gradually make their way to the door leading to the chamber guarded by Frieren's clone. Lawine in particular is able to give insight on the dungeon, as her brothers were part of an advance party sent by the Continental Magic Association to raid the dungeon. One of the members from Edel's team, Dünste, shows up with information that the clones do not possess a mind, and thus hypnosis magic will not work on them. The rest of Edel's team have forfeited the exam after facing the clone of Sense. They decide that Frieren and Fern will face the Spiegel version of Frieren, while the rest of the examinees will share who their worst matchups are. They will then seek out and find the clone examinee that they are the best matchup against. Doing so will prevent the clones from gathering in the innermost depths of the dungeon, which was the cause of the deaths of many people on the raiding team that Lawine's brothers were on. The plan initially goes well, with the examinees easily able to defeat the clones they have been assigned to face. However, the appearance of Sense's clone throws the plan awry, as Lawine and Richter are easily defeated by her and forced to use their escape golems. Denken arrives too late to save them, but acknowledges that he probably cannot defeat Sense's clone anyways. He then meets up with Land and Übel. Übel is able to easily defeat Sense's clone, as her unique method of visualization means that her cutting magic easily slices through Sense's hair.

Scharf is a third-class mage and member of the eighth party along with Wirbel and Ehre for the First-Class Mage Examination. Personality. Scharf is a quiet person with a calm demeanor. He seldom speaks to others outside of his party, instead letting his partner Wirbel lead. However, whenever Scharf becomes incapacitated, he tears up easily and looks extremely dejected, as seen during his battles against Land, and against Denken's clone. Appearance. Scharf is a young man of extremely tall stature. He has short black hair slicked back, and a single thin long bang running down the right side of his face. He wears a white coat with black cuffs, and a belt running down both of his shoulders and across his upper abdomen. Synopsis. Scharf is a Third-Class mage who participates in the First-Class Mage Exam. First-Class Mage Exam Arc (First Stage). During the First-Class Mage Exam, Scharf's party ambushes Fern's party, attempting to steal their Stille. Scharf fights against Land, and slashes his right shoulder deeply with his flower petal magic. Land notes that Scharf is self-taught and lacking in the fundamentals. Scharf threatens to behead Land if he does not surrender, but another one of Land's clones sneaks up behind him and temporarily paralyzes him. Later, Wirbel begins to ask Scharf to help him carry Ehre until realizing that he was also incapacitated. Scharf asks an extremely dismayed Wirbel to carry him. As Ehre thanks Wirbel for not leaving the two of them behind, Wirbel responds by saying he wouldn't mind leaving them there. Scharf begs Wirbel not to leave him behind, to which Wirbel tells him to stop crying. The party manages to pass by coming across a Stille, which Wirbel restrains using binding magic. After the first stage is over, Wirbel and Scharf are looking for a vanguard to assist them with a subjugation request. Fern agrees to let them take Stark, who reluctantly goes. They are later seen reading Sense's letter during the subjugation, leaving Stark fighting alone, and again later seen eating the boar's meat with Stark. First-Class Mage Exam Arc (Second Stage). At the entrance to the Tomb of the Ruined King, Wirbel refuses to team up with anyone he is unfamiliar with, and beckons Scharf to come with him. Ehre runs after them, yelling at them to wait for her. In the dungeon, the group encounters their mirror clones created by Spiegel, the Reflective Water Demon. Wirbel instructs Scharf to obstruct their vision using flower petals, and tells him to take on Wirbel's clone. Ehre is also instructed to take on Scharf's clone, while Wirbel takes on Ehre's clone. The group manage to defeat their clones and come out relatively unscathed. The group is then approached by Methode, who informs them about Frieren's clone at the core of the dungeon and requests them to assist in taking down Denken's clone, which they accept. The battle ends when Frieren shatters Spiegel's body, and Scharf and Ehre are seen unable to move after the fight. Scharf asks Wirbel to carry him on his back, but he is later seen being levitated by magic by Wirbel. First-Class Mage Exam Arc (Final Stage). Scharf is one of the several immediately failed by Serie, presumably for showing fear towards her mana. Scharf is later seen dejected, with Wirbel at his side comforting him. Scharf and Ehre are last seen accompanying Wirbel to the very north until they reach the Imperial Capital's port town. Continued Northern Travels Arc. Scharf is later seen in an inn along with Wirbel and Ehre. Scharf remains seated with Ehre as Wirbel goes to talk to Stark. When Wirbel asks Frieren to let him convince Stark to join them, he is seen laughing and having a good time with the warrior along with the rest of his group. The next morning Scharf along with Wirbel and Ehre leave the inn they are staying at. They say their goodbyes to Frieren's Party before proceeding down the fork in the road that leads to the Neutral Harbor. Relationships. Wirbel. Scharf and Wirbel appear to be extremely good friends, and they voluntarily chose to partner up for the Second Stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. They are also seen together looking for a vanguard, and also taking on a subjugation request between the First Stage and the Second Stage. Scharf, Wirbel, and Ehre all travel together to the Empire after the events of the First-Class Mage Exam.
