Übel/Relationships Relationships. Land. Übel is placed in the same team as Land for the first stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. She initially teases him for his glasses and his reclusive personality and requests that he opens up more to his team members. After the completion of the first stage of the exam, she follows Land and tries to talk with him, but Land voices his distrust of her due to her killing intent. Übel questions Land in an attempt to understand him more, and he deduces that Übel is interested in him so she can copy his clone magic and expresses his dislike for mages like her that don't fully understand how magic works. He then threatens Übel by saying that if she is to kill him there, she will never be able to empathize with him enough to use his magic. Übel lets him go but responds that she has grown curious about him, and she proceeds to follow him throughout Äußerst, continually trying to speak with him despite his attempts to get her to stop following him. During the second stage of the exam in the Ruins of the King's Tomb, Übel follows Land in, and they are ambushed by the Spiegel clone of Übel, who heavily injures Land and steals his escape golem. Übel shows concern for Land's injury and asks him whether the one bleeding out was real or a clone. She offers him her escape golem, but Land refuses, as the golems are to ensure their own safety. Based on this interaction, Übel, guessing that Land is not someone who would let another die and that the Land bleeding out is a clone and not the real one, leaves him the bottle and faces her clone alone. Though Übel's clone comes out on top in their brief battle, an uninjured Land finishes the clone off. Übel thanks him, as she feels like she's able to understand him a little better now. Land asks whether she thinks she'll be able to sympathize with him soon, but Übel says it will take more time. After the third stage of the exam, Land tells Übel to stop following him around, and they part ways. A while after both mages achieve the rank of first-class, Übel travels to Land's house in his hometown and invites him on a mission given by Serie. He is wary of her, but he ends up inviting her inside to talk. Übel talks about her analysis of Land given how he played it safe during the first-class exam, and she concludes that he is either a cowardly individual or someone with poor taste, potentially both. Land, uncomfortable with her presence, attempts to escape, but Übel later tracks him to his grandmother's grave. Übel voices her lack of understanding surrounding Land, and Land tells her about him, his grandmother, and his connection with his village. He reluctantly agrees to accompany her on the mission as a way to escape and break the lingering ties he has with his village. Übel questions if he is hitting on her and requests that he continues to flirt with her. On their mission, they infiltrate a ball by masquerading as a noble couple, which Übel teases Land about, and he brushes her off. When they become cornered by guards, Land pretends that he and Übel are academy students in a relationship to rid them of suspicion. Wirbel. Übel fought Wirbel in the first stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. After figuring out the requirements for his Sorganeil to activate, she immediately tried to slash Wirbel's eyes. Übel was able to deduce that Wirbel's magic gave him the time to steel himself to kill his opponent. After learning his backstory and motivations, she was able to empathize with Wirbel, and afterwards was able to use Sorganeil. Beyond this, Übel has not expressed any significant interest in Wirbel, but she admitted that she is not yet powerful enough to defeat him. Fern. Übel was on the same team as Fern for the first stage of the First-Class Mage Exam. She teased her for using only basic offense magic, to which Fern tells her to voice her complaints to Frieren, as she was the one that taught her. Sense. During the second-class mage exam two years prior to the First-Class Mage Exam, Sense questioned how Übel was able to kill Burg despite his immovable cloak. Übel explained how her visualization surrounding her cutting magic works, which focused on feeling and intuition rather than logic. Upon understanding this, Sense realized that Übel was her worse matchup, as Sense's magic specialization focused on her hair, which Übel could easily visualize as something meant to be cut. This is later proven when Übel easily defeated Sense's Spiegel clone.

Übel/Synopsis Synopsis. History. Übel grew up in a poor family with her older sister. As a child, she would often watch her sister sew and developed a fascination with how scissors would run smoothly against cloth when cutting it and the sound they would make. This experience ultimately influenced her magic specialization and visualization capabilities. At some point after she grew up, Übel pursued the path of a mage and took and passed the third-class mage exam. Just after she achieved the status of a third-class mage and two years prior to the First-Class Mage Exam attended by Frieren and Fern, Übel attempted the second-class mage exam. The examiner, first-class Mage Burg, a specialist in defensive magic, wore an Immovable Cloak layered with defense techniques and prompted examinees to make him move with offensive attacks. Übel managed to easily cut through both the cloak and Burg, killing him and ultimately resulting in her disqualification. When prompted by first-class mage Sense about how she managed to cut through Burg and his cloak, Übel described her past and how fabric was something meant to be cut. Sense internally praised Übel's visualization abilities and considered her to be on the level of a genius. Übel then complimented her hair and mentioned how the maintenance must be difficult, with Sense realizing how one-sided a battle against Übel would be. First-Class Mage Exam Arc (First Stage). Prior to the start of the First-Class Mage Exam, Übel journeys to Äußerst solo. She arrives at the frontier of Graf Granat's Domain and figures the town within should be close, electing to take a break. She is suddenly ambushed by bandits interested in her staff, and she prepares to confront them, voicing that she has to deal with bandits again despite the peacefulness that came to the area after Aura's defeat. Before she can retaliate, Kraft intervenes and punches a bandit, forcing them to flee. Übel thanks him for saving her and introduces herself, expressing awe in seeing an elf for the first time. Kraft tells her that he wasn't trying to save her, and he discovered corpses of bandits nearby that were the work of a frighteningly skilled mage. He states that he won't chide her for utilizing self-defense, but that he simply intended to save some lives. He asks if she is aiming for Äußerst, and Übel confirms. They go their separate ways, with Kraft remembering that Frieren was heading for Äußerst as well. Later, Übel is one of the candidates for the First-Class Mage Exam, held in Äußerst. While in the exam hall, she is pointed out by Falsch, who considers her a troublemaker and the third-class mage that killed the proctor of the second-class mage exam two years prior. Genau announces the start of the first stage of the exam, and Übel is paired up with Land and Fern. At the exam location, they receive detailed instuctions: they must capture a Stille and return with all their party members by sunset of the next day. As the party wanders the exam location, they get lucky with a Stille's nest and Fern manages to catch one with her spell to capture a bird. Übel expresses excitement over potentially fighting against other mages now that they have a Stille to defend, though Land prefers to play it safe and hide. Needing to replenish their water supply, the party makes their way to the central lake. Übel notices a dried up riverbed, and the party realizes that with most of the water sources gone due to the barrier, other examinees will likely be near the lake waiting for the opportunity to catch hydrating Stilles. They choose to avoid the lake and search for other sources of water, but suddenly, they are ambushed by Wirbel's party. Fern manages to defend against the initial attacks from the ambush and Übel immediately moves to confront Wirbel, who instructs her to leave the Stille for them. They are abruptly distracted by the lake being frozen by Lawine but resume fighting shortly after, with Fern pairing up against Ehre, Übel against Wirbel, and Land against Scharf. Übel casts multiple Reelseiden attacks against Wirbel, who is forced to go on the defensive. Übel notices she caused some destruction, with trees fallen due to her attacks, and Wirbel infers that her spell has a range of around five meters, which she confirms. She asks if they plan on continuing to exchange basic spells, and he responds that such is unnecessary, binding her with Sorganeil. With Sorganeil active, Übel realizes she is unable to move or control her mana, and such a spell would be useful for capturing a Stille if Wirbel's party could find one. Wirbel reveals that as long as he can see her, Sorganeil will be active, and he can now kill her easily. Übel realizes he went easy on them during the earlier ambush, and binding them would have been the choice had he intended to kill them. Wirbel tells her to leave the Stille and go, but she notices that Wirbel could have just taken the Stille from her instead of giving an order. She flings the cage with the Stille above her, distracting Wirbel's vision, and immediately gets close to him and aims a slash for his eyes. However, she misses and instead slashes the bridge of his nose. Wirbel tells her she should have gone for his neck to swiftly end the fight, and those that had also gone for his eyes instead in previous battles all displayed an enjoyment for killing. He recaptures Übel with Sorganeil and prepares to kill her. Übel strikes up a conversation with him and asks if he had ever killed women and children, wondering what kind of life he had lived. He notes that Übel is trying to buy time but chooses to answer her questions, and he explains that although the Northern Magic Corps would typically fight against demons, they would also settle conflicts between nations, and such involved the reality of women and children being used as weapons during war. Übel tells him that she finds one's magic specialization to be connected with their life and character, and that Wirbel appears to use Sorganeil in order to give himself more time before making a kill, which is also why he did not mind Übel buying time for herself. She finds it surprising that Wirbel still wishes to be human, and he agrees, but he informs her that he has never skipped out on a necessary kill and prepares to execute her. Right before he can cast a spell, Fern appears beside him and aims her staff at his head, telling him not to move. Wirbel expresses shock towards Fern's mana concealment and observes that she was likely the one to catch the Stille, and Übel confesses they were lucky that they came across a nest and Fern knew a spell to capture a bird. She pities Wirbel's lack of luck, as he could capture anything yet wasn't able to find a Stille. Fern tells Wirbel she killed Ehre, and he accepts his loss, releasing Übel with the explanation that he does not want to make an unnecessary kill. Übel prepares to attack him, but Wirbel advises that doing so will turn an unnecessary kill into a necessary one. Übel complies and lets him go. After he leaves, she applauds Fern for being a decent liar. Fern tries to go assist Land, but Übel claims that he will be fine on his own. The party later regroups and finds shelter in a cave after Frieren destroys the barrier, letting in rain. While waiting for the rain to pass, Übel tells Fern that she is boring for using basic spells and requests she tell Frieren off for bringing in rain, which Fern agrees. They discuss other spells Fern can use, and Land cautions them from revealing too much about each other given that they will be enemies in the second exam. Übel accepts his advice but tells him that he could open up to them more. At sunset, the party successfully defend their Stille and pass the exam, advancing them to the second stage. During the intermission between the first and second exam, Übel follows Land into an alleyway in Äußerst, where she notices that he does not use his clone in town. They converse, with Übel telling Land that she might kill him if he runs, and he replies by asking why she spared Wirbel despite not feeling any guilt about killing. She realizes that Land was watching her battle and responds that it was likely because she empathized with him regarding wanting some time before killing. She proceeds to use Sorganeil on Land, holding him in place, and she explains that specialized magic is connected to one's life and character and she is capable of copying spells through empathy. She asks Land about what his life was like to create perfect clones of himself, and he ignores her question, instead telling her he does not like individuals like her that use magic based on feel rather than understanding. He also states that he does not care if she kills him, but she will never be able to empathize with him if she does. Hearing this, Übel yields and frees him from Sorganeil, and she determines that she is starting to understand him and wishes to continue getting to know him. Although he requests she does not follow him, she accompanies him to a famous restaurant where other candidates are also in attendance, and they dine together. Later, Übel and Land receive details on the second stage of the exam via messenger bird while sitting on a bench. First-Class Mage Exam Arc (Second Stage). Übel arrives alongside the other examinees at the Ruins of the King's Tomb, where Sense outlines the details for the second exam. She chooses to enter with Land, and they traverse the dungeon and reach a corridor. As they continue exploring the area, Übel's Spiegel clone suddenly ambushes them, slicing Land across his chest and stealing his escape golem. Übel and Land are left cornered by the clone at a dead end while Land bleeds out from his chest. Given Land's speciality in cloning magic, Übel asks for his expertise regarding how well the clone has copied her memories and abilities. Land refers to Übel's inability to stop talking even during battle, which she admits, and she further points out that her clone has not spoken and assumes it hasn't copied her memories or personality. Land disagrees and explains it likely can't talk, and given how the clone went for his sole method of escape in its initial attack, it presumably has knowledge of them and their personalities. Übel concurs and notes that she would have done the same in an ambush. Land guesses that the clone may be wary of Übel's Sorganeil, hence why it has yet to attack them again, but Übel suggests that it may just be toying with them instead. Übel notices Land's drastic blood loss and tells him he won't last long in his current state. She asks if he is the real Land, and he chooses not to give a straight answer. Übel hands him her escape golem and instructs him to use it, but he rejects her offer and asserts that the golem is for her survival. Übel leaves her golem and declares she will retrieve his golem, summoning her staff and confronting her clone. The two of them engage in battle and are evenly matched. During their fight, Übel notices that the clone is acting as she would through tactics such as minimizing distance to decrease the odds of its full body coming into view, the requirement for Sorganeil to activate. With such an equal matchup, Übel realizes that the outcome of the battle will depend on luck, and she expresses her displeasure for such battles. The clone manages to separate itself from Übel with a distance long enough for it to cast Sorganeil, binding her. Übel laments her poor luck but tells her clone that it must've been unluckier, alluding to the real Land, who appears right behind the clone. As it turns in surprise to face him, it unintentionally deactivates Sorganeil, enabling Übel to kill it with a slash. As the clone disintegrates, Übel pulls out the stolen bottle and comments that it was fake as well. Land asks why Übel chose the risk of confronting her clone if she was aware that the Land she was talking to previously was a clone, and she explains that she knew he would come to aid her during their battle. He wonders if she truly considers him to be that kind, and she responds that although she did not, his clone didn't take her bottle, and with Land giving off the impression of someone who hated to be involved in another's death, she created a situation where such a circumstance could occur. She thanks and tells him that she is learning more about him, though empathizing with him will still take more time. They make their way further into the dungeon, eventually coming across Denken, who is observing Sense's clone. Denken admits that he would not be able to defeat it, and Übel requests to know if doing so is necessary for clearing the dungeon. He tells her it is, and she offers to handle it. Land reminds her that Denken is the strongest among them, and she was incapable of defeating even Wirbel. Übel acknowledges that she is rather weak in comparison to Denken and Wirbel, but she could defeat Sense's clone with her speciality: Reelseiden. Land mentions that defense magic can block her spell, and Übel agrees, as she cannot easily imagine cutting through something meant to block magic. He argues that if such is the case, her spell will be even less effective against Sense's clone, as her hair has numerous layers of defense magic embedded. Übel replies that it doesn't matter, and visualization is what is necessary. Übel comes out of hiding, and Sense's clone prepares to attack her. She tries using Sorganeil but realizes it doesn't work due to how widespread the clone's hair—which is part of its body—is, making it difficult for her to capture its full body in view. As the clone directs multiple spikes of hair to pierce Übel, she casts Reelseiden. Sense notices that Übel is her clone's matchup and refers to Übel's performance during the second-class mage exam two years ago, where she slashed through and accidentally killed first-class mage proctor Burg despite him wearing his Immovable Cloak. In a later conversation she had with Sense where she confirmed her disqualification from the exam, Sense learned about her visualization technique with Reelseiden that ignored logic and simply relied on Übel's feelings and intuition. Sense notes how that was the point where she lost to Übel, as her magic hair was wholly incompatible with Übel's magic and visualization. Back in the dungeon, Übel cleanly slices through Sense's clone, killing it. As Übel reconvenes with Land and Denken after her battle, Land gets bound by Sorganeil, and they realize that the clone of Übel has reappeared, accompanied by Land's clone. They're also approached by Kanne, Lawine, and Laufen's clone from the other end of the corridor. Übel readies herself for a battle of attrition and expresses her excitement. The three mages ultimately manage to hold out long enough for Frieren and Fern to defeat Frieren's clone and subsequently the Spiegel, resulting in the disappearance of all the clones. The remaining examinees gather at the innermost depths, and Sense congratulates them on completing the second stage of the exam. First-Class Mage Exam Arc (Final Stage). As one of the successful examinees from the second stage, Übel congregates with the others for the third exam, which is an interview with Continental Magic Association founder Serie. During Übel's turn, Serie passes her without exchanging words, and thus, having successfully passed all three exams, Übel achieves the title of first-class mage. After the exam, Land tells Übel not to follow her around. The ceremony for Serie to grant the new first-class mages their privileges occurs soon after, and the following day, Übel departs from Äußerst on her own.

Alt Woods A forest past the Appetit Region. It has hills and bottomless swamps and many fauna of the forest are extremely venomous. The venom of the snake that bites Stark can only be cured in the early stages. There are various herbs in the woods that can be foraged. Overview. The Alt Woods is a heavily forested region. The region also features swamps and mountains. Village. A small and modest village that Sein and his brother live in. It is Sein and his brother's hometown, but they were orphaned when they were younger. Warrior Gorilla once lived in this town, but set out ten years prior to adventure around the Northern Lands. In the autumn, the town celebrates by holding a Harvest Festival. A river runs along the side of the village. History. Sein, Gorilla, and Sein's Brother grew up in the village in the Alt Woods. At some point early in their childhood, Sein and his brother's parents passed away. Sein's Brother would take on the responsibility of caring for his brother. Both Sein and Gorilla had dreams of leaving the village and adventuring. They would often play rambunctiously in the village and Sein would often share these dreams with his brother. When they were younger, a traveling mage visited the village and took a picture of Sein and Gorilla together using photo-taking magic. It is unknown when Sein and his brother began their work in the clergy, but both grew to be skilled with Goddess's Magic. Heiter visited the village while Sein was younger in an official capacity from the Holy City of Strahl. He conducted inspections of the church and assessed Sein's Brother to be the best priest in the region and conferred upon him a Holy Symbol. He also invited Sein's Brother to work in the Holy City, but Sein's Brother refused, as he was fine with his life in the village and didn't want to take Sein's hometown away from him. Sein overhears this and begins to feel guilty for the perceived sacrifice his brother is making for him. Ten years prior to Frieren's Party's visit to the village, Gorilla decides to go out and travel in the Northern Lands. He asks Sein to come with him, as they'd wanted to do since childhood. However, Sein refuses him. Gorilla then states that he will return in three years time for the village's annual Harvest Festival. However, ten years go by without word from Gorilla, and Sein begins to believe he is dead.

Anytime Anywhere Anytime Anywhere is the ending theme for the first season of "" across both its first and second cours. It is written and performed by, composed by milet,, and, and arranged by . Description. "Anytime Anywhere" is the first ending theme of the "" anime series. It is produced and performed by milet with arrangement by Evan Call, the music composer for the anime. The song was released as part of the single album of the same name, "Anytime Anywhere", on September 29, 2023, the same date as the airing of the anime's first episode. It was also included in a limited edition CD released on January 31, 2024 alongside the special ending theme "bliss".

Appetit Region A mountainous region in the Northern Lands. It features snowy terrain, forests, and a town with wood and stone buildings. Overview. A region in the Northern Lands. It is a mountainous region with lush forests. It also supports a town. The Town. A town in the Appetit Region. It houses a sizable population with many establishments. Synopsis. On Stark's eighteenth birthday, Frieren and Fern discuss what to give him as birthday gifts. Frieren decides on a drug that melts clothes, which is quickly shut down by Fern, who pours it on her, leaving Frieren to find a new gift. Fern decides to investigate Stark on her own and ends up asking him directly what he desired. Stark mentions how he never received gifts growing up due to his weakness, and his brother, Stolz, the best warrior in his hometown and the only one kind to Stark, was the one to fight against demons during an attack while he simply fled. Fern comforts him and they find a gift, returning to the inn where Frieren is cooking giant s. Frieren reveals she received the recipe from Eisen, who had always made steaks for Stark's birthday and for the members of the Hero Party during their journey as a way of expressing gratitude towards their efforts as warriors. Stark recalls his brother making a steak for his birthday as well and that his brother was the one who told him to escape the fateful night of the demon attack. In better spirits, he enjoys the rest of his birthday with his companions.

Art Works Volume 1 is the first artbook of the "" series. It consists of over 100 unique illustrations by Abe Tsukasa, including past and unreleased works. The volume was released on December 18, 2023. Overview. The first artbook was released on the same date as Volume 12 of the . It consists of 128 pages of original illustrations related to the series printed in the original B5 magazine sizing.

Aura , also known as is one of the Seven Sages of Destruction directly serving the Demon King. Using her signature magic, Auserlese, she weighs the mana of her opponent's soul as well as her own on her Scales of Obedience, granting the soul with more mana complete control over the other's body. Personality. Aura is, as a demon, an articulate monster who is individualistic and harbors no sense of empathy. Even though she has her executioners as subordinates, she was not distressed in the slightest to learn of their demise. Typical of her race, she has strong confidence in the superiority of her magic and seems to enjoy battles where she thinks she has the upper hand. However, Aura has also shown to be a cautious person. When she is up against enemies whom she could not beat, such as the Hero Party, she will opt to choose to retreat instead of trying to face them head-on. This tendency contributed to her survival when the Demon King was defeated. She also makes sure to check for signs of mana instability in a mage and is aware of the history of renowned mages that she fights, such as Frieren. Appearance. Aura has magenta hair that reaches to the middle of her back. Her hair is gathered in two large pigtails tied at the shoulder. The remaining hair in the pigtails is sectioned off into three braids. Aura has dark blue eyes and two light brown horns protruding through her hair. She wears a dark, sleeveless bodice with white trimmings that has a cutout at her navel and a ruffled white skirt underneath. A magenta skirt tail is fastened at her waist with gold buttons, complementing the golden accessories at her neck. Her opera gloves are the same color as her bodice and wrap around her upper arm in a series of threads, and her boots are striped and reach her mid thigh. Synopsis. History. Aura became a Sage of Destruction more than five hundred years ago and built an army out of the people whom she subjugated with her magic. She is famous for decapitating every person she successfully controlled upon finding out that a person with sufficient willpower could partially defy her magic, granting her the title of "Aura the Guillotine." At some point, she and all Sages of Destruction were called to assist in a coming battle against the Hero of the South under the command of Schlacht. She survived the encounter, though at the cost of three of her fellow Sages and Schlacht himself. When she faced the Hero Party, she suffered the loss of a significant portion of her undead army, was injured by Himmel, and was forced to retreat. The party would go on to defeat the Demon King. Afterwards, Aura remained in hiding until Himmel's passing. After Himmel's death, Aura reappeared and began to wage a war in order to take over Graf Granat's Domain in the . This led to a bitter conflict with the humans there since and resulted in the death of Graf Granat's son after he was enlisted to fight in the war. Aura the Guillotine Arc. Twenty-eight years post Himmel's death, Aura, seemingly tired of war, sends three of her executioners, Lügner, Linie, and Draht, as messengers to negotiate for peace with Graf Granat by the time Frieren's Party arrives. However, her real intention was to lower the Graf's guard and persuade him to disable the powerful barrier surrounding his domain, effectively giving her and her army free access. However, Frieren kills Draht, one of Aura's executioners, and proceeds to confront her outside the town. After a short battle against her undead army, Aura finally decides to use her Scales of Obedience, putting both of their souls on it to see which individual possesses more mana. At first, the scale appears to favor her soul, but it suddenly starts shifting to Frieren. Frieren reveals her mana concealment strategy, and Aura is unable to comprehend that a mage would limit their mana their entire life just to deceive demons. Aura emphasizes that she has lived for over five hundred years, but Frieren reveals that she has lived for more than a thousand years and reveals her true mana output, which is much higher than Aura's. This leads to Aura losing to her own submission magic, giving Frieren free rein over Aura's body. Frieren then orders Aura to kill herself, to which she is forced to comply by cutting off her own head.

Aura the Guillotine Arc The Aura the Guillotine Arc is the second story arc in "." Summary. Prologue. Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel’s passing, Frieren, Fern, and Stark are in Graf Granat’s Domain. As the trio walks into town, Frieren senses some Demon and tries to kill them, but she is stopped by sentinels. The Demon, led by Lord Lügner, are supposedly messengers of peace, however, Frieren calls them incomprehensible wild beasts that mimic human voices. She is then thrown into the mansion dungeon. Fern and Stark investigate and find out Aura the Guillotine, a great demon who served the Demon King as one of the Seven Sages of Destruction, has requested peace after being long at war with the town. Frieren states that it is futile to negotiate with Demon, as they only use words as a means of deception rather than communication. She decides to break out of the dungeon once the disorder starts. Meanwhile, Lügner wonders where he has seen Frieren before and smiles as she is the only one in town who knows the true nature of Demon. Monsters That Speak. Twenty-eight years after the Hero Himmel’s passing, Frieren, Fern, and Stark are in the Northern Lands, specifically Graf Granat’s Domain. As the trio walks into town, Frieren notices that there are many sentinels around and senses some Demon. She tries to kill them but is stopped by the sentinels. The one leading the Demon, Lord Lügner, asks Graf Granat if he is trying to instigate something. He denies it saying he is not foolish enough to harm messengers of peace, and Lügner lets the matter go. He remarks how Frieren looks at him as if she is looking at a wild beast, unlike the townspeople. She concurs with his remark, saying that Demon are simply incomprehensible wild beasts that mimic human voices, making Lügner smile. Frieren is then thrown into the mansion dungeon to serve a two to three-year sentence. When Fern and Stark visit her, they tell her that they investigated and found out that Aura the Guillotine, a great demon who served the Demon King as one of the Seven Sages of Destruction, has been regaining power since over 28 years ago. The town has been long at war with her army but it seems she has requested peace after being growing tired of the war. Frieren calls allowing the messengers inside a bad move, as it is futile to negotiate with Demon. Stark disagrees, saying it will be ideal for the matter to be resolved through negotiation. Frieren refutes him, saying it’s futile because it won’t be resolved. She calls Demon man-eating monsters and recalls an old memory of when she was travelling with the Hero Party. The Hero Party chases and stops an injured, childlike demon who ate the daughter of a villager. As Himmel is about to kill her, she starts saying “It hurts.. It really hurts… Mother”, causing Himmel to hesitate. Frieren steps up to do the deed, but the village chief starts to sympathize with her and gives her a chance to atone by helping him in the fields. Frieren tells Himmel he will regret it if he doesn’t kill her now, but Himmel denies it, stating that she is able to talk to them. They stay in the village to see how things turn out. Some time passes, with the demon girl living with the village chief and playing with his daughter. Then one night, she burns the chief’s house and kills him. She states that she prepared the daughter of the chief as a replacement for the daughter of the villager she ate, saying the chief isn’t alive anymore. As Himmel unsheathes his sword, he cuts the demon’s hand before she can take the chief’s daughter hostage. Frieren blasts the demon, right after she says “Mother” once again. Frieren states that like monsters, Demon have no custom of raising children, so they are mostly alone. The concept of “family” does not exist. She asks the demon why she uses the word “mother” then. The demon replies that saying it prevented her from being killed and calls it a magical word, before dying and disintegrating to black dust. The flashback ends, and Frieren tells Fern and Stark that words to Demon are a means of deceiving humans. She decides to break out of the dungeon once the disorder starts. Meanwhile, as Lügner waits for Graf Granat in his mansion, he wonders where he has seen Frieren before and smiles as she is the only one in town who knows the true nature of Demon. Draht. Right after the events of the previous chapter, Graf Granat leads Lügner and his companions to his son’s room. He tells him about his son and shows his sword that was bestowed upon him by the king. After Lügner asks where he is now, Granat tells him that he died in a war with Aura ten years ago, and thrusts the sword in front of Lügner’s head while the sentinels also surround him. The demon girl gets ready to fire a spell, but Lügner prevents her. Graf Granat angrily tells Lügner that the only reason he allowed the demon envoy in was to get revenge for his son’s death, and states that Aura’s “reconciliation” can go to hell. Lügner looks around the room and notes how it has been meticulously cleaned for the past ten years and states that he has also kept his father’s room intact, who was killed by humans. This placates Graf Granat, and Lügner asks him to negotiate. Granat states that he will give it some thought and the Demon are shown to the drawing-room. On the way out, the demon girl, Linie, asks Lügner what a father is, and he replies, “who knows”. Lügner reveals that his true goal is to get Graf Granat to release the defensive barrier surrounding the town under the pretense of a “reconciliation”. Then Aura’s army will be able to destroy it. He inquires to Linie about Draht, the demon boy, and she replies that he said he went off to eliminate a nuisance. Meanwhile, Draht enters the dungeon after easily decapitating the sentinel at its entrance. He enters Frieren’s cell and introduces himself as a subordinate of Aura the Guillotine, and one of her executioners, and states that he has come to kill her. Frieren warns him that she is powerful, far more than Aura the Guillotine, shocking Draht. He doubts her, telling her it is already over, as he hangs her from the neck on a beam on the ceiling with a magical wire. Frieren is easily able to prevent her decapitation by concentrating her magical power on her neck. She remarks how hopeless Demon are now, as they fight like infants. Frieren cuts off Draht’s arm which was holding the wire, then quickly cuts off his other one as he makes wires from that as well. She lands on him and decapitates him, killing him and remarking that this is the first one to start. The Murder of a Guard. Right after the events of the previous chapter, Frieren exits the dungeon and finds the sentinel dead. Meanwhile, Fern and Stark are having lunch and Fern decides that they should go appeal to Graf Granat for Frieren’s release from prison and then defeat the Demon. Stark agrees as they do not look like enemies they can face alone, especially Lügner, who seemed incredibly powerful. As even with everyone around, he set his eyes only on Frieren, as he believes he can eliminate people like Stark and Fern any time. Fern tells Stark the Hero Party would go regardless of if it would end up in a fight, and Stark agrees. In Graf Granat’s mansion, Linie tells Lügner that she cannot detect Draht’s mana anymore, and he surmises that he must have been killed by Frieren then. Granat enters the room and tells them that the mage they apprehended has escaped and beheaded a sentinel. Lügner offers to help in the search, but the Graf refuses and notes how they are missing a person. Lügner tries to lie by saying he went to the restroom, but the Graf sees through it and asks again where the third demon is. Realizing their plan has failed, Lügner uses his magic to behead all the sentinels that were with Graf Granat, calling Draht an incompetent fool and remarking how he has ruined everything, yet being in the situation which he can only settle through violence made him excited, as they are wild beasts after all. Lügner injures Graf Granat but does not kill him so he can lift the protective barrier on the town. Meanwhile, as Fern and Stark head to the Graf’s estate, Fern spots Frieren stealthily walking in a black cloak. Frieren tells them how she killed a demon named Draht and that when Demon perish, they turn into particles of mana and disappear, so it would seem like Frieren was the one who killed the sentinel. She thinks that she would suffer capital punishment, so decides to leave town. Fern asks her if she is planning to abandon the town as the remaining Demon would reign free. Frieren asks why couldn’t Fern and Stark deal with them, and Stark replies that they don’t seem like enemies they can face. Frieren asks rhetorically if they would not fight an enemy if they were strong, leaving Fern and Stark speechless. She tells them she does not think they are weaker than the Demon in the slightest and leaves them, despite Stark’s pleas. Frieren senses a tremendous magic power a distance away from the town and recognizes it as Aura the Guillotine. Frieren comments how she also despises fighting powerful enemies, and must quickly finish what she dislikes. Frieren the Slayer. Right after the events of the previous chapter, Fern and Stark sneak into Graf Granat’s mansion to rescue him. Upstairs, Lügner tells Graf Granat how Demon devote their lives researching one particular magic throughout their life spans, and after years their magic becomes far more superior and further strengthens them. He says that to prevent demonic invasion, a protective barrier conjured by the Great Mage Flamme protects the town, and magic conjured by a prodigy from a millennium ago can still surpass the magic of today. He states that he despises prodigies, as they lack the beauty that comes form enhancement. Lügner turns around and asks Granat how the magic to control the barrier works, but he stays silent. He gives him time to think over it carefully and leaves the room with Linie, threatening the Graf with further torture if he refuses to tell them. Lügner then tries to find a grimoire relating to barriers in the mansion. A while later, Stark enters the room and tries to cut the ropes which bind Granat to a chair. Granat notices him trembling, and calls him brave, saying his deceased son also trembled before he went off to the frontlines. Stark is unable to cut the ropes as magic has been cast upon them. Graf Granat tells Stark to forget about him and says the townspeople must be evacuated. He tells Stark that if he shows the sentinels the Granat family crest which is on his neck they will abide by anything Stark tells them. Stark refuses and is about to destroy the chair with his axe but Lügner and Linie return to the room. Lügner asks the Graf if Stark is his acquaintance, and he tells him that he’s one of the adventurers from the morning, and lies that he came to negotiate without realizing his mage companion had already escaped from prison. Lügner lets Stark off, but Stark stands in his way. He quickly gets behind Lügner and attacks him, managing to cut his shoulder. Lügner does a counterattack with his blood magic from the blood of his shoulder and subdues him, but Stark manages to protect his vitals. Lügner praises his reflexes. Stark smiles as he realizes Lügner and Linie did not notice Fern outside the window. He tells Fern he has given her the opening, and she uses it to blast Lügner, cutting his arm and part of his torso off. He is shocked that a human mage could slip past Linie’s mana detection. Linie is about to face off against Fern, but Lügner stops her and asks Fern what magic she used. Fern replies that it was typical offense magic, which Demon call Zoltraak. Lügner thinks she’s being absurd, saying Demon conquered Zoltraak over half a century ago. He then asks who she learnt the magic from, but Fern realizes he is stalling for time and aims to finish him off quickly, but Stark suggests they withdraw as the Graf is gravely injured. Lügner tells Linie they will go after them after his bleeding stops, and that his blood is on them so they will not lose track of them. Linie suggests that Lügner doesn’t need to get involved, but he tells her that if she had been hit by Fern’s magic she would be dead. Lügner states that that magic has specialized to kill Demon now. Fern’s conduct reminds him of someone and he says he was once inflicted with the exact same magic. Suddenly, Lügner remembers a scene from his past. Frieren is looking down on him from the top of a pile of demon corpses. He realizes the mage from the morning was Frieren, saying that she greatly contributed to the humans’ research of Zoltraak, and is known as the mage who sent the most Demon to the grave in all of history. Lügner recalls Frieren's nickname: Frieren the Slayer, the kind of prodigy he despises. The Undead Army. Right after the events of the previous chapter, Stark and Fern discuss with Graf Granat how Frieren and the Hero Party had protected the town from Aura before. Granat reveals that Aura fights with a magical object known as the "Scales of Obedience" which weighs Aura's mana against her opponent's. The being with more mana is then given control over the one with less mana. Elsewhere, Frieren calls Aura out on her use of magic to animate fallen soldiers and the two clash. Frieren resorts to an antimagic to dispel Aura's control over the bodies rather than blasting them away (as she had done in the past) as that had angered Himmel. Ambush. Right after the events of the previous chapter, after leaving the Graf, Stark and Fern head towards the town and unexpectedly get attacked by Lügner and Linie. After pinning Fern to a wall, Lügner questions her and asks about the whereabouts of Frieren whilst commenting that Stark will not receive a pleasant death. On the contrary, Stark has engaged in a fight with Linie. After the initial surprise attack by Linie, Stark wonders why her technique is so similar to his master's. Fern then proceeds to grab her staff and break out of Lügner's hold. Lügner tells Fern she would lose her head first if she attacked. Fern remembers Frieren telling her that her Fern's strength lay in her casting speed. She tells Lügner that she, too, has spent half her life dedicated to magic before blasting him with a spell. Master's Technique. Right after the events of the previous chapter, Fern proceeds to attack Lügner who barely manages to defend it. After commenting on each others ability, Lügner then uses an attack of his own, saying "I shall crush you with my full strength". At this moment, it pans over to Stark, appearing in an injured state, after his fight against Linie. Linie mentions that Stark has lost, however Stark stands up remembering his Master's words, "The last Warrior standing wins" before striking again. Lügner in the midst of fighting Fern, watches Linie fade away, before getting blasted in the stomach by Fern. Coward. Right after the events of the previous chapter, Lügner is seen on the verge of death, with Fern approaching him. Before Lügner perishes, he is questioned, but to no answer. Then it flashes back to Frieren's past, where she encounters Flamme, after her village was destroyed. Despite Frieren overpowering the Demon who attacked her village, she couldn't protect anyone. Frieren and Flamme then proceed to have a conversation, to only be rudely interrupted by some Demon. As a result, Flamme eliminates them with ease, which Frieren is left awestruck. Frieren then follows Flamme as her apprentice. The next scene is shown to be the batttle between Frieren and Aura. Scales of Obedience. Right after the events of the previous chapter, it shows Frieren and Aura getting ready to fight. Then it shows proceeds to show the life of Frieren, under the apprenticeship of Flamme. Once Flamme perishes due to old age, it shows Frieren's life just before she is recruited by the hero party. Then it goes back to the present, when the battle between Aura and Frieren has just begun. During this fight Frieren restricts her mana, which results in Aura calling her weak, overlooking her abilities. As Frieren releases the seal placed upon herself, she commands Aura to kill herself. Victory and Funeral. Following from the events in the previous chapter, after the death of one of the Seven Sages Aura, it shows the battlefield, filled with deceased bodies. Graf Granat in response, thanks Frieren for minimizing the casualties. As he looks at the dead bodies, he sees one reminiscent of his son's, before commenting to give them a proper burial. As Frieren leaves the battlefield, she commends Stark and Fern in successfully beating Lügner and his accomplice. Then it cuts towards Graf's mansion where Frieren asks for a grimoire, however Graf Granat reveals that it is fake, yet Frieren says she knew all along and it was just a hobby of hers. As they soon depart from the city, it shows their experiences they had there, before showing the burial ground with people paying their respects. As they leave, they are informed that they need to take a Magic Association exam, but as they head towards they get lost in the snow.

Aureole , also referred to as or Heaven, is a gathering location for souls. It is located in the northernmost end of the continent, Ende, where the Demon King's Castle is also based. Overview. Located in the, Aureole is a place humans refer to as "heaven"; a place where one could meet with the souls of the dead. Recorded in the notes of Flamme, Aureole is where Flamme visited and spoke with her old comrades. Upon reading Flamme's notes of this encounter, traveling north to Aureole and reuniting with Himmel became Frieren's goal for her new journey. Due to Aureole being considered as the heaven of the world, it is presumed that the Goddess of Creation resides there. History. At some point in her life, Flamme journeyed to Aureole and spoke with her former comrades. She documented the encounter in her notes for Frieren to refer to a thousand years in the future, guarding the notes with a long-lasting protection spell. Synopsis. After Himmel's death, Heiter and Eisen correspond over mail, and Heiter discovers the location of a real and existing record of Flamme's notes that includes details of her being able to communicate with the dead. Frieren and Fern visit Eisen to provide any assistance for him, and he requests their aid in looking for the Great Mage Flamme's notes in the Voll Basin. During their search, Eisen explains that he felt pity for Frieren over her regret surrounding not getting to know Himmel more, and their quest to find the notes was to help her directly express to Himmel her thoughts. The group manages to locate a giant tree covering ruins, and Frieren removes the protective barrier that surrounds it. Inside, they find the notes, and the book opens up to the page detailing Flamme's visit to Aureole, where she described her meeting with the souls of her old comrades. With persuasion from Eisen, Frieren decides to make Aureole her destination for the possibility of speaking with Himmel once again. During their travels through the, Frieren and her party encounters Kraft, an Elf with strong faith in the Goddess of Creation. When Frieren tells him about their intended journey to Aureole, Kraft mentions his wish to be praised by the Goddess in heaven when he passes.

Bande Woods The Bande Woods is situated in the Northern Lands. It is a dense forest with bird-like monsters. Bande Woods. The Bande Woods are a dense forest situated in the Northern Lands. The forest is inhabited by dangerous bird-like monsters and other fauna which can be hunted for sustenance. Frieren's Party encounter one such bird-like monster while traversing the region. Synposis. Frieren's Party arrive in the Bande Woods and catch a ride on a wagon with an accessory merchant. Frieren discuses the bracelet Stark bought Fern for her birthday, which shares the same mirrored lotus flower design as a ring Himmel previously purchased for Frieren. Their discussion is interrupted by an attack from a bird-like monster, who lifts their wagon in the air. Frieren jumps out of the wagon and blasts the monster in midair, dropping them to the ground and damaging the wagon in the process. While the party works on reparations, Frieren realizes she has lost Himmel's ring. Meanwhile, Sein reveals that the mirrored lotus represents eternal love, much to Stark's dismay and Fern's annoyance. After the wagon is fixed, Fern realizes that Frieren has lost her ring and assists her in searching for it. With the aid of magic that seeks out lost accessories from the merchant, they locate the ring. As the party proceeds onwards through the woods, Frieren reflects on how she obtained the ring and that she is happy she did not give up on it.

Beyond Journey's End Arc The Beyond Journey's End Arc is the first story arc in "." It follows the beginning of Frieren's journey after defeating the Demon King. Summary. Prologue. After a ten-year journey, a group of adventurers defeated the Demon King and restored peace to the continent. Himmel, Eisen, Heiter, and Frieren are the members of the heroic group, which comprises of humans, dwarves, and elves. They watch the Era Meteors, a once-in-fifty-year meteor shower, together before they say their goodbyes. When the next celestial event comes, Frieren promises to meet them again and give them a better view. She then sets off on a journey across the continent in search of more magical knowledge. Frieren returns to the Royal Capital fifty years later, but things have changed and her former party members have all gotten older. After one more trip together to see the Era Meteors, Himmel succumbs to old age. While initially seeming unfazed at his funeral, Frieren ends up crying in regret at not doing more to learn about him while she could. This spurs Frieren to learn more about humans, and to later go see her old friends. Heiter takes in an orphaned child named Fern, and when his health begins to fail, she agrees to educate and care for her as a favor. While visiting Eisen, he asks her to visit the resting place of souls, Aureole, to wish Himmel a proper goodbye in person and convey her feelings. Frieren and Fern begin a journey together to fulfill Heiter and Eisen's requests while pursuing Frieren's love for magic. The End of the Adventure. The story begins with the Hero Party’s triumphant, carriage-ridden return to the Royal Capital. Some members are already thinking of getting a job, as life still goes on. The Hero remarks that the road ahead for Frieren is so long that it is beyond the others’ imagination. As the party reaches the Capital and walks through the streets, the citizens welcome them with great fanfare, shouting their congratulations and cheering for their victory. In the castle, the king praises the Hero Himmel, Warrior Eisen, Priest Heiter, and Mage Frieren for defeating the Demon King, remarking that a peaceful era will now dawn upon the world. After meeting the king, the party members converse and walk through the plaza, and Eisen and Himmel mention how the party has reached the end of its adventure. The members reminisce about the different parts of their adventure, such as Himmel and Eisen almost being executed for being impertinent to the king, Heiter always being useless after getting a hangover, and Frieren being eaten by a mimic. Despite these ridiculous memories, everyone was glad to have adventured with each other. Frieren states how their ten-year adventure was short though, much to the shock of Heiter and Himmel. As they converse, the Era Meteors, a meteor shower that happens once every fifty years, begin. Himmel remarks that it is a perfect beginning to a peaceful era. Frieren mentions how it is hard to see in town, and she says that next time, fifty years later, she will take the others to a place where the meteor shower can be witnessed more beautifully. Himmel chuckles at this, then agrees. The next day, the party disbands, and Frieren goes on a journey to acquire more magic since she plans to explore the Central Lands for over a century. As she leaves, Heiter and Himmel talk about how they, as humans, cannot perceive an elf's feelings, saying that even a century might feel like just another day to her. In her pursuit of magic, Frieren travels far and wide through different lands and climates. Five decades later, her need for Shadow Dragon horns finally brings her back to the Royal Capital, as she left the one she found in the Demon King’s Castle in Himmel’s possession. She notices how the townscape has changed considerably since she was last here. As Himmel calls out to Frieren from behind her, she finds him to have grown very old. Meanwhile, Frieren herself does not look a day older. Himmel thought he would never see her again. At Himmel’s house, he returns the Shadow Dragon’s horn to Frieren, thinking of it as a treasure that his beloved comrade left to him for safekeeping. Frieren goes outside and sees the statues of the Hero Party are now all degraded due to the passage of time. After Himmel gets ready, he and Frieren go meet Eisen and Heiter at the Capital’s gate. Frieren remarks how Heiter, who has also aged, looks more dignified, and he states that it is because he is a bishop now at the Holy City. Meanwhile, Eisen does not seem to have changed much appearance-wise, as he is a dwarf. Together, they all undertake a one-week journey, with Himmel remarking that the journey is elder abuse, to the place where they can witness the Era Meteors more beautifully. Himmel feels nostalgic throughout the journey, because as they ventured to many places, it reminded him of all the beautiful memories he made with his comrades. As they finally reach location Frieren had in mind, they witness the Era Meteors again and Himmel thanks Frieren, as they were able to have a really fun adventure at the end. Shortly afterwards, Himmel passes away, seemingly content. As the citizens mourn his loss at his funeral, they question how Frieren can show not a hint of sorrow despite being one of Himmel’s comrades. Suddenly, Frieren starts shedding tears, but she is unaware of the reason why, as she simply travelled with Himmel for a mere ten years. She questions why she never thought about getting to know him more, despite being aware of a human’s short lifespan. After the funeral, the party disbands once more. Heiter returns to the Holy City, telling Frieren and Eisen to show their faces more, as he might not be around for much longer. He jokes that his years of chronic drinking might finally be taking their toll. Frieren continues her journey to acquire magic, while also deciding to get to know humans better as well. She asks Eisen to become her vanguard, but he refuses, saying that he is no longer at an age capable of wielding an axe, shocking Frieren. They bid their farewells, and Frieren leaves for her voyage. The Priest's Lie. Twenty years after the Hero Himmel's passing, Frieren is in the Central Lands. She gets lost in a forest in the outskirts of the Holy City of Strahl trying to find Heiter. Suddenly, a young girl appears, surprising Frieren. Frieren tells her that she is trying to find the home of Heiter, and the young girl takes Frieren there.[[File: Heiter's older appearance.png|thumb|393x393px|An elderly [[Heiter]] meets [[Frieren]] outside his house. Heiter, now very elderly, meets Frieren outside the house, where she comments that the [[Heiter|Corrupt Priest]] is still alive. As they enter, Frieren offers Heiter some alcohol, but he refuses, saying that he has already stopped drinking. The young girl, named [[Fern]], turns out to be a war orphan from the [[Locations|Southern Lands]] adopted by Heiter. Frieren mentions that Heiter isn’t one to willingly rescue people, unlike [[Himmel]]. Heiter deflects and asks why Frieren is here, and she replies that she thought she would drop by to meet him, as she was shopping in the Holy City. Frieren also came to repay Heiter before he died, as she owes a lot to him. Heiter requests her to take Fern as a disciple, but she refuses, saying she would not want a child a friend left in her care to die, as the death rate of mage apprentices in the battlefield is very high. Instead of that, Heiter then asks Frieren to decipher a grimoire he dug out from [[Ewig|Sage Ewig’s]] gravesite. It supposedly contains records of lost resurrection and immortality spells. Frieren states that it might take five or six years, and she asks why Heiter wants it deciphered. He replies that he is now more afraid of dying than he ever was before, and that he wants just a little more time. Heiter also asks Frieren to teach Fern some magic in her free time, as he as a priest does not know how to do that. Frieren agrees, and goes out to look for Fern. She finally finds Fern training on a cliff in the forest, noting how near undetectable she is to mana sensory and wondering how hard she has studied at this young age. Fern tells Frieren that according to Heiter, she will be able to handle herself once she can knock down the high rock on the cliff on the other side. [[File: Fern blasts a spell at the rock CH2.png|thumb|left|270x270px|[[Fern]] Demonstrating her magic to [[Frieren]].|alt=]] She Demontrates that when she fires magic from her staff, her mana dissipates before reaching the rock, and asks Frieren how she can train to reach it. Frieren first asks Fern if she likes magic, to which she replies in the affirmative. Smiling, Frieren then starts to teach her the fundamentals of long-range magic. Four years pass, in which Frieren deciphers most of the grimoire. One day, when discussing Fern’s training with Heiter, Frieren states that Fern has reached a point where it would take an average person ten years to reach, remarking how she is a little too devoted. Suddenly, Heiter collapses. After he is carried to his room, Frieren tells him she will hurry up with deciphering the grimoire and goes to find Fern.[[File: Heiter collapses CH2.png|thumb|294x294px|[[Heiter]] collapses while talking to [[Frieren]]|alt=]] Fern is training on the same cliff as usual. When told by Frieren to take a break and go stay by Heiter’s side, she refuses, saying she has to knock down the high rock before Heiter passes away, as she was saved by him. It is revealed that when Fern was younger, she was about to jump off a cliff after losing her parents in a war. Heiter stops her, telling her it would be a waste for her to die. He explains that quite a while back, he lost an old friend of his, who, unlike Heiter, was an upright person who would never leave behind someone in trouble. Heiter states that if his friend lived on instead of him, he would’ve been able to save many people. Heiter considered living quietly for the rest of his life until it dawned upon him. If he were to die like this, then wouldn’t all the beautiful memories he made with his friend disappear from the world as well? Thus it would be a waste for Fern to die with all her beloved memories as well. Fern explains that learning how to survive on her own is her repayment of gratitude to Heiter. Frieren, after seeing her determination, lets her do as she wishes. Some more time passes, and Frieren finishes deciphering the grimoire, finding that neither resurrection nor immortality was recorded within. When asking Heiter if he knew, he replies that if such a thing existed, then Ewig himself would’ve used it. He asks Frieren about Fern’s progress, and she replies that she is no inferior to an adult. Heiter is relieved, as now Fern would no longer be a burden to Frieren, revealing that he calculated this from the start. He asks Frieren to collect her pay and leave with Fern at night, as he doesn’t have much longer and doesn’t want Fern to experience losing anyone else. Frieren rebukes him, telling him that he should give Fern a proper farewell, and try to make as many memories with her as possible. Tears flow down Frieren’s eyes, and Heiter calls her a kind girl. Before leaving him alone with Fern, she asks why he saved her. He replies that the Hero Himmel would have done the same, to which Frieren agrees. She goes to the cliff Fern used to train on and sees the high rock with a hole through it, revealing that Fern managed to reach it. Frieren decides that she too will be like the Hero Himmel. [[File: Fern manages to damage the rock CH2.png|thumb|center|306x306px|[[Fern]] manages to hit the high rock.|alt=]] After Heiter’s burial, Frieren pours alcohol over his grave. Fern thanks her, as she was able to repay Heiter, and Frieren replies that she was simply outsmarted by the corrupt priest. Together, Frieren and Fern continue their journey to acquire more magic. Blue-Moon Weed. Twenty-six years after [[Himmel|Himmel's]] passing, [[Frieren]] and [[Fern]] are in the [[Locations|Central Lands]], specifically the [[Turk Region]]. They help a farmer harvest some pumpkins and receive magic that produces warm tea as a reward. Fern comments that they have only been doing simple jobs, and Frieren replies that that is what it means to be an adventurer. She also notes that they have only been acquiring strange magic, such as magic that turns sweet grapes into sour ones and magic that de-rusts bronze statues. Frieren states that it is a hobby of hers. [[File: Himmel's rusted Turk statue CH3.png|thumb|right|130px|Himmel's statue.]]They come upon a village, whose herbalist asks them to clean a statue of the Hero Himmel, who once fought for the village when a monster attacked it. The statue is in terrible shape. The herbalist is too old to maintain it and the villagers are no longer concerned about it either. Frieren believes it is karma, as when the villagers said they could build him a statue, it took him 18 hours to decide on a pose, which enraged the elderly artisan. In the end, he settled with a foolproof pose. The herbalist calls it a curious story and recalls that there was an elven mage in the [[Hero Party]] as well, to which Frieren smiles. After the Frieren and Fern clean the statue, the herbalist thanks them, and thinks of planting some flowers around the statue to add more color. Frieren almost uses magic that can produce flower beds, but she stops and decides that a [[Ecology#Flora|blue-moon weed]] flower would be best, although she has never seen it before, as it is the flower of Himmel’s hometown. She asks the herbalist, who takes the duo back to her shop, and explains that long ago, all the flower fields within the forest were destroyed, and there hasn’t been a sighting of blue-moon weed for several decades on the continent. Meanwhile, Fern tries to hide a couple of seed rats, which are harmful animals that eat seeds, in her cloak but gets caught by Frieren, so she returns it to the forest. The duo decides to look for some blue-moon weed because if they are able to analyze a live specimen, they possess magic that will allow them to make the flowers bloom. Fern asks if Frieren is doing this for Himmel, but she replies that it is definitely for herself. Six months pass, and they still haven’t found any blue-moon weed. Although a trivial time for Frieren, Fern starts becoming impatient. One day, she goes to the herbalist’s shop alone and asks her if she thinks they will find the blue-moon weed. Fern explains that Frieren’s attachment or magic is abnormal and that at this rate they will keep looking for it for years or even decades. She says that Frieren is a mage who has the power to save many people and should not be spending her time on something nonexistent. The herbalist smiles and hands Fern a small pouch, and says she is sure that Frieren will understand if Fern conveys her feelings to her honestly. Fern goes to Frieren and expresses her thoughts. She shows her the pouch that is revealed to contain seeds of a related species the herbalist stored. Fern suggests planting these around Himmel’s statue instead. Frieren understands and says they will stop after a little more searching. At the same time, a seed rat steals the pouch of seeds and runs away. As the duo pursues it, Fern asks Frieren why she is acquiring magic, to which she again replies that is her hobby. Fern states that it does not seem like it. Frieren recalls a memory from the past when she was with the Hero Party. She used magic to produce a field of flowers, which excited [[Eisen]] and [[Heiter]], causing them to prance around and play in it. Heiter merrily places a flower crown on Eisen’s head, causing Frieren to remark that the scene was disgusting. Smiling, Himmel places a flower crown on Frieren’s head as well. [[File: Himmel places a flower crown on Frieren CH3.png|thumb|left|300px|Himmel smiles as he places a flower crown on Frieren’s head.]] Frieren then tells Fern that it is because there was a fool who praised her for the magic she acquired. Fern calls it a silly reason, and Frieren concurs. They eventually reach an abandoned watchtower where many seed rats can be seen. Frieren picks up a flower petal that was on the ground near it the tower and inspects it. She then explains to Fern that seed rats hide their food by burying it in a safe place away from enemies, but they often forget where they hide them. As Frieren flies up to the top of the watchtower, she recalls another memory from the same day. Himmel tells Frieren about blue-moon weed, the flower of his hometown, and says that he wants to show it to her someday. When Frieren reaches the top of the watchtower, she finds a multitude of blue-moon weed flowers, remarking that she didn’t expect there to be this many. She also remarks that Himmel was pretty late. [[File: Frieren finds the blue-moon weed on the tower CH3.png|thumb|right|250px|Frieren witnessing the great amount of blue-moon weed on top of the watchtower.]] As Frieren analyzes a specimen, Fern also reaches the top and is surprised that they found it. She says she cannot fathom why Frieren dedicates her entire heart and soul towards magic. Frieren says she is sure Fern understands, as she also has not given up on becoming a mage. Fern disagrees, saying she was simply content with any power with which she could survive on her own. Frieren rebuts her, saying that she did choose magic, and Fern agrees. Frieren plants the flowers around Himmel’s statue, and the herbalist thanks them, thinking she would never see blue-moon weed again. She is sure that the statue will never be forgotten now as well. As the duo leaves, Frieren places a blue-moon weed crown on Himmel’s statue’s head, similar to how he placed a crown atop Frieren's head in the past. The herbalist remarks that it is lovely, and Frieren and Fern continue their journey.[[File: Himmel's statue with the flower crown CH3.png|thumb|center|200px|Himmel's statue wearing a flower crown.]] The Mage's Secret. Twenty-seven years after the Hero [[Himmel]]’s passing, [[Frieren]] and [[Fern]] are in a trading town called [[Warm]]. [[Frieren]] decides they should split up to replenish supplies for their journey. However, [[Fern]] feels [[Frieren]] is hiding something from her, and in times like these she ends up buying unnecessary things, like a large skull or a drug that melts clothes, so [[Fern]] starts tailing her. First, she sees [[Frieren]] spend a lot of time concerned in front of an accessory shop before buying something. [[File: Frieren looking for accessories CH4.png|thumb|right|220px|Frieren thinks of what accessory to buy while Fern secretly watches her.]] After that, she asks around for a tasty “candy shop”, and ends up asking for it from wild-looking adventurers in a bar. She then leaves the bar, and to [[Fern]]’s surprise, heads back towards the inn. [[Fern]] quickly finishes her shopping before also returning. [[Frieren]] decides that they should go eat some tasty food as it has been a while. They go to a place recommended to [[Frieren]] which has a nice view. [[File: Frieren and Fern dine together CH4.png|thumb|left|250px|Frieren and Fern dining at a place with a nice view.]] [[Fern]] apologizes to [[Frieren]] for doubting her, but [[Frieren]] does not know what she is talking about. [[Frieren]] tells [[Fern]] to choose whatever she wants as she has some secret savings, surprising [[Fern]]. [[Fern]] asks [[Frieren]] what she will choose, but before [[Frieren]] can say anything, [[Fern]] already answers with merkur pudding. This causes [[Frieren]] to recall a memory with the Hero Party where [[Himmel]] also guessed correctly that [[Frieren]] was in the mood for merkur pudding. She asks him how he knew, and he replies that he has a rough idea as they have been travelling for several years now. [[Frieren]] states that she does not know a thing about any of the hero's party, and [[Himmel]] says that they’ll have to put in some effort for her to learn. He states his favorite dish, and [[Eisen]] states his. Before [[Heiter]] can say his, [[Frieren]] already answers with alcohol, calling him a Corrupt Priest and making him feel embarrassed. [[Frieren]] apologizes to [[Fern]], as she does not know a thing about her, thus she does not know what kind of food she likes. She hands [[Fern]] a box, which reminds her that it is her birthday. She opens the box to find a beautiful hair ornament. [[Fern]] thanks [[Frieren]] and tells her that she is delighted. [[Fern]] tells [[Frieren]] that her attempts to get to know more about [[Fern]] give her overwhelming bliss, even though they are just attempts. The next day, [[Frieren]] and [[Fern]] continue their voyage, with [[Fern]] now wearing her new hair ornament. [[File: Fern's hair ornament CH4.png|thumb|center|300px|Fern wears her new hair ornament.]] She asks [[Frieren]] if there is some goal to their journey. She replies that it is just out of interest to gather magic, and also to retrace the steps she took with the Hero Party as much as possible before they fade away. [[Fern]] thinks that that must be important to [[Frieren]], but she is not sure, and that is why she thinks she’ll find out. [[Frieren]] notes how [[Fern]] has surpassed her in height, and [[Fern]] replies that it is because she is 16 now, a young lady. [[Frieren]] looks at [[Fern]]’s developed chest, comparing it with her own, and wonders why it is so small, even though they practically eat the same things. Killing Magic. Twenty-seven years after the Hero [[Himmel|Himmel's]] passing, [[Frieren]] and [[Fern]] are in the [[Locations|Central Lands]], specifically the [[Größe Forest]]. Frieren is training Fern on defensive magic.[[File: Frieren trains Fern CH5.png|thumb|right|200px|[[Frieren]] trains [[Fern]] on defensive magic.]] Fern seems to have gotten used to defensive magic, as she is able to block attacks from the front, so Frieren targets an opening in her defense, attacking her back. To defend that type of attack, Fern uses defensive magic all around her, and Frieren attacks again, which quickly exhausts Fern's mana. After that, Frieren decides to end training. As they travel, Frieren explains to Fern that defensive magic is powerful, but it burns a lot of mana and that if she continues expanding its size, she will exhaust her mana in a minute or two. Fern states then the correct decision would be to expand it to specific areas the moment she would be hit. They have only been training defensive magic lately as it is directly linked to their survival. This one defensive magic is enough to protect against the majority of offensive magic. Fern is curious about how immensely powerful it is. Frieren asks if Fern read the magic chronicles book she gave her, and tells her that magic is not only about combat. Frieren and Fern reach the village they were looking for, and a villager recognizes Frieren and leads her to the place where [[Qual]] was sealed. Qual is the Elder Sage of Corruption, a [[Demon|demon]] that committed immeasurable atrocities on the land eighty years ago. The [[Hero Party]] sealed him away. Frieren asks the villager how he knew she would be coming, and he answers that before his passing, Himmel would visit the village once every year to check on the condition of the seal. He told the villager that despite not showing up once to check on the seal, Frieren would definitely show up once the seal was close to breaking. They then reach the place where Qual was sealed, and Frieren decides that she will remove the seal the next day and dispose of him. [[File: A sealed Qual CH5.png|thumb|left|290px|The villager leads [[Frieren]] and [[Fern]] to the place where [[Qual]] was sealed.]] Back at the village inn, Frieren explains to Fern that she sealed Qual away simply because he was too powerful to beat. He was an outstanding sorcerer even amongst the [[Demon King|Demon King's]] army. He developed Killing Magic, or [[Zoltraak]], the very first piercing magic in history, which could pierce not just all of mankind’s defensive magics but even equipment imbued with magic resistance. Fern asks if he would not be overly powerful then, and Frieren agrees, saying he was overly powerful, and that is why that power backfired on him. She again states that Fern still hasn’t read the magic chronicles, but lets her sleep instead, as Fern would understand tomorrow anyway. The next day, Frieren undoes Qual’s seal. Frieren tells him that it has been eighty years and the Demon King was killed. Qual supposes that he should avenge him, and fires Killing Magic: Zoltraak at the duo. Fern easily blocks it with her defensive magic, surprising Qual and making him remark that it must be a rather advanced technique. Fern is confused, and she states that Zoltraak was just ordinary offensive magic. Frieren explains that Qual’s magic was overly powerful, but in just a few years after his sealing, Zoltraak was analyzed and Killing Magic was incorporated into the magic systems of mankind, and powerful defensive magics were developed that countered those offensive techniques. The magic resistance in equipment has remarkably improved as well, and Killing Magic no longer kills. Frieren tries to get Qual to cooperate in order to give him a peaceful death, but he is able to deduce that defensive magic is taxing on one’s mana and fires Zoltraak in different directions at them. However, Fern is still able to defend the duo as she has already witnessed this in training. Frieren fires Zoltraak at Qual, destroying him with his own magic, and he dissolves into black dust. [[File: Frieren destroys Qual CH5.png|thumb|right|300px|[[Frieren]] destroys [[Qual]] with [[Zoltraak]].]] When the duo returns to the village, the villager thanks Frieren and says they can now live in peace. Frieren notices his hat and seems to remember it from somewhere, and recalls that the old villager was a stupid brat who once flipped up Frieren’s skirt when the Hero Party came to the village a long time ago. This angered Himmel, making him say that he always wanted to look under there. Frieren wonders at the fact he is still alive, and the villager replies that because of Frieren, it seems he can live longer and that it was worthwhile to believe in Himmel’s words. Frieren and Fern continue their journey, and Fern tells Frieren that she thinks Himmel believed in Frieren, making her smile. New Year's Festival. Twenty-eight years after the Hero [[Himmel|Himmel's]] passing, [[Frieren]] and [[Fern]] are in the [[Locations|Central Lands]], specifically the [[Granz Channel]]. A village requests them to clean up the washed-up debris from the coast, rewarding them with a grimoire by the Great Mage [[Flamme]]. Frieren accepts the request despite the grimoire being a counterfeit, as Fern was able to tell. Frieren accepted the request nevertheless because the village head looked concerned, and also for herself. [[File: Frieren and Fern observe the debris CH6.png|thumb|left|210px|[[Frieren]] and [[Fern]] inspecting the debris on the coast.]] Three months pass, and winter arrives. Fern always has to take care of Frieren like a mother - waking her up, brushing her hair, feeding her, and clothing her. [[File: Fern takes care of Frieren CH6.png|thumb|right|250px|[[Fern]] taking care of [[Frieren]] like a mother.]] She asks if the [[Hero Party]] was never angered by Frieren oversleeping, and she replies that they were once. Fern remarks that they must have been rather tolerant, and Frieren strongly agrees. The village head visits them one night to ask about the progress of the clean-up and comments that it would be delightful if they could witness the sunrise during the New Year's Festival. The next day, Fern asks how cleaning the coast is related to the New Year's Festival. Frieren replies that the village has a custom of watching the sunrise on the New Year's Festival and that it is truly picturesque when the sunlight reflects off of the untainted sea, although she herself has never seen it as she could never wake up for it. They hurry with their clean-up and finish in time for the eve of the event. The village head thanks them, and welcomes them with open arms for the New Year's Festival. Frieren states that she will pull an all-nighter to be able to see it. At night, she recalls a memory of when the Himmel was cross when she didn’t attend the New Year's Festival. Even [[Heiter]] drank too much alcohol and fell asleep. Frieren asks if it wasn’t enough when the others managed to go. Himmel replies that they wanted her to have fun as well. Frieren doubts that she would have had fun, but Himmel disagrees because that is who she is. Frieren ended up sleeping anyway and was quickly woken up by Fern. They head for the New Year's Festival, and Frieren thanks Fern on the way. They reach the port and witness the sunrise reflecting off of the sparkling sea. [[File: Frieren and Fern watch the sunrise CH6.png|thumb|center|380px|[[Frieren]] and [[Fern]] watch the beautiful sunrise together.]] Frieren thinks it is beautiful, but not worth waking up for. As she is about to head back to sleep some more, she sees Fern smiling, captivated by the sunrise. Fern notices how it seems to be invoking joy in Frieren, and she replies that it is because Fern was smiling. This suddenly makes Frieren realize what Himmel meant many years ago, and she smiles. The Land Where Souls Rest. The chapter begins with a flashback of when the [[Hero Party]] visited [[Eisen|Eisen's]] home. [[Heiter]] sees a couple of graves and asks if they are Eisen’s family. He replies that his village was attacked by Demon once, and Heiter starts praying for them.
